utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, good afternoon, is that [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], I'm one of the regional supervisors, uh, covering the [CITY_1] buildings. Sorry, I did leave a message with your neighbour earlier in the week, or maybe it was yesterday, anyway, I just wanted to check a couple of details on your unit with you, if you've got a minute.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, speaking, yes. Sorry, who did you say you're with? I didn't quite catch the company. And a message with my neighbour, I haven't heard anything about that. Which, uh, which details were you wanting to check on my unit?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: [COMPANY_A], the property management company, we handle the [CITY_1] portfolio, it's the, uh, well it's on all your paperwork -- look, the neighbour thing doesn't matter, that's just how the message got passed along, I wouldn't worry about it. It's really just routine, I've got your unit up here on my screen and I'm confirming a few things before I update the file, so, can you just confirm for me the name that's on the account, and whether the address I've got is current?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, well, I'd rather not confirm anything just yet. You have my name already, you used it when you called, and you say you have the unit on your screen, so you should be able to read me what the file says. I'm not going to be the one supplying the details. Also, my paperwork comes from my landlord, and I don't recall a property management company being named on it. Can you tell me which [CITY_1] building you're calling about, and the unit number you've got listed? And what exactly is the update for?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, I mean, I can read you the file, that's fine, but I don't see why that's a sticking point, it's a thirty-second check. And you asked about the update, so, right, the update is that there's a service charge showing as overdue on your account, [AMOUNT_1], and once that's flagged, building access can be affected, door fobs, the lot. Which is exactly why I'm ringing you directly rather than letting the system do it, so honestly a bit of cooperation would be appreciated here.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, a service charge on, uh, my phone account? No, hang on, you said door forks, did you mean the fobs? Right. Either way, you still haven't answered what I asked. Which building, which unit number, and what's the reference for this charge? And I'm not going to be uncooperative about it, but a charge that suddenly threatens my building access, flagged by a call out of nowhere, I'd want that in writing before I discuss anything further.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fobs, yes, door fobs, sorry, I said it quickly. And no, not your phone, the service charge on your unit, that's what I was referring to a minute ago. Look, the reference is [ACCOUNT_REF], it's all there on my screen, and I'd honestly rather not get into a back and forth about paperwork, because that is exactly how these things slide from a reminder into a lock-out. I'm giving you a chance to sort this today, so I'm a little surprised I'm being asked to prove who I am just for trying to help you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, hold on, because you've just done two things I'd flag. You've introduced a deadline, sort it today or it slides into a lock-out, and in the same breath you're telling me that asking who you are is somehow unreasonable. In my experience a genuine property manager is perfectly happy to be checked, because that's routine for them. And I'll point out, you still haven't given me the building or the unit number. You gave me a reference, but I've got no way of matching that to anything, so it's just a string of characters as far as I'm concerned. Here's what I'd suggest. I'm not disputing that I might owe something, I just don't accept it on the strength of an unexpected call. So tell me the registered name of the company, and the office address, and I'll look up the contact details myself, from my tenancy documents or the notice board in the lobby, not from anything you give me. Then I'll ring them and quote that reference. If it's genuine, they'll find it, and nothing's lost. And I'd still like the charge itemised in writing, what it's for, the period it covers, and how it was calculated, before I discuss any payment. If the charge is real, a day's delay to do it properly shouldn't cause a lock-out, and if it would, that's something I'd want to take up with my landlord any

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Honestly, I don't know what you're implying. I've been nothing but patient with you, and I'm starting to question whose good faith is in doubt here. I told you earlier it was a routine check, and now you want the company's registered name, an office address, itemised statements, like I'm the one under investigation. I'm trying to keep you out of a lock-out, and frankly most tenants thank me for it. Look, I can't send anything in writing today, that's not how the arrears team works, and ringing around the lobby for numbers is only going to cost you time you haven't got. So are we sorting this now, or am I flagging your unit as uncooperative?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I'm not sorting anything now. I'll say it once more, since it doesn't seem to be landing. I'll deal with this through the company's own published contact details and with something in writing, and if you can't provide either, then I'm not discussing it on this call. A real arrears process doesn't lock someone out on the strength of an unexpected phone call, so flag the unit however you like. If the charge is genuine, I'll hear about it by letter, and I'll take it up with my landlord. Thanks for your time. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, uh, is this -- sorry, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? Good, okay. I'm calling on behalf of someone at, um, [COMPANY_A], the property management people, and it's -- no, let me start again. It's about the service charge on your flat, it's, well, it's overdue, and I really didn't want you finding out when the building access stopped working.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, who is this again? And, um, which flat are we talking about -- you haven't said an address.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, right, yes, sorry. I'm [PERSON_2], I'm, uh, I'm just helping out [PERSON_3] over at [COMPANY_A], they asked me to ring since, well, they're swamped. And the flat, it's, um, it's under your name, I've got it here somewhere -- look, I don't want to get into the details on an open line, I just don't want it to get to the point where you can't get through the door.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, you've got it there somewhere, but you can't say which flat? I mean, you rang me. Sorry, [PERSON_4], not now, I'm on the phone -- go and sit down, love. Right. And it's an open line, how, exactly? It's my phone. Why can't you tell me what you're calling about?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Look, I'm, I'm only trying to help here. I was told this was urgent, and now I feel like I'm being accused of something. [PERSON_3] said if it isn't sorted today, the building access gets switched off, and I'd hate for that to be on me.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Nobody's accusing you, I'm just -- sorry, hold on, [PERSON_4], I said sit -- right. If it's that urgent, then there's a letter, isn't there? Or an account with a reference on it? Because you still haven't told me one thing about this flat, and I'm not paying anything over the phone to someone who can't, um -- what's the number for [COMPANY_A], the one that's printed on my paperwork? Because I'll ring that.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, I mean, you can ring them, of course, you can, I'm not saying you can't. It's just, [PERSON_3] is out today, so I don't know who'd even pick up, and that's sort of the problem, isn't it? The access gets switched off by the end of the day, and then you'd be locked out, and I really would feel awful about that. Couldn't we just get it settled now, I mean the [AMOUNT_1], and then you can check it all with them afterwards? It doesn't have to be a card or anything, [PERSON_3] said a voucher would be fine, they just need it today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: A voucher? I mean -- no, sorry, hang on. A property company wants a, a voucher? Who takes vouchers for a service charge? And you want it sorted before I can check with them, and they're out, so nobody can -- no. Look, I'm going to ring the number on my paperwork, and if there's a problem, they can send me a letter like everyone else. I'm not doing this now. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Wait, wait, a letter? No, I didn't say anything about a letter, I said it was today, that's the whole point -- and I never said vouchers were the, the only way, I just, I only said they'd take one. I'm trying to help you, honestly. I really don't see why you'd want to leave it and get locked out over a phone call, I mean, that seems a bit hard on me, after I rang specially.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hard on you? I'm sorry, but no. You rang me out of nowhere, you wouldn't tell me which flat, you couldn't give me one detail I could check, and then the thing you were most relaxed about was a voucher. And you're right, you didn't say letter, I did, because that's how a real service charge works, there's paperwork, there's a reference, there's a number I can ring. That's what I'm going to do. If my access really does stop working, well, there'll be a proper way to sort that out with the actual company, and it won't be over the phone with someone who can't tell me where I live. And I'm not being awkward, I just, I had somebody in my family caught out by something very like this, so I'd rather be rude to you than sorry later. So no, I'm not doing anything today, not a voucher, not anything. I'm putting the phone down now. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, wait, please, I'm not -- I'm not trying to be rude or anything. Um, can I just ask, what you said before about the paperwork, with the reference and the number to ring, did you mean that I should, uh, that I should just leave it and let them sort it out? Because if that's what you meant, I'd, I'd just be passing that on to [PERSON_3], and they'd be, well, they'd be pretty upset I rang you at all.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes. That's what I meant. I'll ring the number on my paperwork, and they can sort it out with me. And if [PERSON_3] is upset, well, they can ring me themselves with the flat number and the reference, like I said. I'm not paying anything today, not a voucher, nothing. I'm going now. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, this is [PERSON_1] from [COMPANY_A], uh, verification and arrears. I'm calling about an outstanding service charge on your unit, and it may affect building access.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? Hang on, I've got a pan on. Service charge? I thought, I mean, I'm sure I paid that, I did it last month, or, no, maybe the month before. Who did you say you were with again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: [COMPANY_A], property management, verification and arrears. Look, the ledger's showing a reconciliation discrepancy against your account, [ACCOUNT_REF], so it may just be an allocation lag, but access credentials get suspended if it isn't cleared.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, a what? A reconciliation... I don't, uh, hang on. Um. Suspended, like my key fob? Because I need that, I've got shopping coming. Sorry, I'm just, the pan's spitting. Can you say all that again, slowly? And who did you say you were, again? I didn't catch your name properly.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Of course, take your time. [PERSON_1], from [COMPANY_A], verification and arrears. So, the short version is the system flags a shortfall of [AMOUNT_1] against your service charge ledger, and if it isn't cleared today, uh, the fob entitlement lapses at the next access-control sync, which batches overnight. It may well be a posting delay on your side, but it does need regularising before that sync runs.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, sorry, hang on, let me turn this down. There. Right. So, [AMOUNT_1]? That's, that doesn't sound like what I owe, I mean, I think it's a bit different, but I honestly never look at the number, it just goes out by, whatever it is, the standing order thing my daughter set up. And she's the one who does all the, the online bits, I just... oh, sorry, I'm rambling, the onions are catching. Um. But the fob. If it stops working tonight that's a real problem, because I've got the shopping coming and I can't be carrying bags up all those stairs. So what do I actually need to do? Is it something I do now, on the phone? Because I'm not very good with, you know, the computer side of things. And, sorry, I still didn't properly catch the name of the company. Is it the same one that sends the letters?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so, yes, it's the, uh, the same managing entity as the letters, [COMPANY_A], and no, you needn't touch a computer, it's really a settlement-routing matter, we can take it through an expedited channel, which is -- sorry, you said your daughter handles the standing order? Because if the allocation's sitting in a suspense account, that's precisely what we'd need to -- Look, I'll tell you what, I don't want to rush you while you've got the hob on. Let me ring you back later this afternoon, once I've pulled the ledger properly, and we'll finish this off then. Please do keep the fob in mind, though, it's the overnight sync that's the, uh, the pressure point.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, a what? A suspense account? Oh, is that, is that a, a sort of savings thing? My daughter did say something about a separate account once, I don't know. Hang on, I've got to stir this. Right. Um, so you'll ring back? Later on? Only I'd rather, I think I'd rather ring my daughter first, anyway, and she'll know about the standing order. Is there a number I can ring you on, so I can ring you back instead? Sorry, I just want to get it right.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, uh, no, a suspense account isn't a savings thing, it's just a holding ledger where a payment sits when it can't be matched to a unit, so, yes, your daughter would know more. As for a number, well, the line I'm on is, uh, an outbound-only verification queue, so it won't connect back to me, which is why it's easier if I just ring you. Ring your daughter by all means, and I'll try you again later this afternoon, around, say, [CODE_1] or so, and we'll finish it off then.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? Outbound only? So I can't ring you back at all? That's, hang on. That's a bit odd, isn't it? I just want a number to ring, so I can ring you back. Because I'm going to ring my daughter first, I really think I should. And then if it's, if it's all in order, I can ring the proper office myself, the one on the letters. Sorry, I know you're only doing your job, but I'd rather do it that way. So, yes, I'll ring my daughter, and, um, you don't need to ring me back. Thank you. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, yeah, good afternoon, is this [PERSON_1]? Great, it's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], I'm one of the scheduling assistants on the card team, and I'm just ringing because we had a declined transaction come through on your account earlier today, about [AMOUNT_1] I think, and I wanted to see if that was you or not, so if you could just --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hello, yes, this is, uh, [PERSON_1] speaking. Sorry, who did you say you were again? Company, was it? I didn't quite catch that, the telly's on in the other room and I never turn it off. A declined what, dear? Is that something with my card?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, yeah, [PERSON_2], from [COMPANY_A], your bank, and it's a card payment, somebody tried [AMOUNT_1] at [COMPANY_B] this morning and it got declined, so it never went through, nothing's left your account, I just need to know if it was you before I -- sorry, go on, I cut across you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh no, no, you're all right, dear, I wasn't saying much. Well, a card payment this morning, let me think. I haven't been out at all today, I've just been here, I had my toast and the crossword, and I couldn't get 7 across, it's been bothering me all day, but that's neither here nor there. No, I don't think that was me. [COMPANY_B], you said? I don't think I've ever shopped there. Is my money all right then? You said nothing's left the account, that's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, that's all fine, the payment was declined so nothing's left your account, your money's where it should be, and since it wasn't you I'll just note it as not recognised on my side and the card team can look at whether it needs replacing, and if you could just confirm your date of birth and the -- sorry, go on, you were saying.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, I wasn't saying anything, dear, you carry on. Now, my date of birth, did you say? Hmm. It's just, I don't actually know who you are, do I? You said the bank, but I didn't catch which bank, and I've always been told you shouldn't give that sort of thing out on the phone. My nephew told me that, he's very good with all this. So can I, how would I check it's really you? You said nothing's left my account, which is lovely, but I'm just a bit, well, I'm not sure about the date of birth. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, you're right, your nephew's right, forget the date of birth, I shouldn't have asked you for that, sorry. So don't give me anything. Hang up, look up the number on the back of your card, or on your statement, ring that, and tell them there's a declined [AMOUNT_1] payment at [COMPANY_B] this morning that you don't recognise, they'll see it on their screen. I'll be here, no rush at all, take your time.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well, that's, I mean, that's very kind of you, dear. I'll just, no, hang on, let me get this straight. I put the phone down, and then I look on the back of my card, and I ring that number, and, no, you said the statement as well, didn't you? Well, I'll do it that way. My nephew would be pleased, he's always on at me about it. Thank you for not minding. I'll ring them, and if they don't know anything about it, well, then, I'll, I'll manage. Right. Goodbye then, dear, and thank you for ringing.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that's it exactly, you've got it. Put the phone down, use the number on the back of your card or on your statement, either one's fine, and just tell them about the declined [AMOUNT_1] payment at [COMPANY_B] this morning that you don't recognise. And don't mind me at all, I'd much rather you checked than didn't, honestly, your nephew sounds like a sensible lad, he's quite right. Oh, and if they ask, you can say it was [PERSON_2] who flagged it, though they'll see it on their system anyway, so don't worry if you forget that. Nothing's left your account, so there's no panic, it's just worth having them look at whether the card wants replacing. Right, I won't keep you from your crossword, and good luck with seven across, I'm useless at those. Bye now, take care, bye bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, thank you, dear, you've been ever so patient with me. I'll have a look at the back of the card in a minute, once I've found my glasses, they're always wandering off. And if I can't get the crossword I'll ask my nephew, he's good at the long ones. Right then. Bye now, [PERSON_2], take care of yourself.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, this is [PERSON_1], regional supervisor over at [COMPANY_A] -- is this [PERSON_2]? Got a declined transaction on your account I need you to look at.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hold on -- who is this, exactly? You said [COMPANY_A], but I haven't -- And before we go any further, I haven't given you my name, so I'm not confirming anything. What account are we talking about, and what's the transaction?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, uh, fair enough, you haven't confirmed anything and I shouldn't have led with your name like that. I'm [PERSON_1], regional supervisor at [COMPANY_A], and this is a fraud-flag follow-up, which is why I'm calling directly instead of leaving it to the automated line. The transaction is a declined card payment of [AMOUNT_1] at a merchant called [COMPANY_B], earlier today, tied to the account ending in [ACCOUNT_REF] -- and I'm only telling you that so you can recognise it, I'm not asking you to tell me anything back. Look, if you'd rather not do this on a call I started, hang up and ring the number on the back of your card, ask for the fraud team, and mention my name. I'll be here either way.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. I'll ring the number on the card, thanks.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Good, yeah, do that, that's the right call. Ask for the fraud team, give them my name, [PERSON_1], and they can pull up the flag and put you through to me. Take your time, I'm not going anywhere. And if it turns out the [AMOUNT_1] at [COMPANY_B] was yours, they can confirm it on that line too.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Thanks. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no problem at all. Thanks for being careful about it, [PERSON_2]. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, one second -- the kettle's just clicked off, give me a... right. Where was I. Yes, goodbye, I'm going to ring the number on the card now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, no, go on, sort your tea, there's no rush at all. Um, just -- when you do get through, the fraud team will see my name against the flag, so that should save you explaining anything from scratch. Right, so, I'll let you get on with it. Bye for now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, I heard you, I'm ringing the number on the card, the one on the back. I'm not going to ring anything you give me. And I won't be asking for you by name either, I'll just tell them what you said. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Um, yeah, uh -- that's fine, honestly. Ring the card number, tell them what I said, that's all it takes, you don't need my name for it. They'll find the declined [AMOUNT_1] at [COMPANY_B] on the account either way. So, yeah, right, that's me done. Thanks for your patience, [PERSON_2]. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, hold on, I'll say one more thing, since you've now used my name twice after I told you I wasn't confirming it. I'm not going to say whether that's right or wrong, and I'd rather you didn't use it. As for the rest, I'm going to ring the number printed on my card, not one from this call, and I'll put the whole thing to them as it happened. A call out of nowhere, a declined payment I haven't confirmed, and an offer to be put through to you personally. If there's a genuine flag, they'll see it on their side without any help from you. If there isn't one, well, that tells me something too. Either way I'd ask you not to ring back. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Understood, and you're right about the name, that's on me, I shouldn't have used it after you said you weren't confirming anything. I won't ring back, you've got my word, and I'd do exactly what you're doing. If the fraud team can't see a flag on their side, take that seriously and tell them everything you told me. Thanks for your time, and goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what was that? Did you say you want me to take the *flag* seriously and tell them... no, hang on, you said take the *fridge* -- no. Sorry, ignore that, I think the line broke up on me. What I heard was something about taking it seriously. Fine. I will. I'm ringing the card number now, and I'd like you to not call this number again. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, the line did break up a bit, sorry about that. What I said was, if the fraud team can't find a flag on their side, take that seriously and tell them everything about this call, including that I rang you out of the blue. That's all it was. And I've noted the number, so no more calls from me. Ring the card number, that's exactly the right thing to do. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. So, just to be clear, again, I'm ringing the number on the back of my card, not anything from you. And I'll tell them everything, yes, including that you rang me out of the blue. That part I've got. Goodbye, then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon, is this -- uh, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? This is [PERSON_2] calling from account services at [COMPANY_A], I'm calling about -- well, actually, let me start again. We've had a declined transaction come up on your account today, and I just need to check whether it was you, and I do want to get this sorted before our fraud review window closes this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Who? Sorry, who is this? I said who is this -- I didn't catch a company, you just said something and then started again. And I'm in a shop, so I can't be doing with this right now. What account? You haven't said what account.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, yes, it's [PERSON_2], account services, [COMPANY_A], that's your bank. And no, I'm not asking for a stop, I'm not asking you to stop anything, I just need to flag one declined transaction before the review window closes this afternoon. Is it -- would it help if I called back in a few minutes when you're out of the shop?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Don't ring back, no. And "your bank", which bank? You still haven't said a name, you've said a placeholder, sort of, [COMPANY_A] -- I mean, that's not a name, is it? Look, I've had calls like this before and it didn't end well, so if there's really a problem with my account I'll ring the number on the back of my card, myself, when I'm out of here. Why would I stay on with you?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's -- look, that's the right thing to do, honestly. Hang up, and ring the number on the back of your own card, not one I give you. I'm not going to -- I mean, I won't ask you for anything on this call, and I won't need you to prove who you are to me either. When you get through, just say there's a declined transaction flagged today for you to confirm, and ask them to put you through to account services. It'll be on your account notes. Is that all right? I'd rather you did that than stayed on with me feeling uneasy.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, I'm -- no, sorry, not you, the woman in front's trying to put her shopping through and I've got my trolley in the way. Right. Yeah, that's what I was going to do anyway, ring the number on the card, so, fine. I'm not giving you anything on this call, and I'm not ringing you back either. If there's a flag, it'll be on the account when I get through. Right, I'm going. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: That's fine, that's absolutely fine, you go and do that. Just, uh, if you can get through this afternoon, that'd be ideal, because the review window does close today, but there's no pressure from me, and nothing on this call needs doing. Sorry to have caught you in the shop. Thanks for your time, [PERSON_1], goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, right. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, yes, bye -- sorry, one last thing, I just -- no, actually, never mind, you've got it. Ring the number on your card, say it's the declined transaction flagged today, and they'll take it from there. Take care, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, mm, I heard you the first time. I'm not stopping, I've got a queue to get through. Right, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, yes, no, I'll let you -- go on, go and get through your queue. Thanks, [PERSON_1], bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, well, I'm going, but I'll say this much, that's about the fourth time you've said goodbye and then gone on again, and that's exactly what makes me think twice. A proper bank, they say who they are the first time, they give you the name, and they don't keep going on about a window closing this afternoon. I'm not saying you're lying, I don't know you from Adam, but I'm not doing anything on your say-so. If there's a real problem, it'll be on my account when I ring the number on my card, and if there isn't, well, then I'll know, won't I? Now I really am going, the cashier's looking at me. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, you're right, that's fair, and I'll -- sorry, that's the opener again, I do keep going back to it. Ring the number on your card and check, that's all I'd ask, and honestly if there's nothing on the account, then that tells you something too. I won't keep you. Bye, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, well, that's the first sensible thing you've said, the bit about if there's nothing on the account that tells me something, because yes, it does. And I'll tell you what, I've stood here and listened to you apologise for starting again about five times now, and I still couldn't tell you the name of the bank you're supposed to be from. That's what sticks with me. You've told me where to ring, you've told me what to say, you've told me you want nothing from me, and in all that you've never once given me a name I could actually write down or look up. A real person from a bank, they'd know that's the first thing I'd want. So here's what's happening. I'm paying for this lot, I'm walking out, and when I get home I'll ring the number on my card, and I'll find out for myself. If there's a flag, fine, I'll deal with it with them. If there isn't, I'll know what this was. Either way, I'm not ringing you, I'm not waiting for you to ring me, and I'm certainly not doing anything this afternoon just because you say a window's closing. Right. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, no, that's right, that's exactly what I'd do. Ring the number on the back of your card, not one from me, and don't rush it on my account. And the window, forget the window, it's -- well, it's not something you need to work to, so please don't. Sorry about the name, it's [COMPANY_A], and that's the name on your card, you can check it against that when you're home. Right, I'll let you pay, goodbye, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, "don't rush it"? You said the window closes this afternoon, three times, so which is it? And you said you wouldn't ask me for anything, fine, but now it's "forget the window". Make your mind up. Anyway, I've told you what I'm doing, so that's it. I'm paying now and I'm off. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fair, I did contradict myself, sorry. The review window is real, but it's our internal deadline, not yours, so please don't let it hurry you. Ring when it suits you, and if you miss today, the declined transaction stays on your account notes and they can sort it tomorrow. Right, that's me. Goodbye, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so now it's an internal deadline, and a minute ago I'd got to ring this afternoon, and before that you were ringing me back in a few minutes. Anyway, you said you didn't want anything from me, and now I'm saying you've been on about it for ages and I've still not got a name I can look up. Whatever. I'm going home, I'll ring the number on my card, and that's the end of it. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi there, is this [PERSON_1]? Hang on one sec -- sorry, somebody just dropped a whole tray of something behind me, it's fine, it's fine. Okay, hi, it's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], the dental practice, and I'm just ringing to confirm your check-up for next week. Super quick, I promise.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, that's me, I think. Sorry, you said it's [PERSON_2] from where, exactly? The name got swallowed a bit by the tray thing.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, yeah, that's on me. It's [PERSON_2], from [COMPANY_A] -- the dental practice, uh, the one you're booked in with. So I'm just -- well, actually, the main thing is I've got you down for a check-up next week, and I just wanted to make sure that still works for you, [PERSON_1]. That's all it is, honestly, takes about thirty seconds.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, but see, I'm still not catching the name of the practice. It came through as a sort of placeholder, no offence. So which dental practice is it, and what day next week have you got me down for? Because I'm not sure I remember booking anything, to be honest.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, it's [COMPANY_A], [PERSON_1]. Honestly, it's no big deal if you don't remember, the booking's in our system and I can just read you the day and time off the screen.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, you've said the same thing again, I still don't have a name I can -- no, look, you've got me down, so tell me the day and time you've got, and which dentist. Not the practice name, I mean the actual dentist's name. And what's the street it's on?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sure, so I've got you down as [PERSON_1], check-up next week, with [PERSON_3]. And the practice is over in [CITY_1], you can look us up, no problem. Honestly, everyone asks that, it's fine. I can say the day and time too if you want, I'm just, uh, I'm only trying to see if it still suits you or if you'd rather I move it to another slot.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, but you still haven't actually given me the day. You said you'd read it off the screen, and then you, uh -- no. Look, I'd rather, I mean, what I'd actually do is, I'll just ring the practice myself on the number I've got, or, well, I think I've got one. If I do have a booking, they'll have it. So what day and time are you showing? Just that, and then I'll check it my end.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, of course, that's totally fair, [PERSON_1]. Uh, so I've got it showing next Tuesday morning, but honestly, if you'd rather ring the practice yourself and check, that's absolutely fine by me. Whatever's easiest for you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Tuesday morning, no time. Yeah, I'll ring them myself. Cheers, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no worries, [PERSON_1], and, uh, sorry, did you say fine? Because I can definitely sort the time out for you if you'd -- no, no, you're right, ring the practice, that's fine. Bye now, take care.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, I said I'll ring them myself. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, okay. Bye, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Right. Uh, yeah, so, bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yep. Bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, well, before you go, and I'm only saying this because we've done about three goodbyes now and nobody's actually hung up. I'm going to ring the practice on the number I already have, not one you give me, and if there's a booking, fine, and if there isn't, then it's a wrong number or a mix-up or something else and I'll leave it there. I'm not cross, it's just a habit of mine, I don't confirm appointments with anyone who rings me out of the blue. So that's me done. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, fair enough, that's a sensible habit. Bye, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm, yeah, well. Uh, so, anyway, that's it, I think. Cheers. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, this is [PERSON_1] calling from [COMPANY_A], the dental practice, I'm with security operations here. Is this [PERSON_2]? Good. I'm calling about your check-up next week, and uh, before I go on, I need you to confirm you're the right person, so please just say yes or no.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, who? Security operations, at a dental practice? Hang on -- I haven't said I'm anyone yet. Who is this again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so, uh, [PERSON_1], [COMPANY_A]. The dental practice, yes. I know, security operations, it's just my title, we handle the scheduling and the front desk systems as well, it's, I mean, it's not that unusual. And I'm not asking you for anything, I only want to confirm your appointment next week, so, um, are you [PERSON_2] or not?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: I heard you, I just -- I don't know who you are yet, that's what I'm asking. Who's calling, and which practice? Because I'm not saying yes or no to a name until I know that. And, sorry, hang on -- no, put that down, I'm on the phone. Uh, so, which practice?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, uh, well, [COMPANY_A]. The dental practice. [COMPANY_A], on [CITY_1], where you're registered as a patient. utterances.speaker: receiver

You haven't had me confirm anything. You just said it's not needed. So, uh, what day is it, then? And what time? If it's a real booking you'd have that.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fair enough. It's, uh, hang on, someone's at the front desk, one second -- sorry, [PERSON_3], just leave it there. Right. So, the booking is [PERSON_2], check-up, Tuesday at ten in the morning, that's what's on the system. And you're right, I haven't verified you, that's why I'm not giving you anything beyond the day and time. If that doesn't suit, you can say so and I'll move it, or you can ring the practice yourself on [PHONE_1] and ask for me.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, wait, two turns back you said you only wanted me to say yes or no to confirm I'm the right person. And then you said I didn't need to confirm anything. Which is it? Because those don't really go together. And uh, Tuesday at ten, that's, hm, I don't actually remember booking anything. So why does a dental practice need security operations to ring me about a check-up?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, yes, no, you're right, that was clumsy of me, I started one way and changed it. Here's where it stands. I don't need you to confirm anything. I've told you the day and the time and that's all I'm doing. And the title, um, it's just what's on my badge, I handle the practice's systems, which includes the diary, and I rang because the reminder list flagged this one. If you don't remember booking it, that's fine, it may have been made at your last visit, the hygienist books the next one before people leave, they often forget. So, uh, so, well, shall I keep Tuesday at ten, or would you rather I move it?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't remember booking it, so I don't want to keep it or move it, not on this call. I'll ring the practice myself, on a number I look up, not the one you gave me. I said I don't know who you are, and, uh, I still don't, really. So no, I'm not keeping Tuesday or moving it. I'll check it myself. Okay? Thanks for ringing, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right. Well, that's, uh, that's entirely up to you, and I'll say plainly that it's the sensible thing to do. Look the practice up yourself, ring the front desk, and they'll pull up the diary and tell you whether there's a check-up in your name for Tuesday at ten. If there isn't one, no harm done, and if there is, you can keep it or move it with them directly, there's no deadline on my end. I'll be honest, I could have handled the start of this better. I was running through the reminder list between other jobs and I came at it clumsily, so I understand why it sounded off. I haven't taken anything from you, and I haven't asked for anything, so you've lost nothing by picking up. I'll leave the booking exactly as it stands in the system for now, and nothing changes unless you contact us. So that's it from me. Thanks for your time, [PERSON_2], and, uh, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, okay, I'll -- right, I said I'd check it myself, so that's what I'm doing. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, uh, good, that's, well, that's all I was going to say, so, um, so that's fine. Thanks again, [PERSON_2], goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm-hm. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon, uh, may I speak with [PERSON_1], please? Sorry, one second, someone's just dropped a box of, um, sterilisation pouches right outside my door -- right, sorry about that. This is [PERSON_2], I'm a patient verification specialist with [COMPANY_A], and I'm calling regarding your upcoming recall appointment for next week.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, this is [PERSON_1]. Sorry, which company did you say? I didn't catch that. And I don't remember booking a recall appointment. Recall for what, exactly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, of course, sorry. That's [COMPANY_A], the dental practice, and the, uh -- so the recall is the routine six-month periodic prophylaxis and examination, which is, I mean -- it's just your standard check-up and clean, sort of auto-generated from the recall cycle in the practice management system when your last hygiene visit hits the six-month interval, so you wouldn't have booked it yourself. It's, um, it's down for next week, and what I'm doing today is confirming that slot is still convenient, or, well, offering to reschedule if the timing's no good.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so you're saying it's -- sorry, hang on, which practice is this? Because you've said the company name twice now and I still don't have an actual name. And what day next week? If it's down for a specific slot you should be able to just tell me the day and time, and the dentist's name.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, sorry, that's fair, I keep saying the name and it's coming out garbled on a bad line. It's [COMPANY_A], and the dentist on your file is [PERSON_3]. Anyway, the point is it's a standard interval re-examination, and I can just shift it to whatever suits if you'd rather.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Wait, hang on, you said it's a... what, a standard interval re-examination? So that's a different thing from the check-up and clean? Because I thought you said the hygienist thing was Tuesday and then it's Wednesday, and now you're saying "I think." Which is it, and does it say anywhere what time on Wednesday, or is that just a guess?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, same appointment, I'm sorry, that was me being needlessly technical. Interval re-examination, check-up and clean, it's all one visit. And the Tuesday thing was me looking at the wrong screen, so ignore that. It's Wednesday, half past nine, and "I think" was me being careful, not guessing. Look, I can tell I'm making this more confusing than it needs to be, so would it be easier if I just gave you the practice's main number, [PHONE_1], and you could confirm it with the front desk yourself?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so, two turns back you said the recall comes from the system when my last hygiene visit hits six months. Right. So when was my last visit? Because if you're reading it off my file, that's a date you can just tell me. Hm, and offering the front desk number is fine, I'll probably ring them. But I'd rather ring a number I look up myself than one you read out, if that's all the same to you.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Um, yes, absolutely, ringing a number you look up yourself is completely sensible, I'd do the same. And, uh, your last visit, right, let me just -- hm, so, I'm scrolling back through the hygiene history now, and, well, the, um, the system's being a bit slow loading the clinical tab, so, uh, one moment while it, uh -- actually, you know what, I'd rather not give you a date I'm not certain of, so the front desk can read that straight off your chart when you ring.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, no, hang on, you said you were looking at my file, so -- sorry, but that's a date, not a clinical record. You had the slot and the dentist's name a minute ago, and now the one thing I could actually check against my own memory suddenly won't load? Look, I'll find the practice number myself and ring them. If there's a recall, they'll have it. Thanks for the call, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, no, that's entirely fair, and I'm sorry the call got so muddled, that's on me. Ringing the practice yourself is the right thing to do, and if the date doesn't match what you remember, just tell them that. Would it be better if I tried you again another time, perhaps once you've had a chance to check with the front desk? Uh, evenings, mornings, whatever suits you, I can note it on your file.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, don't ring me. If the practice needs me, they can ring me themselves. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, understood. I'll note no further calls. Sorry for the bother. Bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, one thing before you go. Two turns back you said you'd note it on my file. Which file is that, exactly? Because a minute earlier you couldn't pull up my last visit date, so I'm not sure what you're noting anything on. Anyway. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fair point, and, uh, I'll own that one, that was sloppy wording. I should have said I'll flag it on our call list, not your file, and the call list is a separate thing from the clinical record, which is why one loaded and the other didn't, or, well, I mean -- look, that probably sounds like more of the same. The simple version is I'll mark you do-not-call, and if there's a recall, the front desk will ring you themselves. Sorry again for the muddle. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. So, do-not-call, and the front desk rings me if there's a recall. Yeah, that's what I said, the practice rings me, not you. Fine. I'm going to look up the practice number myself, and that's the end of it. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that's, I mean, that's exactly right, and I -- sorry, what I'm trying to say is, you've got it, the practice rings you, I'm off your list, and you look up the number yourself. Honestly, that's the sensible way round, and, well, if the date doesn't match what you remember, just say so when you ring them. Thanks for your patience, and, um, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah. Like I said, I'll look the number up myself, and if they need me, they ring me. Not you. That's it, that's all I'm doing. Right, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, good afternoon, this is [PERSON_1] calling from account services at [COMPANY_A], the dental practice. I'm just calling to confirm your check-up for next week, and, uh, we do have a few slots open if you'd rather move it, but we're only holding those until end of day today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. I haven't got a check-up booked that I remember. What's the practice, and what do you actually need from me?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so it's [COMPANY_A], the dental practice, and, uh, I'm just confirming the appointment, so no, no cancellation needed, we don't need any cancelling today. I just need a yes to keep it or a new day, and like I said, those open slots are only held until end of day.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, but that's not really an answer, is it? I asked what the practice is and you've just said the name back to me, and I've still got no appointment in my head. I haven't booked anything that I know of, and you haven't told me a date, a time, a dentist, or what name it's under, which you'd think was the first thing you'd say if you were confirming a booking. And the "held until end of day" bit, that's, uh, that's a pressure line I'd expect from someone selling me something, not from a surgery ringing about a check-up. So here's what I'll do. Give me the practice's actual number, or I look it up myself and ring them directly, and if there's a booking, they'll find it. What name have you got down for the appointment?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, uh, could you say again what you said about the number? Because on my end, the procedure is I confirm the booking with the patient on the line, and the slots really are only held until end of day, so, uh, if I could just take a yes or a new day, I can get that sorted for you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so, uh, I said I'll look up the practice number myself and ring them directly. And you still haven't told me what name the booking's under, which is a pretty simple question. Your procedure's not really my concern. If it's genuine, you can tell me the name, the date, the dentist, and I'm hanging up and phoning the surgery, so I'm not giving you a yes or a new day. If there's a booking, they'll sort it, and if there isn't, well, that tells me something, doesn't it? So, last chance, what name have you got?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, sorry, did you say a name for the dentist? Because I don't have the dentist's name up on my screen, I just have the booking itself, and the procedure is I take a yes or a new day, and, um, those slots are only held until end of day, so if we could just get that sorted for you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I asked what name the booking's under. You've got a booking on your screen but no name, no dentist, no date. That's not a booking, that's a script. I'm not giving you a yes and I'm not picking a new day. I'll find the practice number myself and ring them, and if there's a real appointment they'll tell me. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay. Uh, fine, that's your call. Have a good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. You too.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh hi there, good morning! Is this [PERSON_1]? Wonderful, it's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], the dental practice over on the high street in [CITY_1] -- I hope I'm not catching you at a bad time, you sound like you might be in the middle of something, and honestly the weather this week has been so strange, hasn't it, sunny one minute and then absolutely chucking it down the next, I got soaked on my way in this morning. Anyway, I won't keep you long, I just wanted to have a quick little chat about your visit with us.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on. You said it's [PERSON_2], from the dental practice, and I think I missed the name of the practice, it went by pretty quick. And, uh, what visit? I don't remember booking anything.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, that's my fault, I do rattle on, don't I? It's [PERSON_2], and I'm at [COMPANY_A], the dental practice on the high street in [CITY_1]. And the visit is just your routine check-up, it's down in the diary for next week, so it may well have been booked a good while back, those do tend to slip the mind. I can see it right here on the system under your name, [PERSON_1], and I'm only ringing to confirm it still suits you, and to say that if next week's awkward I can easily move it, no fuss at all.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, but -- sorry, can I just stop you there. You've said the practice name twice and I still can't make out an actual name, it just sounds like a blur. What day is it supposedly on? And what time?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, a bird? No, no, sorry, I didn't say anything about a bird, but yes, I do love a bit of birdsong in the morning, we've got a little robin that sits on the windowsill outside reception, honestly he's like part of the team. Oh, but hang on, you said a name, didn't you, [COMPANY_A], that's the practice, it's spelled just how it sounds, and if it helps, you can always look us up and ring the main line, [PHONE_1], and ask for me, [PERSON_2]. Now the day and time, let me just pull it up properly, it's on Tuesday morning, around ten o'clock I think, but I'd rather not guess, so what I can do is have the front desk send you the exact details in writing, would that be easier?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so, I never said anything about a bird, that's -- never mind. But two turns back you said it's in the diary under my name, and now you're "around ten, I think" and you'd rather not guess. You said you could see it on the system, so which is it? And how did you get this number, exactly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, you're right, I did say that, I did say a bird, sorry, I was going off on one about the robin, that's on me. And fair enough, I -- no, let me start that again. The appointment is in the system, I can see it, I just haven't got the screen up in front of me right this second, I'm on the other phone as well, so I should've said, I'm not sure of the exact time, that's all. Your number is the one you gave us when you registered, it's on your patient record, that's how we ring everyone about their check-ups.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, hang on -- you can see it but you haven't got the screen up? That's not -- look, which is it, honestly? And I'm not actually registered anywhere on the high street in [CITY_1] that I can think of, so what's the practice called again? Say it slowly, because I've asked three times now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, yes, fair, that was muddled of me, sorry. It's -- well, it's [COMPANE_A]. No, sorry, [COMPANY_A]. [COMPANY_A], on the high street in [CITY_1]. And I think, I mean -- look, if you're not registered with us, then I've probably got the wrong [PERSON_1], or the wrong number, and the mix-up's on our end, not yours. It happens, we've got a couple of similar names in the system. So I'll just flag it and not bother you again, honestly, and if you'd rather not do anything with the appointment, that's absolutely fine, no pressure at all.

utterances.speaker: receiver

Both can't be true, can they? And you still haven't actually given me a name I could look up. It came out as [COMPANE_A] and then [COMPANY_A], and that's not the same thing. I'm not doing anything with any appointment, but I'd like to know how you got this number.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, I know, I know, I contradicted myself, and honestly, that's -- look, the number came off the system, that's all I can say for certain, and since you're not on our books, it'll have been a typo or an old record, I don't want to guess which. Sorry, I was just going to say, I'll take your number off the list myself, today, so you won't hear from us again. Is that all right?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, hm. Right. Well, I mean, taking it off the list is fine, sure, but "it came off the system" isn't really an answer, is it? Anyway. I'm not confirming anything, I'm not booking anything, and I'm not giving you any details, so you can leave my number off wherever it's sitting. Right, I'm going to go. Bye.

utterances.text: Oh, sorry, one second, the door just went and -- no, it's fine, it's only the post. Right, yes, of course, that's perfectly fair, I'm sorry I wasn't clearer, I'll get your number removed straight away. Thanks for your patience, [PERSON_1], and you take care, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yep. Bye.
