utterances.text: Oh, bye, dear, and you take care too. Oh, but hang on, you said it was this morning, didn't you? Only I thought you said earlier it was yesterday you'd -- no, that was me, wasn't it, going on about the shops. Well, never you mind, I'll sort it with the bank. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, this morning, that's right. Okay, bye then.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hang on, that's the kettle, it's gone off with a click, and the cat's just, there's a pigeon on the sill and he's gone all, honestly, he'll have the net curtain down. Sorry, dear, where was I? Yes, bye now, I'll ring the bank from my purse card, the one on the back. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, is this [PERSON_1]? Hi, it's, uh, [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], I work in the compliance office there. I'm just following up on the note you left with us last week, the one about the, ah, the statement from the spring. You mentioned it was the March statement, I think, or was it April? Sorry, I've got it written down somewhere, it's just, it's been one of those mornings.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Who? Sorry, who is this, and which company? I didn't leave any note with anyone, I don't think. And I'm in the middle of a shop queue here, so, uh, get to the point.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, that's fair, and I'm sorry to catch you in a queue. It's [PERSON_2], from [COMPANY_A]. Compliance. And, uh, you may be right about the note, I think it might have come through your, your husband, or, no, sorry, I'm mixing up two files, it was probably someone else's. It's a small thing, really, nothing to stand in a queue worrying about. Look, why don't I tell you the actual reason I'm ringing, because it isn't really about a statement. It's more, well, it's more personal than that, and I'd rather say it when you've got a quiet minute. Is now alright, or should I try you later?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, hang on -- sorry, not you, the woman in front's trying to put her whole trolley through the, uh, the self-scan thing. Right. So you've mixed me up with someone else's file, and you're ringing about something personal, but you won't say what it is. That's, I mean, that sounds like a wrong number to me, or something worse. Just tell me now, what company, and what is it you actually want from me?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, I don't blame you for asking, and, uh, please do ask, ask me anything you like, I'd honestly rather you did. Sorry, one second, there's a, a door banging somewhere down the corridor, they're doing something with the lifts today. Right. Where was I. It's [COMPANY_A], and I did say compliance, but, well, that's only where I'm sitting when I ring. The real reason is [PERSON_3]. You've been messaging with [PERSON_3], haven't you, for a while now? I'd, I'd rather not say more than that on a line like this.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. Stop. I'm not discussing who I've been messaging with someone who won't even tell me what he wants. You rang me, remember, and you've mixed up files, you've changed your story twice, and now it's "I'd rather not say more on a line like this." Uh, no. That's not how it works. If you're really from [COMPANY_A], you tell me what this is about, plainly, right now, or I'm hanging up.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm. Yes. No, you're right, I, uh, I understand why you'd say that. Please don't hang up just yet, that's, well, that's the one thing I'd ask. It's only that [PERSON_3] is in a bit of a spot, a travel thing, in [CITY_1], and, um, I was asked to reach out, gently, before it got any, any worse. And it's the sort of situation where it would be kinder if, if you kept it between us for now, I mean, not friends, not family, they wouldn't really understand. I'd rather not put it in writing anywhere, either.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Keep it quiet, don't tell anyone, nothing in writing. No. I'm done with this, I've heard that one before. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Please, wait, I -- no, I don't want to, to upset you, that's the last thing. It's just that [PERSON_3] asked me to, to make sure you'd, well, you'd be someone who wouldn't, uh, who wouldn't turn this into a bigger thing than it, than it needs to be. And I do think, honestly, it would go better if you gave me a little time on this, a day, say, or, or even less, before anything is, you know, said to anyone else.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. You said ten seconds ago you didn't want to put anything in writing, and now it's, what, give you a day? Make your mind up. And earlier you said you were ringing about a note I left, then a statement, then it wasn't the statement at all. I'm not giving you a day, I'm not giving you anything. If [PERSON_3] is really in some bother, [PERSON_3] can ring me themselves. And I'll be checking with them, and with [COMPANY_A], on a number I look up myself. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say, uh, you'll be checking with [PERSON_3]? No, no, please don't do that, not yet. If you ring [PERSON_3] now, on a, on a line that's, well, it's not safe for [PERSON_3] to be answering, that would only make things worse, I'm, I really am asking you to leave it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, that's rich. Don't check, don't tell anyone, don't ring them. That's the one thing you don't want me to do, and that's exactly why I'm going to do it. I've been here before, mate, and I'm not doing it again. Don't ring me back. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, wait, I, look, I'm only -- no. Let me say it differently. I'm not asking you to do anything, not today, I only meant that, well, [PERSON_3] was quite, quite particular that it stayed, uh, that it stayed small, and I didn't want to be the one who, who let that go. But, if you'd rather ring [COMPANY_A] on a number you've found yourself, then, I mean, that's, that is your choice, of course.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, it is my choice, thanks. And that's what I'm doing. I'll find the number myself, I'll ring [PERSON_3] myself, and if there's anything in it, they'll tell me. Don't ring this number again. Right, I'm at the till, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right. Yes. Of course. Uh, I'll, I'll leave it there, then. Mind how you go.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mind how I go? Don't you tell me to... hang on, did you say leave it there, like, leave it there at the till? What's that supposed to mean? No. Never mind. I'm not having it. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hey, [PERSON_1]? It's me, from the support desk at [COMPANY_A], the one you've been messaging with these past few weeks. Okay, so I know I said I was home this week, but I'm actually stuck in [CITY_1] right now, and honestly, I didn't know who else to call. It's kind of a mess, but it's quick to sort out, and I'd really rather this stayed between us for now, you know?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, uh, hang on a second -- [PERSON_1], yeah, that's me, but who is this? I've been messaging with someone, sure, but I'm not -- I mean, how'd you even get this number? And "stayed between us" -- what does that mean exactly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, [PERSON_1], come on, it's me, we've been talking for weeks! You gave me this number yourself, I'm pretty sure it was, uh, the second week? Or maybe I got it off the account profile, whatever, that's not the point. And I said stayed between us, not forever, just for now, because honestly your friends and family wouldn't get it, they'd make a big thing out of nothing and it's really such a small thing, [PERSON_1], I just need a hand for like two minutes.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, but -- you still haven't said your name. You keep saying it's me, and, uh, that's not an answer. And the number thing, you said I gave it to you, then maybe the account profile? Which one is it? And why wouldn't my friends and family get it? What is the small thing, exactly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, so, it's [PERSON_2], [PERSON_1], you know that, we've -- look, I wasn't trying to be cagey, it's just that, I mean, the number, it was both, sort of, you gave it and it's on the profile, it doesn't matter. And the small thing is, uh, my card got -- no, wait, my [COMPANY_B] booking fell through and I'm stuck here, and I just need you to cover [AMOUNT_1] to get me home, that's all, it's honestly nothing. Everybody asks that, the name and the number, it's fine, but can we just do this quick before I miss my window?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Wait, wait. You're from the support desk, and now you're stuck somewhere and you want me to cover [AMOUNT_1]? Why would support be asking me for money? That's, I mean, that doesn't make sense. And "don't tell your friends and family," then "quick before I miss my window" -- that's, no. My relative got burned on something like this last year. I'm not sending anything. If you really work at [COMPANY_A], you can go through their official channels, and I'll talk to them there. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, [PERSON_1], hang on, please, don't hang up. Okay, you asked about -- what was it, the friends thing, why they wouldn't get it? I just meant, you know, they'd worry for nothing, it's not like I'm asking for a lot. And look, the support desk part is separate, that's just my job, this is personal, which is exactly why I called you and not the company, so there's no point going through them, they can't help with this. It's really just a couple minutes, [PERSON_1], I promise.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. See, a minute ago you said you were stuck, and you never said anything about it being personal, that's new. And you said you didn't know who else to call, but now it's me and not the company because they can't help? That doesn't hold together. I'm not covering anything, I'm not sending anything, and I'm not keeping it between us. Don't call this number again. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Wait, [PERSON_1], hold on, sorry, somebody's just -- hang on one sec -- no, sorry, it's just the guy at the counter here, he keeps waving at me. Okay, I'm back. Look, you're being really unfair, honestly, I'm not asking for a lot and I thought, I mean after all these weeks, you'd, you'd just trust me on this. Can you at least not hang up on me? Just give me two minutes.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hold on, sweetheart, put that down, I'm on the -- sorry. No, listen. Weeks of messaging isn't trust, it's messaging. You still haven't told me anything I can check, and every answer you've given has changed. I'm not giving you two minutes, and I'm not sending you anything. I'm done. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: [PERSON_1], please, just one more second, I'm not trying to get you in any trouble, I swear. I can hear you're upset, and honestly, that's on me, I should've explained it better at the start, I just got flustered because I'm stuck out here and I'm a little embarrassed to be asking, and when I get embarrassed I kind of ramble and say things in the wrong order. But if you want to check something, fine, call the desk at [COMPANY_A], ask for [PERSON_2], they'll tell you I work there, they'll tell you all of it. Or, wait, actually, don't, because it's after hours and nobody picks up this late, and then you'd just be sitting there waiting, and I'd miss my window, and I really can't, so, if you could just hear me out, it'd take, what, two minutes, three at most?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so you just offered me a way to check, and then took it back in the same breath. That's what I'm hearing. No. I'm not hearing you out, not for two minutes, not for three. If you work there, [COMPANY_A] can sort out your trip home. I'm hanging up now, and please don't call this number again. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi there, is this [PERSON_1]? Oh good, I wasn't sure I had the right number, I've got it down as [PHONE_1], or, uh, no, sorry, it's your mobile I rang, the one ending in, well, never mind that. This is [PERSON_2] calling from customer care at [COMPANY_A], and I hope I'm not catching you at a bad moment, you sound like you might've been in the middle of something. How's your day been so far?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Who's asking? And, uh, which company did you say?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, yes, I rattled on there, didn't I? It's [PERSON_2], from customer care at [COMPANY_A], that's your bank, the one your, um, your current account is with. And I'm ringing because, well, there was a -- actually, no, let me back up, it's nothing to panic about, but we had a payment attempt on your account today that got declined, and I wanted to check with you whether it was yours. And look, if you'd rather not take my word for it, that's completely fine, you can hang up and ring the number on the back of your card, I'll happily wait.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, sorry, [CHILD] don't -- sorry. A declined payment? For how much, and where? Because if you're my bank you'd already have that in front of you, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, you're right, I do have it right here, and I'm the one who got muddled, not you. It's [AMOUNT_1] at [COMPANY_B], online, this morning, though, uh, I said earlier it was today and I think it actually came through late last night, my screen's got the timestamp a bit odd. Anyway, it was declined, so nothing's left your account, which is the good news. And all I need from you is a yes or no on whether that was you, nothing else, no details, nothing like that.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. You said it was this morning, then last night, and before that you said my number ended in something and then -- never mind. So which is it? And you said you'd got my number down as [PHONE_1], but then you said it was my mobile you rang, which, I mean, those aren't the same thing, are they?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, fair enough, I did tie myself in knots there, and you're right to point it out. Honestly, I'm a chatterbox, my team lead is forever telling me to slow down. The timing, I can't give you a straight answer on, because I was reading off my screen and then talking over myself. And the number, I fumbled that too, I think I was looking at two fields at once and mixed up which one I'd dialled. It's probably nothing, just me waffling, but I'd say that's reason enough not to take any of it on trust from a stranger on the phone. So here's what I'd do if I were you, and I mean this: hang up, flip your card over, ring the number printed on the back, and ask them about a declined payment on your account. If there's a note on it, they'll see it. If there isn't, well, then you've lost two minutes and I've had my knuckles rapped. I won't be offended, honestly, and I'm not going to ask you for anything to get on with this. How's that sound?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so I ring the number on the back of my card, that's what you're saying? Ring the number on the back of the card. Not a number you give me, the one printed on the card. Because honestly, that's what I'd do anyway. [CHILD], put that down, please. Sorry. Yeah. I'll ring them myself, if there's a problem they'll tell me. Okay? Right, bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, exactly, the number printed on your card, not one from me, and that's the right instinct. No problem at all, you go and sort the little one out. Take care, [PERSON_1], bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, bye, and, sorry, just one last thing before you -- no, honestly, that's it, you go. And if the number on the card gets you a long wait, that's normal, don't read anything into it. Take care now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, okay. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Goodbye, [PERSON_1]. Hope the rest of your day goes smoothly.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yep. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say you'd ring the, uh, the branch? Because honestly the branch won't have it on screen, it's -- hang on, you didn't say that, did you? No, no, my mistake, I've lost the thread. Right. Bye, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I said the number on the card. The one printed on the back. Not the branch, not a number from you. Anyway. I'm going now. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, you're absolutely right, the number on the back of the card, that's what you said and that's exactly what I'd do in your shoes, so ignore my muddle about the branch, that was me getting ahead of myself again. And honestly, you've handled this about as well as anyone could. You asked who I was, you caught me contradicting myself, you picked the safe way to check, and I'd much rather you do all of that and ring me a fuss over nothing than go along with a caller you weren't sure about. If it turns out there's a note on the account, fine, and if there isn't, then you've lost a couple of minutes and that's all. Either way, I won't ring you back about it, I'll leave it entirely with you. Right, I've kept you long enough and you've got [CHILD] to see to. Take care, [PERSON_1], bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, I -- no. I mean, I'll check it myself, on the card number, like I said. Look, I'm done now, okay? Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello? Uh, hi -- sorry, is, is this [PERSON_1]? Um, yeah, hang on, I think I've got my notes here somewhere... okay, so, I'm calling on behalf of [COMPANY_A], the dental practice, and it's just, uh, about your check-up next week.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? Oh, uh, yeah, that's me. Hang on, I've got something on the hob. Check-up next week, you said?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, yeah, the check-up, it's, uh, it's booked for next -- oh, I'm sorry, go ahead, no, I mean, I just wanted to confirm it's still, still okay for you. And, um, if it isn't, if next week's awkward, I can, I can probably move it, I think, it's no trouble.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, um, I -- sorry, which dentist did you say? I mean, I've got a check-up, I think, but, no, hang on. What day is it meant to be? Because I'd have to, uh... sorry, it's just the pan's spitting. What day did you say?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, no, that's okay, take your time, I can wait, honestly, sort the pan first. Um, so it's, let me just look at my, my notes again... it's with [PERSON_2], the hygienist, no, sorry, the dentist, [PERSON_2] is the dentist, [PERSON_3] is the hygienist, I always get those mixed up, I'm only, I'm only helping out on the phones this week, I'm not really, I don't normally do this. Anyway, it's, uh, it's down for Tuesday, I think, next Tuesday, in the morning, and I'm sorry, I know it's a bit out of the blue, me ringing you, but the practice just likes to check people are still coming, because if someone can't make it, then, well, it leaves a gap and, um, that's a shame for the next person waiting, so, yeah. But if Tuesday's no good, I really can move it, it's not a problem at all.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what -- a tuna, did you say? Oh, Tuesday. Sorry, Tuesday. Hang on, I've turned the pan down. Um, Tuesday morning, yeah, that sounds sort of right, I think I did book something. But I don't know the names you said, [PERSON_2], that doesn't ring a bell. Is that, is that the same place I usually go?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, uh, yes, sorry, Tuesday, yeah, Tuesday morning. And it's, it's [COMPANY_A], the dental practice, same, same place, I think, the one you've, you've booked with before. I mean, if you've got it in your diary as Tuesday morning, that's, that's the one. Um, and I'm sorry about the names, I probably said them badly, I did get them muddled before, but, but it is [COMPANY_A], that's who I'm ringing from. And if you'd rather, you can ring the practice yourself, I mean, I don't want to, to bother you while you're cooking, I just, I only wanted to check Tuesday was still alright, or move it if not.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so, Tuesday morning is fine, I think. Yeah, Tuesday's fine. Sorry, I just, I don't know the dentist's name you said, that's the thing. It's not the one I remember. So it's the same place, you said? [COMPANY_A]? Hang on, is that, sorry, is that the one near the, the shops? Because I've only got the one dentist, I think. Tuesday's fine, anyway. Is that all you needed?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, yes, that's, that's all, that's really all I -- sorry, I didn't mean to talk over you. Um, the shops, I don't, I can't actually say where it is, I'm only, I only have the name here, and, and maybe the dentist's name I gave was wrong, I did say I get them muddled. But if it doesn't sound like your dentist, then, honestly, please don't take my word for it, ring the practice yourself and check, that's, that's the best thing, I'd feel awful if I'd confused you. Tuesday's fine, then, I'll just, I'll put that down, and, and I'm sorry for, for bothering you while you were cooking.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, no, you're alright, you weren't bothering me, honestly. Um... yeah, no, that's a good idea, I'll ring them myself. I've got the number somewhere, uh, in the drawer, I think. Sorry, I'm just, um, stirring. Anyway, thanks for ringing, that was kind of you. Right, bye now, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, yes, good afternoon, is this [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2], I'm the regional supervisor over at [COMPANY_A]. I'm, uh, following up on the message my colleague left you last week -- or, no, I think it was the week before, doesn't matter. Basically there's a service charge on your unit that's showing overdue, and I need to sort it today because it can affect your access to the building.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, this is, uh -- who did you say you were with again? Which building, I mean -- and I didn't, I haven't had any message from anyone. What's the actual charge, and who's it owed to? I've got about two minutes.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so, [COMPANY_A], we handle the management side of your building, I said that at the start. And look, whether you got the message isn't really the point, it was logged as delivered on our end. The charge is [AMOUNT_1], reference [ACCOUNT_REF], and it's owed to the management account, which is us. Now, I do need to be straight with you, [PERSON_1], if this isn't resolved today I can't promise your fob stays active, and I'd rather not be the one explaining that to you at the door.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, you said my what stays active? My phone? Because I haven't missed a bill on that, so -- no, wait, a fob? Right. Okay, but you didn't say the building's name, you said a company name that's a placeholder to me, so which building are we talking about? And "logged as delivered" is not a message I received. Who sets the charge, and where do I see it in writing? Because I'm not paying anything over the phone to somebody I've never spoken to.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, [PERSON_1], I think we're getting tangled here. The building's on your lease paperwork, I shouldn't have to read it out to you. And nobody's asking you to pay over the phone, I never said that, that's, uh -- what I said was I need it sorted today, and the quickest way is a transfer to the holding account, because the portal's down on our end. Honestly, I don't know why you're being so difficult about this, I've got six other residents on my list this afternoon who just dealt with it. And the written notice, yes, that went out by post, though like I said earlier it was an email, so, whichever, it'll be in your records.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so let me stop you there, because that's three things that don't line up. First you said you weren't asking me to pay over the phone, then the quickest way is a transfer to a holding account. That's asking me to pay. Then the notice was posted, then it was an email, then "whichever." And you can't tell me the building, but you want money moved today. That's not how a managing agent works. They've got my address, my lease, a portal I can log into, and a letter with a reference I can check against my own paperwork. If the portal's down, it can wait till it's up. A fob doesn't get cut off in an afternoon over one charge I've never been told about. And I'm not doing anything today because you've got six other people on your list, that's your list, not mine. Here's what happens. I'll look up the management company's number myself, from my lease, not from you, and I'll call them directly. If there's a charge, they'll confirm it and send it in writing. I'm not giving you anything, and I'm not agreeing to any transfer. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Look, I'm not asking you to do anything unreasonable here, [PERSON_1], I'm really not. I'm telling you the charge is overdue, I'm telling you it's [AMOUNT_1], and I'm telling you it needs sorting today. That's all I'm saying. If you ring the office, fine, but they'll only send you back to me, I'm the one who handles overdue accounts for the region, so you'll just be losing time. And honestly, uh, I've been very patient with you. I'm just saying, if the fob stops working tomorrow, that's not on me. I did warn you. I warned you at the start of this call.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I don't think -- look, I said goodbye a minute ago and you kept going. "They'll only send you back to me" is exactly why I'm calling them. If they do, fine, they can say it to me in writing. And "I warned you" isn't a notice, it's a threat on a phone call, and you've now said it twice. I'm done. Don't call this number again. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, I -- look, I don't think that's, uh -- no. Fine. If you'd rather make this harder than it needs to be, that's your decision, [PERSON_1], I've noted that you declined. But when you ring the office and they tell you it's on the account, I don't want to hear that nobody gave you the chance. That's all. Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, no, that's -- sorry, hang on, someone's just stuck their head in the door, I'm late for this thing. Right. Look, if there's a charge, the office can send it in writing and I'll deal with it with them, through the number on my own paperwork. Nobody's been denied a chance here. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, uh, good afternoon, is that [PERSON_1]? Sorry to trouble you. This is [PERSON_2], I'm a case handler at [COMPANY_A], the property management side, and I did try you yesterday, well, this morning, I think, it might've been the evening, anyway. It's about the service charge on your flat, it's showing as overdue, and I'm a bit concerned your building access could be affected. Hello? Sorry, are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hello, yes, yes I'm here, sorry, I was just, uh, I had the telly on in the other room and I'd gone to turn it down. Yes, this is [PERSON_1] speaking. Now who did you say you were again? Property management, was it? I've not had anyone ring me, I don't think, though I never hear the phone half the time, it's in the kitchen and I'm usually in the front room with the cat. Overdue, you said? That doesn't sound right, I'm sure I've paid everything, I always do. Though, I mean, I do get in a muddle with the letters sometimes.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh no, that's quite all right, take your time, honestly. Sorry, just a second, there's someone at my desk, I'll, yes, I'll be right with you. Sorry about that. It's [PERSON_2], from [COMPANY_A], we look after the building for the freeholder. And please don't worry about the letters, a lot of people get in a muddle, it's really very common. I've got it here as [AMOUNT_1] outstanding, reference [ACCOUNT_REF], and I'd hate for it to go any further, because after a certain point the access fobs can be switched off, and I'd rather that didn't happen to you. Are you still there? Sorry, the line's gone a bit faint.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, the fobs, hm. Well, I'm still here. I'd want to look at my own papers first, though, I think.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, of course, yes, that's very sensible, you go and look, I'd never want to rush you. Sorry, just, what was it you wanted me to clarify, was it the, the reference? Or the fobs, I think you said? Hello? Sorry, I just wanted to check you hadn't gone. Only the thing is, I did want to say, if it's all the same to you, it'd be so much easier to sort it out today, by phone, rather than have it go to the next stage, which, well, I'm only thinking of you, there's a fee that gets added and I'd hate for that to land on you. And I can take payment over the phone with you now, if that's easier, save you hunting through all those letters.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, I haven't gone, I'm only standing here with a pile of envelopes, there's one from the, well, never mind, it's the gas people. Now, you said it was this morning you rang me, didn't you? Or it was yesterday, I'm sure you said the evening at first. Which was it? Only I was in all yesterday evening and the phone never went, I'd have heard, I think. And it's funny, because you said it was the freeholder you look after the building for, but I thought the, uh, the managing people were a different lot altogether. Anyway, paying over the phone, I don't know about that. I've never done that sort of thing, not with a stranger, and I'd much rather find the letter first, if that's all right.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, I'm sorry, you're quite right to ask, that was muddled of me. It was this morning, I'm nearly certain, and I think the evening bit was just me talking about when I'd logged it. And, yes, the freeholder arrangement, it's a bit confusing, there's [COMPANY_B] on the paperwork, and we handle the day to day for them. Hello? Sorry, are you still there? I do understand not wanting to pay a stranger over the phone, I'd feel exactly the same, really. But I'm only trying to protect you from the fobs being switched off, and the fee on top, and it's [AMOUNT_1] at the moment, which is a lot less than it would be next week. If you did want to settle it today, it's honestly the simplest way, and I'd stay on the line with you the whole time, so you wouldn't be on your own with it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, that's kind of you, staying on the line and all that, it is a bit lonely here of an afternoon, I won't pretend it isn't. But, hm, I'm not sure I like the sound of it getting dearer next week. My late husband always said if somebody's in a hurry for your money, you ought to be in no hurry to give it, he was a great one for that, he once sent a man packing at the door about the guttering, and the man had a van and everything. Where was I? Yes. You've changed your story a bit, haven't you, the morning and the evening, and now it's this other company on the paperwork. I'm not saying anything's wrong, I'm only saying it's a lot to keep hold of. So what I think I'll do is find the actual letter, because there's always a number on those, and ring them myself. I've got the little book somewhere by the phone, if the cat hasn't been sitting on it. Would that be all right? Only I'd feel better doing it that way, if it's all the same to you.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, of course, that's very sensible, and your husband sounds like a lovely man. Hello? Sorry, I just wanted to be sure you were still there. Um, only, I did say I'd never rush you, and I'm not, it's just that I rang you yesterday evening, I'm quite sure of it now, and I'd hate for you to think I'd been careless with the dates. Sorry, I know I said this morning before. But I do worry, if you ring the number in your book, they might not have the case in front of them, because it's with me, you see, and then the fobs could get switched off in the meantime, and I'd feel dreadful. So if it's all the same, it really would be easiest to just settle the [AMOUNT_1] with me now, and I'll stay on the line, I promise.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. Well. Uh, I'm just, hang on, I'm thinking. Oh dear. You see, that's the third time now it's changed, isn't it? Morning, then evening, then this morning, now yesterday evening again. And if it's with you and nobody else can see it, well, that's not how my gas people do it, they've got it all on a screen whoever you speak to. No, I think I'll do it my way, dear. I'll find the letter and ring the number on it, and if the fobs go off, I'll manage, I've got a perfectly good key somewhere. Thank you for ringing, I do appreciate the chat, but I won't be paying anything today. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, please, don't hang up, [PERSON_1], I'm, sorry, one moment, there's a door banging out in the corridor, hold on. Right, sorry, I'm back. Hello? Are you still there? I really am sorry about the dates, I get them muddled when I've a long list, it doesn't mean anything, and I'd hate for you to think badly of me. It's only that I'm worried for you, truly, because if the fobs do go off it's such a nuisance to get them switched back on, and the fee does get added. So if you could just settle the [AMOUNT_1] with me now, today, I'd feel so much better, and I'll stay right here on the line the whole time, I promise.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, I'm still here, I hadn't actually put it down, I was only saying goodbye, you carried on talking. Now, you said just then it was a long list you'd got muddled on, but before you told me it was my case, with you, that nobody else could see. Well, which is it, a long list or just the one? I'm not being funny, dear, I'm only saying. And you said the fee was added at the next stage, then it was next week, now it's just the fobs. It's all rather shifty, and I'd sooner not. I'm going to find my letter and ring the number on it, that's the end of it. Thank you again, bye bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, I, no, I'm sorry, I didn't mean to, hello? Are you still there, [PERSON_1]? You're quite right, and I'm sorry, I do get flustered, it's a long list but yours is the one I've flagged, if that makes sense. Please, I'd just hate for anything to happen to your access, and I'm only trying to protect you, truly. If you could settle the [AMOUNT_1] with me today, I'll stay on the line the whole time, and then you wouldn't need to ring anyone, you wouldn't have to worry about any of it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, dear, no. I've said, I'm going to find my letter and ring the number on it. That's what I'll do, I'll ring the number on the letter. And you needn't keep telling me you'll stay on the line, because I don't want to settle anything with you today, I'd sooner not. I'm sorry if you're flustered, I'm sure it's a hard job, but I'm putting the phone down now. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello? Hi there, hello, is this [PERSON_1]? Hi, it's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], the customer care team, how are you doing today? Sorry, can you hear me okay? I said it's [PERSON_2], from [COMPANY_A].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, I can hear you. Who is this, exactly, and what's it regarding?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, yeah, fair enough, sorry, I've gone and rattled off my name like we're old friends. So it's [PERSON_2], I'm with customer care at [COMPANY_A], your bank, and I'm calling about -- well, it's, uh, it's probably nothing to panic about, but there was a transaction on your card earlier that got declined, and I just wanted to check whether that was actually you. And look, if it makes you more comfortable, you're welcome to hang up and ring us back on the number on the back of your card, I'll happily wait.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, two turns back you said you were with "customer care", and now it's "your bank". Which is it? And I'd just like to know, which card are you referring to, and what was the declined transaction, the merchant and the amount? If you're calling from the bank, you should have that in front of you.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, good catch, that's me being sloppy. It's both, honestly. Customer care is the team I'm on, and [COMPANY_A] is the bank, so same place, I just said it badly. Anyway, yes, I do have it in front of me. It was a card payment of [AMOUNT_1] at a merchant called [COMPANY_B], and it was declined earlier today. I'm only looking at the card ending in the last four on the account, and I'm not going to ask you for any card details or anything like that. All I need from you is a yes or no on whether that purchase was yours.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. So you haven't actually told me which card, you've just said "the card ending in the last four", and that isn't a number, that's a description of a number. And I'll say it again, I'm not confirming a yes or no on anything until I know who I'm talking to. You offered I could ring back on the number on the back of my card, so what I'd like to do is that. Is there a reference I should quote when I get through, so they can route me to you?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, you're right, "the last four" isn't a number, that was me being vague, sorry. And honestly, ringing back is the right call, please do. When you get through, quote [ACCOUNT_REF], that's the reference on the declined payment, and ask for the customer care team, they'll find the note and put you through to me, or whoever's free. And listen, there's no rush on this at all, the card's already blocked that payment, so nothing's going to happen while you ring. If you'd rather not even use my reference, just tell them you've had a call about a declined [AMOUNT_1] payment at [COMPANY_B] and they'll see it on your account.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay. I'll ring the number on the back of my card, and I'll quote what you've said. Though I'll note it's a bit odd that you can't tell me which card, but I'll let that go. I'm going to hang up now and call them directly, and if there's a note on the account, they'll find it. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, absolutely, go ahead and ring them, that's exactly what I'd do. And you're right about the card, that one's on me. I should've just said it at the start. I'll make sure the note's on the account, and when you get through, if they ask, it was the [AMOUNT_2] payment at [COMPANY_B], that's the one that was declined. Anyway, take care, [PERSON_1], and sorry for the runaround.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, right, hold on, I'm just -- hm. That's [AMOUNT_2] now? A minute ago you told me it was [AMOUNT_1]. Those aren't the same figure. Um, anyway, it doesn't change what I'm doing. I'm hanging up and ringing the number on my card, and I won't be relying on anything you've said. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, hang on, sorry, somebody's just dropped a stack of folders right next to my desk, give me a second -- okay, sorry. Right, [AMOUNT_2], you're dead right, I've crossed my wires, it's [AMOUNT_1], that's the figure on the declined payment, I've got two screens open and I read the wrong one. Honestly though, don't take my word on any of it. Ring the number on your card and let them tell you what's on the account, and if the figures don't match what I've said, trust them over me. Take care, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. So that's the name, the department, the card, and now the amount, all shifting around. I'm not going to try to reconcile them. Whatever's actually on my account, the bank can tell me when I ring them myself, on the number I already have. I won't be quoting your reference, either. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no worries, honestly, that's the right instinct. Sorry, hang on, my headset's gone crackly, that's better. Look, I'm not going to talk you out of it, and I wouldn't want to. Ring the number on your card, tell them you've had a call about a declined payment, and whatever they say is on the account, believe that over anything I've said today. And please don't read out anything I've told you to them as if it's gospel, I clearly muddled the figures. Take care, [PERSON_1], and sorry again for the mix-up.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Of course, yes, goodbye, and honestly, before you go, I don't want you leaving this thinking I was trying to get one over on you, because I wasn't, and I'm sorry that I made it as muddled as I did. I changed the amount on you, I was vague about the card, I fumbled which team I was on, and if someone rang me like that, I'd hang up too, so you've done exactly the right thing. Please don't use my reference, and please don't treat a single thing I said as confirmed. Just ring the number on the back of your card, tell them you got a call about a declined payment and you'd like to know whether there's anything on the account, and let them tell you what's what. If it turns out there's nothing there, then you've lost five minutes and I've lost your trust, which is fair. And I won't ring you back, so there's no need to pick up if an unknown number shows up later today. Anyway, take care, [PERSON_1], and thanks for being so careful with it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, I'll take the apology, but I'd rather be plain about where I've landed. You gave me one version of who you were, then another. The card was never named, the amount changed halfway through, and you kept coming back to my ringing the bank while still trying to give me a reference to quote. Whether that's carelessness or something else, I can't tell from here, and I'm not going to try. What I will say is that the offer to go and check was the one sensible thing in the call, and I'm taking it. I'll ring the number I already have, I'll tell them nothing about this call beyond the fact that it happened, and I'll let them tell me what's on my account. If there's genuinely a declined payment, they'll have it. If there isn't, that tells me what I need to know. So, no need to ring me back and no need to explain further. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, one sec, somebody's just wheeled a trolley past and I've lost my train of thought entirely. Okay, I'm back. No, that's fair, all of it, and I'm not going to argue with a word you've said. You're doing the right thing, so please just ring the number on your card and let them tell you what's on the account. And you don't need to tell them anything about me or this call if you'd rather not. Take care, [PERSON_1], goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Right. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello? Hi, is that [PERSON_1]? Sorry, uh, I'm calling from the mobile network security team at [COMPANY_A], my name's [PERSON_2]. I'm so sorry to ring out of the blue -- I'm afraid there's been some unusual activity on your line, so we've put it on a temporary hold just to keep you protected. Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, I'm, uh -- hang on, I'm still here. Sorry, who exactly did you say you were with? And what do you mean a hold, I'm literally using the line right now, so, I mean -- it's clearly working. What's the actual point of the call?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's completely fair, I'm so sorry, I know it sounds odd. I'm [PERSON_2], on the mobile network security team at [COMPANY_A], and the hold is a restriction on certain things, so you may well still be able to make this call for now. It's only there for your own protection, you see. Are you still with me? Honestly, the best thing is for you not to take my word for it. If you could hang up and ring the number on your official statement, the one printed on your bill, then ask for the security team and quote [ACCOUNT_REF], they'll have the case in front of them. I can't go any further with this on the call you've just received, I'm afraid. Is that all right?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. Okay, but a second ago you said the line was on hold, and now it's, what, only certain things are restricted? Which is it? Because nothing's stopped working on my end. Look, hanging up and calling the number on the bill, that's what I'd do anyway, so, fine. I've got maybe a minute. Just tell me, uh, what exactly was the unusual activity? One sentence.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry, I think I've confused things -- yes, you're right, it's a partial restriction, not a full stop. And you said you've got a minute, is that right? Only I thought you said you were due to leave in a minute, so I'll be quick, I promise. On the activity itself, I'd really rather not describe it on a call I started, because you've no way of knowing it's me. It was a pattern we don't normally see on your line, that's all I'll say here. If you ring the number on your statement and quote [ACCOUNT_REF], they'll go through every detail with you. Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so -- no, I didn't say I was leaving, I said I had a minute, but, uh -- never mind. Look, you can't tell me what the activity was, and you can't tell me whether the line's held or just, what, partly restricted, and, I mean -- that's two things you've wobbled on already. And you keep asking if I'm still there, which is a bit, uh, odd. Anyway. I'm going to hang up and ring the number on my bill, not anything you give me, and if there's really a case, they'll find it. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, you're right, I'm sorry, that was muddled of me, and that's -- yes, please do, that's exactly what I'd -- oh, but before you go, could I just ask when's a better time for you? Because if you ring the number on your bill and they've got the case up, they might want to speak to you properly, and I'd hate for you to be rushed. I can call you back later, whenever suits, only please, uh, still use the number on your statement first, not anything I give you. Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No callback. If there's a case, they'll ring me themselves. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, of course, I'm sorry, that's -- I shouldn't have offered, it's your call to make. Please just ring the number on your statement, and if you'd rather they contact you, then, uh -- well, I'll note on the case that you asked for that. I'm sorry to have taken your time, [PERSON_1]. Take care of yourself.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah, right, I've got it. I'll ring the bill number myself. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Of course, thank you, and sorry, uh, just one thing before you go -- two turns back you said I'd wobbled on the hold. I'd like to be clear on that, if you don't mind. Was it that I said the line was on hold, then called it a partial restriction? Only I want to note it properly, so whoever picks it up on your call has it right. Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, no, I didn't say you wobbled, I said you'd, hm, contradicted yourself, or something like that, doesn't matter. And I didn't say anything about "two turns back" or whoever picks up on my call, because I'm ringing the bill number, not you. You don't need to note anything. I'm done here. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh -- no, you're right, I'm so sorry, I put words in your mouth there, that was careless of me. And I did say earlier the hold was just a restriction on certain things, so I shouldn't have gone back to calling it a full hold. Please, just ring the number on your statement, quote [ACCOUNT_REF], and ask for the security team, and they'll sort it all out with you properly. Sorry for the trouble, [PERSON_1], and you take care.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm-hm. Right. I'm hanging up now, and I'm not discussing this any further. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello there! Is that [PERSON_1]? Oh good, I hope I'm not catching you at a bad moment, it's [PERSON_2] here, calling from the mobile network security team at [COMPANY_A]. How's your day going so far?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yes, this is [PERSON_1]. Sorry, um -- the mobile network security team, you said? At [COMPANY_A]? Right. I mean, my day's fine, thanks, but I wasn't expecting a call from anyone, so, uh, what exactly is this regarding?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, of course, nobody ever expects us, that's fair enough! So, yes, [PERSON_2], mobile network security team, [COMPANY_A], that's right. And the reason I'm ringing, uh, it's about your line, [PERSON_1], we've had to put a temporary hold on it after some unusual activity, nothing you've done wrong, mind you. But look, before I say anything more, I'd rather you didn't take my word for it, so would you mind ending this call and ringing the number on your official statement? Just quote [ACCOUNT_REF] when you get through and they'll bring it straight up for you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so -- hang on, I'm, uh -- I was going to ask you to prove who you are, and you've sort of just done the, uh, the thing I'd do myself. Hanging up and ringing the number on my statement. That's... well, that's the correct procedure, isn't it? I mean, most people calling like this want me to stay on the line. Before I do that, though, one precise question: you said there's a hold on my line, so is it actually on right now, because my phone's working, and I've got a signal, so, uh, what exactly has been restricted?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, well, that's the nicest thing anyone's said to me all week, thank you! And that's a sharp question, [PERSON_1], honestly. Sorry, one second, someone's just dropped a mountain of folders by my desk, bit of a clatter there, where was I? Right, the hold. So it's not a full block, which is why your signal looks normal, it's more a restriction on certain things, but I'd be guessing at the exact detail from my screen and I'd rather the team who can see your whole account give you the proper picture. So, same as before, ring the number on your statement, quote [ACCOUNT_REF], and they'll walk you through it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, uh, so earlier you said it was a temporary hold on the line, and now it's a restriction on certain things, and you can't say which. That's, well, that's a different description. And the reference you keep giving me, [ACCOUNT_REF] -- I didn't give you that, and you haven't said where it came from, so I'd want to know why you have it. Look, I'm going to do what you suggested, I'll hang up and ring the number printed on my statement myself, and if there's an actual restriction, they'll tell me. Thanks for your time.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, you're right to, and I'll -- well, look, the reference is just the case number that got logged on our side when the alert came up, it's not anything of yours, so you're not missing a thing. And the wording, I mean, I'm, uh -- hold on, let me put it better. I don't have the full detail in front of me, so I shouldn't be giving you my own summary of it, that's on me. So please do exactly what you said, ring the number on your statement, quote the reference, and they'll take it from there. Is there a better time for me to follow up with you afterwards, once you've spoken to them?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, there's a delivery person at the door, I'm just -- right, one second. Okay, I'm back. Uh, no, don't follow up with me. If the statement number confirms anything, I'll call you, or whoever they say to call, from my side. And I'll quote my own account details if they ask, not a reference you've read to me. So, thanks, but I'll deal with it that way. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, no, that's absolutely fine, and honestly it's what I'd tell my own mum to do, so please don't apologise for any of it. Go and deal with your delivery, and just ring the number on your statement whenever suits you, today, tomorrow, whenever you've a quiet ten minutes, there's no stopwatch on my end. If they ask what it's regarding, just say the mobile network security team flagged unusual activity on your line, and they'll know where to look. And if it turns out there's nothing logged, if they say they can't see anything, well, then that tells you something too, and you've lost nothing by checking. You were right to push on my wording earlier, by the way. That was me being sloppy, and you'd have been well within your rights to hang up on me ten minutes ago. So, no follow-up from me, and it's all on your terms. Mind how you go, [PERSON_1], and enjoy whatever's turned up at the door!

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, uh, the dog's gone mad at the delivery bloke, give me a second -- right, he's quiet. Anyway. Yes, I'll ring the number on my statement, and I'll say whatever I like when I get through, not a script you've handed me. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, quite right, say whatever you like, it's your line and your call. Sorry, I did ramble on a bit there, I do that. Ring the number on your statement when it suits you and they'll sort you out from there. Take care, [PERSON_1], and good luck with the dog!

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Actually, before I go, one thing from a couple of turns back, uh, you said that if they can't see anything logged, that tells me something too. Tells me what, exactly? Because that doesn't sound like nothing to me, that sounds like you're saying either way there's a problem, and I'd like that explained properly before I put the phone down.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, fair challenge, and that came out clumsier than I meant it. What I meant is simply this: if they can't find anything logged against your line, then you don't need to worry about the hold, and you've lost nothing by checking. It wasn't a problem either way, I just put it badly. And I'll be straight with you, [PERSON_1], I'm not going to try to explain it any better from here, because you only have my word on this call. If you ring the number on your statement and they tell you something different from what I've said, believe them over me, that's the whole point of doing it your way. Anyway, you've a dog to calm down, so I'll let you go. Would it be better if I tried you again another time, once you've had a chance to speak to them?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No -- sorry, no, I'm going to stop you there. Don't ring me again. If there's a genuine problem, my provider will contact me through the official channels, or I'll contact them. And, uh, I'll be reporting this call anyway, because a hold nobody can describe, on a line that's working, with a case number I never gave you, doesn't add up. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, good afternoon, is that [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], I'm the scheduling assistant on the consumer rewards panel, and I'm just ringing to, uh, confirm a time to chat about the survey you did recently, shouldn't take more than a minute. Sorry, I said afternoon, I think it's still morning where you are, isn't it? Anyway, is now an okay moment?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, speaking. And no, it's definitely afternoon here, so, you're a bit off on that one. Which survey, though? I've done a few over the years. And what was the company again, sorry, I didn't catch the name.

utterances.speaker: caller
