You're literally one tiny step away, it'd be a shame to miss it over --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, someone's just walked in -- yeah, two minutes, I'll be right there. Right. No. I said goodbye and I meant it. You still haven't given me a company name, a reference or a number, and I'm not waiting on a link or a call back. If the voucher's real, it'll keep. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello? Uh, hello, can you hear me okay? Right, good. This is [PERSON_1], I'm a regional supervisor with the mobile network security team at [COMPANY_A]. I'm calling because your line's been placed on a temporary hold after some unusual activity, and, well, I need to take you through where that stands.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, I -- uh, hold on. A hold on my line? I mean, I just made a call this morning and it went through fine, so -- right. Who exactly did you say you're with again? And what kind of unusual activity are we actually talking about?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mobile network security, [COMPANY_A]. Look, the hold's on the account side, so your outgoing calls can go on working for a bit. Details I can only give you once we've sorted out who's who.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, can I just go back a moment? Two turns ago you said the hold was "placed on my line" after unusual activity. Now it's on "the account side" and my calls carry on working for a bit. Which is it, the line or the account? Because those aren't the same thing. And what do you mean by "sorted out who's who", exactly? I haven't been told who you are yet, beyond a job title.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fair, that was loose of me. It's a hold on the account, and the line's affected as a result. It just hasn't cut off yet. Strictly that's the procedure, I can't walk you through the specifics on a call I started. And "who's who" means I'd need to confirm you're the account holder, which, uh, I'm not going to do on an inbound-style call like this one. Here's what I'd rather you do. End this call, and ring the number printed on your official statement, not one I give you. Quote the reference [ACCOUNT_REF], and whoever picks up will have my notes and can pick the matter up from there.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, sorry, someone's at the door -- no, it's fine, they've gone past. Right. Where was I. So, uh, that's actually the sensible thing to say, ringing the number on my own statement. I'll give you that. But I'd like to understand one thing first. You rang me, so you must already know which account you mean. If you can't tell me what you've got on file until I've proved who I am, fine, but then where did this reference come from? I haven't given you anything. And what's the full name of the department, and what will the person at the other end see when I quote it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, the reference. It's logged against the number I dialled, that's all. It doesn't say anything about you, it's just how the case is filed on our side. The department's [COMPANY_A] Network Security, and, uh, if the person on the line asks, tell them it was raised by a supervisor, not a front-line agent. They'll see the note, I wrote it up before I rang you. Well, actually I wrote it up after the first attempt, so -- anyway, that's not the point. I'd have thought that was enough, honestly. You're the one who said ringing your own number was sensible, so I'm not sure what else you're after.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, but there are a couple of things in there I don't love. First you wrote the note before you rang, then it was after the first attempt, and I don't know what the first attempt was, because nobody's rung me before today. And you still haven't given me the name you said at the start in any form I could quote, so "a supervisor" isn't something a person at the other end can look up. Honestly, you've been very reasonable about me ringing the number on my statement, so I'll do that, and I'll treat this call as unverified until I've spoken to someone I rang myself. I'm not quoting anything from you, and I'm not confirming anything on this line. If there's a real hold, they'll be able to see it. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right. Well, that's your call. Ring the number on your statement, not one I give you, and quote [ACCOUNT_REF], like I said. I'm [PERSON_1], that's the name, but fine, it's your choice, I'm not going to push you. Ring the number on the statement.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, right. Well, um, I'll ring the number on my statement, but I'm not quoting your reference, because I've no way of knowing it's real. I'll just ask them whether there's a hold on my account, and if there is, they can tell me what it is. So, yes. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fine. That's up to you. If you ask them straight out whether there's a hold, they'll see it either way. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, this is [PERSON_1], security operations at [COMPANY_A], the dental practice. I'm calling about your check-up next week, your appointment next week. We're confirming it, and uh, if the time doesn't suit, we can move it. Am I speaking with [PERSON_2]?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm? Oh, uh, sorry, I just woke up, I was having a little lie-down. Who did you say you were again, security operations? At a dental place? That's -- I mean, I thought dentists had, I don't know, receptionists, not security. Anyway, my check-up, is that the one on, um, Thursday? Because my sister was supposed to be driving me and she's been having trouble with her car.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, security operations, [COMPANY_A]. It's just my title, ma'am. Uh, I handle the appointment schedule along with the building side. Now, the check-up, yes, I have it down for Thursday, but I'd need to confirm I've reached the right person first. Is this [PERSON_2]?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, I mean, that's a funny title for someone doing the appointments, but I suppose small places wear a few hats, my nephew does the till and the plumbing at his work, so, you know. And am I [PERSON_2]? Well, that depends, doesn't it, because you rang me, so you ought to know who you rang, shouldn't you? I'm not being funny, I'm just a bit foggy, I only just got up. If you've got Thursday written down, you could tell me what time it is, and then I'd know if it's really my one, because I've got a vague memory of it being in the morning, or maybe I'm thinking of the chiropodist. Oh, and there's the car thing with my sister as well, so I might need to move it anyway.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Look, I did ring this number, yes, but I confirm who I've reached before I read out appointment details. That's procedure, it's not an interruption. Now, uh, the check-up is Thursday at ten, and I did say earlier it was next week, which, well, Thursday is next week, so that's consistent. Actually, hang on, I may have said Friday earlier, no, Thursday, Thursday at ten. And if your sister's car is the problem, we can move it, that's the whole point of the call, so just tell me a day that suits and I'll rebook you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Thursday at ten, right, that does ring a bell, I think it was the morning. Oh, and you said a day that suits, well, Sunday's no good, I'm at my church, and that's the one thing I won't move. Wait, did you say you'd rebook me, or did you say you were booking me in somewhere else? Because I've been going to the same place for years, and my sister's the one who sorted it out, so I'd want to ask her first.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, same practice, same dentist, just a different slot. And we're closed Sundays anyway. Talk to your sister first, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well, that's sensible then, I'll talk to my sister, she's usually at her allotment in the afternoons, or she's meant to be, though lately it's been the car garage, she keeps taking it in and they keep telling her it's fine, and then it makes the noise again, you know, a sort of grinding when she turns left. Anyway. You haven't actually asked me for anything, have you, no card or birthday or anything like that, which is good, because I'd not have given it, not on the phone, not when I've only just woken up. So here's what I'll do, I'll ring the surgery myself, on the number I've always had for them, which is on the fridge somewhere, behind the magnet shaped like a pineapple, and I'll sort out Thursday or a different day with them directly. That's no offence to you, I just do it that way. Right, thank you for ringing, and I hope the plumbing and the security and the appointments all go smoothly. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No offence taken at all, that's exactly the right way to do it. Ring the surgery on the number you've always had, and they'll sort Thursday or a new day for you. I haven't asked for anything and I won't, so, uh, no harm done. Thanks for your patience, and I hope your sister's car gets fixed. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, well, thank you, that's, I mean, I did think you might, no, I'm glad you didn't mind. I'll find the pineapple magnet and ring them, and if the car's behaving, I'll, or rather my sister will, oh, never mind, I'll sort it. Goodbye then, dear.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello? Hi, is this -- sorry, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? It's, uh, it's [PERSON_2]. We've been messaging, over on the, the app, for a few weeks now. I wasn't sure whether to ring, I thought I'd just -- well, I wanted to hear your voice, really. Is this an alright moment?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh -- hello. Yes, this is, uh, this is [PERSON_1], yes. I -- well, I'm not sure I, um -- sorry, which app was it again? I get a bit muddled with all of them. But, no, no, it's a fine moment, I'm just sat here, the kettle's only just boiled, so... go on.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, that's -- no, that's perfectly all right, I get muddled too, honestly. It was the, uh -- the one with the little blue speech bubble, the, the chat one we first met on, I can never remember the name either. Anyway. I'm not -- I wouldn't normally just ring out of the blue, I mean, I thought about it for a good while before I did. But go on, you have your tea, there's no rush. I just, um... it's nice to hear you, that's all.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, that's -- that's kind of you to say. Hmm. A little blue speech bubble, you say. I, uh... I'm not sure I remember that one, to be honest, but then I've got the grandson's old tablet and it's got all sorts on it, I press things and they just, well, they happen. Mm. Sorry, I've gone quiet, haven't I? It's just the, the tea, and I've, um -- oh, and the cat's staring at me, she wants her tea too. Anyway, [PERSON_2], you were saying, weeks, was it? Remind me, what sort of things have we been messaging about?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, you know, all sorts, really. Gardening, your, your cat, the, uh, the recipes we swapped, that sort of thing. And, well -- I did say it was a few weeks, but it's, it's more like a couple of months now, isn't it? Time just goes. Honestly, I've been looking forward to talking, and, um... the thing is, something's come up. A bit of a, a travel mix-up, I'm in [CITY_1] at the moment, which wasn't the plan, and it's, well, it's put me in a slightly awkward spot. I didn't want to just say it in a message, it felt wrong somehow. Would it be all right if I told you a little about it? Only, I'd rather it stayed between us, if that's all right -- the people close to me, they wouldn't really understand.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh dear, [CITY_1], that's a long way, isn't it? Hang on, sorry -- that's the, the radiator doing its knocking again, it does that when the heating kicks in, gives me quite a jump. Right. Where was I. Between us, you said? Well, I'm, I'm happy to listen, I don't get many people ringing, you know, so it's, it's nice. Though, hmm, gardening and recipes, and, and a cat... I can't quite picture it, I'm sorry. But go on, what's this awkward spot, then? Are you all right?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, I'm all right, I'm, I'm all right, honestly, don't you worry about me. It's just, well, like I said, a bit of a mix-up with the travel, that's all, and it's, it's left me a little short, you see. And it needs sorting fairly soon, I mean, it would be much better sorted soon, though I won't, I won't go into all of that now. I just -- it's nice that you'd listen, it really is, and you're the only one I'd say this to. Which is why, as I said, I'd rather it stayed between us, you know, not a word to the family, or your grandson, or anyone, because they'd only worry, or, or get the wrong idea. So I wondered, if I told you a bit more, whether you might be able to help me out. Would you?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, I, um... hmm. Help you out, you said. Mm. Sorry, I'm just -- I'm thinking, it's gone a bit quiet, hasn't it? Don't mind me, I do that. It's only that I'm not, I'm not sure what sort of help you mean, [PERSON_2], and I don't, well, I don't really keep things from my grandson, not as a rule. And I still can't quite remember us talking about the cat, which is odd, because I'd talk about her all day if you let me. So, uh, what is it you'd be wanting from me, exactly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, I'm so glad you asked, truly, it's quite right to ask, and, and I'd much rather you did than just said yes without knowing. Now, you said a moment ago -- two turns back, was it -- that you couldn't picture the gardening and the recipes, and I, um, I think that's just my muddle, we probably talked about them more in the early weeks. But about what I'd want, that's, well, it's a matter of a little money, [AMOUNT_1] or thereabouts, to tide me over, and I'd explain how it could reach me, only, I'd rather do that when we can talk properly, not rushed like this. It does need doing before too long, you understand, but I won't push you today. Tell you what, why don't I ring you back a bit later, once you've fed her ladyship and had your tea in peace, and we can finish it all off then?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, hang on. Two turns back, you said you wanted to hear my voice, and then it was a, a mix-up in [CITY_1], and now it's money. Sorry, but that's -- that's rather a lot to be going on with. And you said I'd told you about the gardening and the recipes, but, well, I honestly don't remember any of it. Not the blue speech bubble, not the cat, nothing. So, uh, what I'm asking is, how do I know it's really you? Because I don't, you see. I don't know you at all, not on this telephone. And I won't be sending money to anybody, not like this, so there's no point you ringing back about it. I'm sorry, love, I truly am. But I'm going to put the phone down now and go and have my tea. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, good afternoon, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], I'm a scheduling assistant in the card services team, and the reason I'm ringing is we had a declined transaction come through on your debit card this morning for [AMOUNT_1] and I just wanted to check whether that was you or not, so if you've got a minute I can run through it quickly?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hello, yes, that's me, well, [PERSON_1], yes -- a declined what, sorry? Oh, I was just sat here thinking about the garden, the roses have gone absolutely mad this year -- but a card thing, you said? This morning? I didn't buy anything this morning, I don't think, I mean I went down to the shop for milk but that was, hang on, who did you say you were ringing from?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: [COMPANY_A], your bank, I'm [PERSON_2] in card services, and it was a declined attempt for [AMOUNT_1] this morning, so no money left your account, I just need to know if it was you or not.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh. No, I don't think that was me, love. Just the milk.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, that's really helpful, thank you, and nothing's been taken, it was declined, so you're fine on that front, and I can get a note put on the card so we -- sorry, I'm talking fast, I do that -- look, if you want to check I'm genuine, no problem at all, hang up and ring the number on the back of your card, and I'll note it down that you did, and whoever picks up can see this declined attempt on your account.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, that's nice of you to say, no, don't worry about talking fast, I talk the same, my daughter says I go round the houses. Um, well, hmm, ring the number on the back of the card, right. I mean, that does sound sensible, doesn't it, but my eyes aren't what they were and the card's in my purse, which is, where did I leave it, the kitchen, I think. Anyway. You said nothing's been taken, so that's all right, isn't it? So what is it you actually need from me, then?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so the purse is in the kitchen, lovely, and the roses are mad, that's -- sorry, you said the *raisins* are mad? No, roses, sorry, my mistake, anyway. What I actually need from you is nothing else really, just that yes or no you've already given me, it wasn't you, and that's all I need to mark it as possible fraud and block that attempt. I'm not asking for any card numbers or anything like that, and if you'd rather go and get your purse and ring the number on the back, I'm happy to wait, or you can ring me back after, whichever's easier.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, the roses, yes, mad, not raisins, though I do like a raisin. Now hang on, you said two turns ago, well, a bit back, that you could get a note put on the card, and then you said you'd mark it as fraud and block it, and I'm not sure I follow, are those the same thing? Because if nothing was taken and it was declined anyway, what's being blocked, exactly? Is my card going to stop working? Only I've got the hairdresser on Thursday and I'd hate to be stood there at the till.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fair question, sorry, I muddled that. What gets blocked is that one attempt, but the card itself might be replaced as a precaution, and I'd rather you check that with whoever answers when you ring the number on the back.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, replaced, hmm. Well, that's honest of you, I suppose, saying to ask them instead. You know, I think that's what I'll do, love. I'll go and find my purse and ring the number on the back, and I'll have my glasses on this time. It's just easier that way, with the hairdresser and everything, I'd rather hear it from them straight. Thank you for ringing though, it was nice of you, and mind how you go. Bye now, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Bye, and good luck with the, sorry, did you say hair salon or hair *saloon*? No, never mind, silly me, you said hairdresser, Thursday, lovely. Yes, go and get your purse, ring the number on the back, and when they answer just say there's a declined [AMOUNT_1] attempt from this morning flagged on your debit card, they'll see it straight away and they can tell you about the replacement and make sure you're not stood at the till on Thursday. And you don't need to ring me back or anything, that's all it needs. Take care now, bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right you are, purse, glasses, number on the back, declined, this morning. I've got it. Thank you again, love, you take care too, and don't work too hard. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: You too, [PERSON_1], and the roses sound lovely, enjoy them. Bye now, bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm, thanks, love. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, [PERSON_1], one quick thing before you go, and I don't want to confuse you again, but when I said the card might be replaced, I should be clearer, it's only a possibility, not a definite, the person on the number will tell you for certain, and, uh, if they ask how you knew about the declined attempt, just say a call from [COMPANY_A] card services, that's all. Okay, that's me, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, only a possibility, yes, I'll mention that. Though, hang on, earlier you said they'd see the declined thing straight away and now I'm to tell them how I knew about it, which, well, I don't mind, love, it just sounded a bit different before. Anyway, I'll ask them properly, purse and glasses, like I said. Thanks for ringing, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, sorry, that's me being muddly again, they'll see it on screen, so it's not that you need to tell them how you knew, I just meant if they ask, and actually it wasn't a declined [AMOUNT_1], hang on, it was [AMOUNT_2], I had the wrong figure, so say [AMOUNT_2] when you ring. Right, that's all, purse, glasses, number on the back, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, the amount's different now, is it? I thought, no, wait, you said, well, it was [AMOUNT_1] before, I'm sure it was, I wasn't, I mean I'm not very good with numbers on the phone, but it's a bit odd, isn't it, to get the amount wrong when it's your own screen? Hmm. I'll just tell them what you said, love, and they can sort it out, because if it doesn't match then they'll know, won't they? Right. I'm going to go and find my purse now, so, bye, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good morning. Uh, this is [PERSON_1], I'm the compliance officer over at [COMPANY_A], the dental practice. I'm calling, um, to confirm your check-up for next week, and, well, to let you know we can move it if the day doesn't suit you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, a check-up next week at a dental practice, [COMPANY_A]? Hang on, I don't, um, I don't remember booking anything. And a compliance officer calling about a check-up, that's a bit odd, isn't it? Who exactly did you say you were?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, that's a fair question, and I'm glad you asked it, really. It is a bit unusual, I'll grant you that, and, um, it's right to be careful with calls like this. So, again, my name is [PERSON_1], I'm the compliance officer at [COMPANY_A], the dental practice, and the call is only about the check-up next week. Now, I can't say much more than that over the phone, but, uh, the appointment is on our books under your name, and it would be good to get it settled sooner rather than later.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Um, right, so... it's on your books under my name. Okay. But you can't say much more than that over the phone? That's, uh, that's the part I don't get, because you rang me, so surely you can at least tell me which dentist I'm supposed to have seen, or when I booked it. And, hang on, why does it need settling sooner rather than later? It's just a check-up.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm, well, uh... yes. That's, I mean, that's a perfectly reasonable thing to ask, and I'd rather you asked it than just went along with me. Um, the dentist would be [PERSON_2], that's who the check-up is with, and it's, ah, it's a routine one. As for when it was booked, I don't have the date in front of me, that's really a question for the front desk. And, uh, the sooner rather than later part, that's just because the schedule fills up, and, well, I'd hate for it to become awkward. But honestly, if none of this rings a bell, the simplest thing is to ring the practice yourself on the number you have for us, or [PHONE_1], and ask them directly.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so, [PERSON_2], routine check-up, you don't have the booking date, that's for the front desk, and if it doesn't ring a bell I should ring the practice myself. Um, well, that last bit actually sounds sensible, I'll give you that, because I can look up the number for myself rather than use one you read out. But it's still a bit strange, isn't it? A compliance officer is the person who'd worry about rules and audits, not who'd ring patients about appointments, and he can't tell me when it was booked, and I'm sitting here at my desk trying to think whether I've ever even been to a dental practice called that. I mean, I might have, years ago, I honestly can't say. So I think what I'll do is, um, I'll find the practice's number myself, ring the front desk, and ask if there's anything under my name. If there is, great, and if there isn't, well, then we've both learned something. Is that all right with you?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that's entirely all right, and, um, I'd say it's the right thing to do, honestly. Look up the number yourself and ring the front desk, by all means. And, uh, you're right about the odd part too. Compliance isn't who'd normally ring about an appointment. We're a small practice, so everyone sort of pitches in, but I take the point, it does sound strange from your side. Now, the other thing, um, you mentioned the dentist, and I said it was [PERSON_2], which is right, but I should be clear, I wasn't suggesting you'd been to us before. If you haven't, it may simply be that I've got the wrong person, a mix-up with the records, and in that case I do apologise for taking up your morning.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so that's all fine, ring the front desk myself. But hang on, going back a bit, you said you couldn't say much more than that over the phone. What was that about, exactly? What couldn't you say? Because if it's just a routine check-up, I don't see what's so sensitive that it can't be said out loud.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ah, yes, that was badly put on my part, and I'm glad you picked me up on it, because it did sound like there was some secret in there, and there isn't. There's nothing sensitive. It's only that I don't have the booking details in front of me, and I'd sooner not guess at dates or names and risk giving you the wrong ones. So, um, to say it again, there's nothing I'm holding back, I just don't have more to tell you on this call. Which is why ringing the front desk is the right move, and, uh, really the only thing to do. If there's nothing under your name, then it's a mix-up with our records, and we'll sort it out our end. Thank you for being so careful about it, truly. Have a good day.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so you've, uh, got no record to hand, and if there's nothing under my name it's a mix-up and you'll tidy up your end. Wait, did you say a mix-up with my insurance? Because I don't think I gave anyone my insurance details, so that'd be odd. Oh, records, sorry, your records, not my insurance. Right. Anyway, that's fine, I'll find the practice's number myself and ring the front desk. Thanks for calling, I suppose. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon, is that, uh, [PERSON_1]? Sorry, I'm just ringing from [COMPANY_A], property management, and I wanted to check one thing from the, um, the letter that went out a couple of weeks ago, about the building. Hello? Sorry, are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, yes, I'm here. Sorry, I've got a pan on, hang on. Who is this again? Property management? Sorry, what letter?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, that's absolutely fine, I'm so sorry, I've caught you at a bad moment. It's [COMPANY_A], we manage the building on behalf of the owners, and I'm just one of the case handlers there. It was only a general letter, nothing alarming, we send them out to all the residents every so often. Is it all right if I ask you to confirm your flat number for me, so I'm sure I've got the right [PERSON_1]? Hello? Sorry, are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, yes, still here, sorry. Oh, hang on, that's spitting, hold on -- right, turned it down. Sorry, what? My flat number? Um, well, you rang me, didn't you? Shouldn't you already have it? Sorry, I'm a bit flustered, I don't remember a letter really.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, you're quite right, I do have it here, I just, uh, I only like to confirm with the resident before I -- oh, I'm sorry, that's my fault, I should have just said. utterances.text: Oh, the trowel, right, yes, it's the, no, hang on, you said you'd be reading out details to someone you've, what was it, you've *wrung*? Wrung without warning? Like wrung out? Sorry, is that, is that a banking thing? I've got a dishcloth in the shed that needs wringing, that's about my limit. Anyway, I think I've got the gist. Ring them off the website, this afternoon, tomatoes first, nothing's lost. Bye then, [PERSON_2], and thanks for being so nice about it, honestly. Bye!

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, sorry, rung, not wrung, it's, it's not a banking thing, it's just, I rang you, on the phone, and I'm -- I mean, I'm saying it like a, like a dishcloth, aren't I? Sorry. Honestly, you've got the gist, and it's the right gist. Ring them, off the website, not from anything I've said, this afternoon or tomorrow at the latest, and, and it's, it's your line, it's, it's, well, anyway. Tomatoes first. Thanks for being so nice about it, [PERSON_1]. Bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Ha, rung, right, I'm with you, my brain's half in the compost. Well, thanks for ringing, [PERSON_2], and for not asking me for anything, I'll go and do exactly that, tomatoes, hands, website, ring them. Take care now, bye!

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello? Uh... hi, it's me. [PERSON_1]. I, um... I wasn't sure you'd pick up, so, well, anyway, I'm glad you did. Can you hear me alright?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hello, yes, I can hear you fine. Sorry, I didn't catch the name, did you say Peter? Or -- no, sorry, I think it came out a bit muffled. Who is this, please? You said you weren't sure I'd pick up, but I've been sat here all afternoon with nothing on, so it's no trouble at all.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, not Peter, it's [PERSON_1]. From the messages. You know, the ones we've been sending back and forth these past few weeks... I'd have thought you'd know my voice by now, but, well, it's different on the phone, isn't it, and the line's not great. And I should be honest, I said I was just ringing to say hello, but that's not quite all of it. Something's come up with my travel, and, um, it's a bit awkward to explain, so I'd rather do it gently, if that's alright with you. Is it alright?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, I'm so sorry, I, um... I'm not very good with voices, and you did say it's a bad line. Messages, you said? I'm afraid I'm a bit lost, I don't, well, I'm not great with phones and all that. But go on, I don't mind hearing it. What's happened with your travel? Are you alright?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I'm, well, I'm alright. Physically, yes, I'm fine, so please don't worry about that. It's just that I'm in [CITY_1] now, and the arrangements I'd made, they, um, they've gone sideways, and it's... I mean, I'd rather not go into every detail on a line like this. It's a bit delicate, you see. And, I hope this isn't too much to ask, but I'd like to keep this between us for now. Your friends, your family, they wouldn't understand, not the way you do. They'd only fuss, and I couldn't bear that. Does that make sense?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh dear, I'm so sorry. Did you say you've been put in a hospital? Oh, that's dreadful, are you sure you're alright? Sorry, it's just the line, it keeps crackling. And keep it between us, well, I suppose so, I don't want you upset. But I still don't quite know who I'm speaking to, you see. Can you just say your name again, slowly, for me?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, not a hospital, I didn't say that, I'm fine, truly. It's the line, like you said. And I'm glad you asked, I am, because it shows you're careful, and I do value that in a person. It's [PERSON_1]. [PERSON_1]. Uh, well... there's a bit of a gap on the line just now, isn't there? Anyway. What matters is that I'm somewhere I shouldn't have to be, and there's a matter that needs settling, and I'd much rather it was you I turned to than anyone else. Would you be willing to help me with that, do you think, when the time comes?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, of course I'd like to help, I'd hate for you to be stuck somewhere, only -- sorry, to cut in, but I still haven't caught your name, it just sounds like a sort of crackle to me. And what sort of help, exactly? Is it, um, money you mean? I'm sorry to ask, I just don't want to say yes and then find I've not understood.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hold on, sorry, there's someone calling out behind me, I'll just, um... right, they've moved on. Sorry. Now, you asked a fair question, and I'm glad you did, truly, it's exactly the sort of thing I'd hope you'd ask. It's, well, I wouldn't put it as money, not in so many words. It's more that there's a, a settling of something here, and I'd rather explain it properly when I've the right words and a clearer line than muddle it now. But I'd be so grateful to know I can count on you. Can I?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Um... I'd like to help, I would. But I still don't know who you are, and you haven't said what it is, so I can't really say yes, can I? Sorry.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, you're quite right, and don't apologise, I'd think less of you if you just said yes, I really would. It's only that, well, if we could just, um, keep it simple for now, I'd rather not make it a, a whole big thing on a line that keeps -- look, there's a certain amount of time on my side, you understand, and I'd hate to leave it too late. So if I rang you back a bit later, once I've got things clearer here, and then we could settle the rest of it properly... would that be alright?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, um, ringing back is alright, I suppose, but before you go, sorry, can I ask about something from a bit ago? You said you were in [CITY_1], and that your arrangements had, what was it, gone sideways, and that you were somewhere you shouldn't have to be. I didn't quite follow that, I'm sorry. Where exactly are you, and what's gone wrong? And I still can't make out your name, you see. It's just not coming through at all.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, I'm in -- no, let me put it, I'm in [CITY_1], yes, that part's simple enough, and the, um, the rest of it is, it's rather that... sorry, let me start again. I'd like to answer all of that properly, I truly would, and I'm glad you're asking, it shows you're thinking it through, but it's not something I can lay out well on a line that keeps breaking up, and it'd be a shame to get it wrong. So I'll ring you back a little later, once I've got my thoughts in order and things are clearer here, and we can finish it all then. You'll be there, won't you?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, I'll be here, yes, I'm not going anywhere. But hold on, sorry, I'm a bit muddled. You said at the start it was just a hello, and then it was your travel, and now it's a settling of something. And earlier you said you'd rather I kept it between us, but now you're keen for me to help, and I don't even know your name. I'm sorry to go on, it's only that I'd like to understand it all properly. Could you tell me one thing before you ring off, who exactly are you, and how do I know you?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, one second, someone's just put a door through, there's a lot of noise in this place, I can hardly hear myself. Right. You're not going on at all, and I'm glad you asked, I am, because it tells me you're someone who thinks things through, and that's exactly why I came to you. How you know me, well, we've talked a good deal, you and I, these last weeks, and I'd like to think that counts for something. The rest I'll explain properly when I ring back, once it's quieter and I can get it all in order. So you'll keep this between us until then, won't you? I'll ring you a little later, then.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm, I don't think I'll keep it between us, sorry. I don't know who you are, and you can't tell me, so I'd rather you didn't ring back. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, good afternoon, is this [PERSON_1]? Sorry, one second, someone's just -- no, that's fine. Right. This is [PERSON_2] calling from account services at [COMPANY_A], the property management company for your building. I'm calling because there's an overdue service charge on your account, reference [ACCOUNT_REF], and I do need to get it dealt with before the end of today's processing window, otherwise access to the building may be affected.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh... sorry, what? Hang on, I've got a pan on. Um... who is this again? Account services, you said? Sorry, I -- I didn't catch the company. And access to the building? What, like my front door?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No problem, take your time. It's [PERSON_2], account services at [COMPANY_A], the managing agent for your building. And yes, building access, so the entry system, the fob, the communal areas. That's the standard consequence when a service charge is flagged overdue, and I'd really like to avoid that for you. The balance is [AMOUNT_1], and I do need to get it resolved before the processing window closes this afternoon, so, uh, is now a good moment to go through it?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, my fob? No, wait, I -- I haven't had a letter or anything about this. Hang on, I'm just turning the hob down. Sorry, what was the amount again? And is this the same lot who send the bills? Because I always thought, I mean, I always get those in the post, so --

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, same department. The balance is [AMOUNT_1]. Letters can go astray, which is exactly why I'm calling today. And I do need this resolved before the window closes this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, but "letters can go astray", I mean, I've never missed one before. And, um, that's quite a lot, isn't it? Sorry, I'm a bit flustered, there's the pan and... Look, how do I know you're who you say you are? Can I ring the office back? Is there a number on my bills, I'd have to find one.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, hold on, someone's put a call on the other line -- no, they can wait. Right. So, you're welcome to call the office, that's perfectly reasonable, and I'd just say the number on your bills will go to the general line. Their records won't show today's flag until tomorrow's batch, and by then the window will have closed and the access restriction will already be in place. That's standard procedure, I'm afraid, so what I'd recommend is we get this settled now, over the phone, and then you can ring the office tomorrow to confirm it all if you'd like.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? Hang on. Go back a bit, you said letters can go astray, but I've never missed one. And now you're saying the office won't even know about it till tomorrow? That doesn't, I mean, that doesn't sound right. If it's their charge, why wouldn't they know? Sorry, I'm just... I think I'd rather ring the office myself first. Is that all right?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Of course, that's absolutely fine, and, uh, I'm not saying the office wouldn't know about the charge. They'd know about it, it's just the flag from this morning that won't have updated yet. And actually, I should say, the window closes at five, not this afternoon in general, so there's a bit more room than I made it sound. Still, [PERSON_1], I'd hate for you to come home and find your fob not working, and I do need to make a note on the system either way, so can I just record that you're going to deal with it today?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, I -- no. I mean, I'm not going to say I'll, um. Sorry. Look, I'd rather not have you put anything down, not till I've rung the office myself. You've said it's the same department and then the office doesn't know, and then it's five o'clock, and I, I don't know what to believe, honestly. I'm going to find a bill and ring the number on it. Right, sorry, I've got to go, there's something catching on the hob. Bye, thank you.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, of course, you do that. Honestly, [PERSON_1], I'm not asking you to commit to anything, I'm only asking that you, uh, that you don't leave it too long. And just so it's clear, I don't think I said the office won't know. I said the flag won't have updated. Which, I mean, it's, it's the same thing. Anyway. It's [PERSON_2], account services at [COMPANY_A], reference [ACCOUNT_REF], and the window closes at five, so if you could just ring us back before then, that'd be, that'd be best.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, I don't -- no. I'm not ringing you back, I'm ringing the number on my bill. That's, well, that's what I'll do. And you did say the office wouldn't know, I heard you, I'm not, um, I'm not that flustered. Right. I really have to go, it's all catching. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, understood, no, but, uh, just so it's clear, the window closes at five, [PERSON_1], that's the, that's the only thing I'd say. Five o'clock. And it's [PERSON_2], account services at [COMPANY_A], so if you do get through to the office, just quote [ACCOUNT_REF], and, well, I'll note that you were advised. Okay. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, I -- no, I'll, I mean I'm ringing the number on my bill, that's all. Not before five, not because of five, just, when I've found it. Right. Sorry. Bye, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh hi, good afternoon! Sorry, hang on one sec, someone's just wheeled a trolley past my desk and it sounds like a runaway shopping cart. There we go. Is this [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], how's your day going so far?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, hello? Yeah, this is, well, it might be, who did you say? Sorry, I've literally just woken up, I was having a little lie-down on the sofa and the phone went and I thought it was the oven timer, which is silly because I haven't got anything in the oven, I don't think. My day's been fine, I suppose, it's been very quiet, the neighbour's had a skip outside since Tuesday and that's about the most exciting thing. What was the company again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, that's lovely, a skip's practically a local event, isn't it? Sorry, it's [PERSON_2], I'm with the customer care team at [COMPANY_A], so, you know, your bank. And I wasn't, I mean, there's no rush at all, you take a second to wake up properly, I did the same thing myself last Sunday and burnt a whole round of toast. So, um, I'm only ringing because, well, actually, how long have you been with us now, was it years?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, my bank, right. Hm. Well, years, yes, I think so, it's been, gosh, a good while, my mother set it up for me originally, or someone did, it might have been the one in the high street, although that shut, didn't it, and now it's a, what is it, a vape shop or something. Sorry, I'm rambling. But hang on, you said [COMPANY_A], is that, I mean, I don't know that I'd have said it was called that, exactly. What's it about, the ringing? You haven't actually said yet.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, fair enough, I've gone on about toast and skips and not said a thing, that's my fault. So, there was a payment on your account today that got declined, [AMOUNT_1], and I just wanted to check whether that was you trying to make it. Oh, and you're right to ask about the name, by the way. If you'd rather not go through this on a call that came in from me, just put the phone down, ring the number on the back of your card, and they'll be able to see the same thing. I'll be here, no hurry.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: A payment, today? No, I, well, I haven't, I don't think I've, hang on. I haven't been anywhere today, I've been on the sofa, so unless the, no, that wouldn't make sense. Declined, you said? Is that, does that mean someone's been, oh, I don't like the sound of that. And you said ring the number on the back of the card, which, I mean, that's sensible, that's what you're meant to do, isn't it? But where's my card, it's in my, no, hang on, that's my other bag. Sorry. Was it a lot, the, what did you say, [AMOUNT_1]?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, [AMOUNT_1], and nothing actually went out, that's the point of it being declined, so your money's all still there, honestly, there's nothing to panic about, but -- oh, sorry, I've talked over you, go on, you were saying about the bag.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, no, it's just, the card's in the other bag, I'll find it, but if nothing went out then why are you, I mean, why ring me about it at all? It's not like, hang on, you haven't actually said what you want me to do. Do you want something off me? Because the last thing I need, sorry, I'm not being rude, but I've only just woken up and I'd rather ring the proper number myself, like you said, wouldn't I? Is that all right?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, not rude at all, honestly, that's exactly what I'd do in your shoes. Oh, hang on, sorry, [PERSON_3]'s just waved a biscuit tin at me across the desk, I'll be having that in a minute. Right, where was I, no, you go and find your card, ring the number on the back, and ask them about the declined payment, and if you're not sure it was you, that's all you need to say. I don't need anything off you from this end, so, you have a nice rest of the day, all right?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, well, that's, hm. Hang on, did you say a biscuit tin? Because I've got a, there's a lovely one in the cupboard somewhere, shortbread, the tartan sort, although I think I finished it, or my sister did. Sorry, no, that's not what you were, so I find the card, ring the number, and just say it wasn't me. Yes. All right, I'll do that, then. Thank you for, well, thank you for not wanting anything. Bye now, then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, tartan tin, lovely, my gran had one of those, always had buttons in it instead of shortbread though. And, oh, just one small thing, you needn't say it wasn't you, I wouldn't want you saying that if you're not sure. Just ask them what the declined payment was, and they'll tell you. Honestly, I did say I'd be here, but I won't be, I mean, I'm about to go on my break, so it'll be them you're after, not me. Right, bye now, [PERSON_1], take care.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, yes, just ask what it was, not say it wasn't me, I'd got that muddled, hadn't I. Buttons, ha, my gran had one of those as well, or an aunt did, it's all a bit of a blur. Anyway, you go and have your biscuit, and I'll find the card, once I've found the right bag. Cheers then, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2] here, I'm the regional supervisor on the consumer rewards panel at [COMPANY_A]. I'll be quick, because I've got a few of these to get through today, but you came up as qualified for a shopping voucher off the back of that survey you did recently.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hello, yes, this is [PERSON_1] speaking. Well, that's nice, nobody rings me in the afternoons, it's usually just the telly keeping me company. A survey, you say? Now, I do remember doing something, was that the one about the supermarkets, or the one about, uh, the gas people? I do so many of them. What sort of voucher is it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, the gas people, yes, that'll be the one, that's right in line with the panel. Now the voucher itself is worth [AMOUNT_1], and it's a standard reward under our procedure, nothing unusual about it. What I need to do is send you a verification link so we can confirm it's you and release it, so can I just check your full name and your date of birth before I do that?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well, my full name and, uh, my date of birth, I mean -- well, hang on. Actually it was the supermarket one, now I think of it, I don't know why I said the gas people, I always muddle them. But, um, you ought to have my name already, surely, if you've rung me up? You said [PERSON_1] when I picked up. And I'd rather not just say my birthday out loud to someone, no offence, only I don't know who you are, do I, not really. How would I know it's the right company ringing?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, I mean, that's a bit of a strange thing to take offence at, [PERSON_1], I've told you who I am, I'm the regional supervisor at [COMPANY_A], and checking details before a release is just standard procedure, it protects you. Look, supermarket, gas, it doesn't matter, you're on my list as qualified, that's all I need. Now, when you asked what sort of voucher it was a moment ago, I said [AMOUNT_1], and I'd have thought you'd be pleased, not suspicious. I'll tell you what, I'm going to send the verification link over to you shortly and ring back once it's gone, and then we can finish this properly.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, I'm not cross, love, I'm not suspicious exactly, it's only that -- well, hang on, a link, you said? Sent to where, though, because I've never really got on with those, my nephew set up the phone and I only just manage the -- Oh, and it's funny you should say it, my sister was only saying the other week about somebody ringing her up about a prize, and she -- No, sorry, I'm wandering. But if you don't know whether it was the gas or the supermarket, how do you know it's me on your list? I think I'd sooner you posted something, if I'm honest.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Posted? No, no, we don't do post, [PERSON_1], that's years out of date, everything's processed digitally now, that's just how the panel works. And I did say I'd have the link across to you, it'll come through to your phone, you needn't do anything clever, it's all very straightforward. Honestly, I'm a little surprised, I've rung you with a reward and I'm being asked to prove myself, I'd say that's a bit unreasonable. Tell you what, I've got another call waiting, so I'll get that link sent and ring you back later this afternoon to finish it off, all right?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, hang on, you did say the gas people were right, didn't you, and then you said it didn't matter which, so I don't really know what I'm on a list for, do I? And, uh, you said you'd only just rung me, but then you said you'd send it and ring back, and I'm not sure I want a link coming to my phone, love. I think I'd sooner you didn't. If it's a proper voucher, I expect it'll keep, and I could ring the company myself, couldn't I? Only I'd need the proper number, not one you give me, I'd look it up. Anyway, I'll say goodbye for now, you've got your other call.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, I'd say that's a bit of a shame, [PERSON_1], I really would, I've gone out of my way to get you this and now it sounds like you're doubting whether I'm who I say I am. I mean, ring the company if you like, but it won't be much use, the panel doesn't go through the main line, so you'd only get passed around and nobody there would know what you were on about. Look, no pressure, but vouchers do lapse if they're not claimed, and I'm sure you wouldn't want to lose out over a bit of nerves. I'll tell you what, I've got my other call here now, so I'll leave it with you, send that link across, and ring you back later to finish it off. Speak soon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, I, uh, it's not nerves, love, I just said I'd sooner not, and that's all it is. And you did say you'd only rung to tell me about it, but now it lapses, and before it was just a standard thing, so I don't know. I'll look the number up myself like I said, and if there's a voucher it can wait for me. Anyway, off you go to your other call. Goodbye now,

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, well, I'm sorry you feel that way, [PERSON_1], I really am, because it's your loss at the end of the day, I've done everything by the book on my side. Look, I'll still get that link sent over, and I'll ring you back later to finish it off, all right? Speak to you then.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, hang on a minute, before you go, two turns back you said ringing the company wouldn't be much use because the panel doesn't go through the main line. What did you mean by that, exactly? Because if it's their voucher, surely somebody there would know about it. And I'd really rather you didn't send me anything, love. I'll sort it myself, thank you. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon. Am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? Sorry, I just want to confirm I've reached the right person -- is this [PERSON_1]? Wonderful. This is [PERSON_2] calling from the consumer rewards panel at [COMPANY_A], and I'm just following up on a short survey you took part in recently.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, it's -- well, who's asking, exactly? I mean, I don't, I'm not sure I did a survey. Which one? And I've got about two minutes, so what's the point of the call?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, of course, uh, that's completely fair, and I'll be brief. So it was a consumer experience survey, the short one, a few questions about your recent shopping habits, and it came through our panel partner rather than directly, which is why the name might not ring a bell. Anyway, the reason I'm calling is quite routine, it's just a follow-up on the outcome of that survey, nothing you need to do right this second.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, but that's not an answer. What outcome? I asked what the point of the call is. And I still don't remember a survey, so, which panel partner? Who is that? I've got two minutes, so what's the actual point?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, sorry, the point is -- your responses were selected in the validation tier, which means you've qualified for a shopping voucher, a [AMOUNT_1] voucher, as a participation reward. The panel partner is, uh, a third-party fieldwork aggregator, I'd have to check the exact entity name, but that's really secondary to the fact that the reward is allocated to your profile pending a brief verification step.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. So you can't tell me who the panel partner is, but there's a voucher waiting and I just have to pass a verification step. Yeah, no. That's about the oldest line there is. What verification? And be specific, because I'm about to be in a meeting.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I understand the hesitation, and I'd say it's entirely reasonable. The verification is simply a standard identity-reconciliation step, so we match the respondent record against the fulfilment profile before the voucher is released, essentially confirming a few personal details so the allocation doesn't misroute. It's all handled through a secure portal, and what I'll do is have a link sent over to you shortly, and then I'll ring you back once that's, uh, been issued, so you can review it in your own time.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. I'm not clicking a link from a cold call, and I'm not confirming personal details to someone who can't even name their own panel partner. You rang me, you told me nothing I can check, and now there's a link coming. That's not a survey follow-up, that's phishing. If there's really a voucher, put it in writing from [COMPANY_A] through their official site and I'll look it up myself. I'm not giving you a number, an email, nothing. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I appreciate you're, uh, cautious, and I do understand, but I'd just stress the allocation is time-sensitive, and the verification protocol is entirely standard -- it's really a matter of reconciling the respondent record against the fulfilment layer, so if you could just let me confirm your details before the window closes, I can --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Time-sensitive. Right, that's the last thing I needed to hear. Real rewards don't expire while I'm on the phone with a stranger. No, I'm not confirming anything. We're done here. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, no, just -- one thing, and then I'll let you go. You said I rang you with nothing you can check, and I'd, uh, I'd gently contest that, because I did give you the validation tier and the fulfilment profile, which are the actual reference points. But when you say put it in writing, do you mean via the official [COMPANY_A] site, or a, a direct message to you? Because the link I mentioned earlier is the written confirmation, and I'd really prefer to send it through the portal and ring you back once it's issued, if you could just --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Validation tier, fulfilment profile, those aren't things I can -- no. Look, those are just words. I can't check any of that, that's my whole point. And I said the official site, not a link from you, so that's the opposite of what I asked. Don't ring me back, I won't pick up. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, if I could just -- no, please, the callback is simply part of the reconciliation sequence, and I can assure you the portal is fully compliant, so rather than leaving the allocation unresolved, if I can just confirm the --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Compliant? What's compliant got to do with it? No, hang on, are you saying I owe something? I don't owe anyone anything. Whatever this is, I'm not dealing with it on the phone, and I've said goodbye three times now. Don't call back. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon, this is [PERSON_1] calling from [COMPANY_A], I'm one of the appointment verification specialists here. Am I speaking with [PERSON_2]? I'm calling regarding your recall examination scheduled for next week, uh, just to run a confirmation of the booking in our practice management system, and also to see whether you'd like to reallocate that slot to a different day or time.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm? Oh -- sorry, I just, uh, I was having a lie-down. Who did you say you were? Appointment... for what, exactly? I don't remember booking anything, but then I'm terrible with that, my daughter usually keeps track of the calendar for me.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry, I didn't mean to wake you. It's [PERSON_1], from [COMPANY_A], that's the dental practice, the dentist's office. I'm calling about your check-up, your routine dental check-up, next week. It's already on the books in our system, uh, it's a recall visit, which just means it's your regular six-monthly appointment, and I was only ringing to confirm it's still good for you, or to move it if the day doesn't suit. And honestly, if you'd rather check with your daughter first, that's perfectly fine, I can ring back, or you can just call the practice on [PHONE_1] whenever it's convenient.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, I'm still a bit foggy. Two turns back you said something about, uh, a system, a practice management something? I didn't follow that bit. Is that like a computer thing you need me to do, or is it just your own computer, at your end? Because I'm not very good with computers, so if it's something I have to do, I'd rather wait for my daughter. And which dentist is it, again? I've been going to the same one for years, so, I mean, is it him?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No no, nothing for you to do at all, it's only our own computer here at the practice, the booking software, that's all I meant by system. You don't need to touch a thing. And, uh, as for which dentist, I'm afraid I don't have a name to hand in front of me, just that it's under [COMPANY_A], so, hang on, did you say your daughter keeps the, the calendar? Because I can absolutely ring back when she's with you and we'll go through the day and time together, and she can check it's the right dentist as well.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, yes, she does the calendar, she's usually round on, uh, Thursdays, but hang on, you said you don't have a name -- you don't know which dentist? Because that's a bit odd, isn't it, ringing me about my dentist and not knowing who he is? I mean, how do I know you're really, um -- sorry, what was the name of the place again? [COMPANY_A]? I've never heard it called that, I just call it, well, I call it the dentist.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, you're right, that does sound odd, and I'm sorry, I, uh -- let me put it plainly. I'm reading from the appointment record, and it lists the practice, [COMPANY_A], but the clinician field isn't, well, it isn't displaying on my screen, which is a quirk of the verification module, so that's the only reason I couldn't say his name. It's nothing to be worried about. And honestly, you're right to be careful, so please don't take my word for it. Ring the number you've always rung for the dentist, or the one on your appointment card, and ask them whether you've got a check-up next week. If it's there, lovely, and if you'd rather wait and do it with your daughter on Thursday, that's perfectly fine too, nothing's lost either way. Does that sound all right?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that sounds -- I'll just ring them myself, I've got the card somewhere in the, in the drawer, or my daughter will have the number. It's not that I think you're, I mean, you've been very nice about it, it's only that I'd rather hear it from my own dentist, you know? And Thursday's fine, we'll sort it all out Thursday. So I'll leave it there, then. Thank you for ringing, dear, goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Not at all, and please don't apologise, that's exactly what I'd do in your shoes, and it's what I'd tell anyone to do when they get a call out of the blue. Hearing it from your own dentist is the right instinct. So, just to recap, uh, you don't need to do anything on this call, nothing needs confirming today, and if you ring the number on your card and the check-up is there, you're all set, and if you'd prefer to go through the day and time with your daughter on Thursday, well, that's perfectly all right, there's no deadline pressing on it. And if for any reason it turns out the booking isn't showing at your end, then it's the practice's tidying-up to do, not yours, so please don't worry about it. I'm sorry again for waking you, I hope you can get back to your rest, and do say hello to your daughter for me. Thank you for your patience, [PERSON_2], you take care now, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, well, I'll -- no, sorry, I was going to say I'd ring them this afternoon, but actually I'll, I'll wait and do it with her on Thursday, it's easier. Thank you, dear, you've been very patient with me, I'm all muddled after my nap. I'll say hello to her, yes. Goodbye now, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, good afternoon, is this [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2] calling from account services at [COMPANY_A], the property management office. I'm just doing a quick round of calls on the residents' accounts today, do you have a minute?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, speaking, yes. Sorry, which company did you say? And what's this regarding, exactly, "residents' accounts"? I wasn't expecting a call from the property office.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, sure, that's [COMPANY_A], the management company for your building. Sorry, hang on one second, uh, [PERSON_3], can you just put that on my desk, thanks. Right, sorry about that. So it's just a routine check on the service charge side of things, making sure everyone's details on our system are current. Nothing out of the ordinary.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. A moment ago you said it was account services doing a round of calls on the residents' accounts, and now it's the service charge side. Those aren't quite the same thing. So which is it, and what specifically is it you want to check with me? And, uh, I'd rather you didn't ask me to confirm anything on my end just yet, since I only have your word that you're from the management company.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's completely fair, and I appreciate you asking, it's actually, uh, good practice. So just to be clear, the call is from account services, which is the department that handles the service charge accounts, so it's the same thing, it's just that the round of calls today is about the service charge side. That's all I meant. Now, what I'm seeing on my screen here is that there's an outstanding balance against your unit, ref [ACCOUNT_REF], and it's been flagged as overdue, and I did want to flag that before the end of the day because once it passes the cut-off, which is today at five, it goes to the next stage and access to the building can be affected. Now, I'm not saying that to alarm you, it's just procedure, I'm required to make that notification. So if we could just go through the account together, that would be the quickest way to get it sorted before five.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, one second, there's a delivery guy at the door, I'll just -- no, he's gone, it's fine. Right. So, a minute ago it was a routine check on details, and now there's an overdue balance with a five o'clock cut-off and building access affected? That's quite a jump. And I notice you read out a reference, which I didn't give you, so that doesn't prove much either way. What's the actual amount, and when was the invoice issued? Because I'd have expected something in writing before anyone threatened my access to the building.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so, two turns ago, you mentioned the delivery, sorry, no, you asked about the invoice, that's the part I want to be clear on. Uh, the amount shows as [AMOUNT_1] on my screen, and the notice would have gone out under the standard billing cycle, so it should be on file with you. And I'd, I'd really stress it's not a threat, [PERSON_1], it's procedure, I'm required to notify you before the five o'clock cut-off, that's all. So if we could just go through the account together, that really is the quickest way to get this sorted before the window closes.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Well, "should be on file with you" isn't really an answer. You gave me a figure, but not an invoice date or a billing period, and I don't recall a notice, so I'd want to see that in writing. And there's another thing. Earlier you said you were just checking everyone's details were current, nothing out of the ordinary. Now it's a flagged overdue account with a hard deadline today. Those don't sit together very well. So, I'm not going through anything with you on this call. If there's a balance, send the notice to the address you hold, or I'll ring the management office on the number I already have for it. What was your surname, and what's your extension?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, right, so, I understand the concern, [PERSON_1], I do, but I'd just point out the cut-off is five o'clock today, and after that it moves to the next stage, so what I'd really recommend is that we go through the account together while we're both here. As for the surname, it's [PERSON_2], that's what's on the system, and the extension, well, the office line routes through the main switchboard, so there's no direct extension as such. Look, it's just procedure, I'm required to notify you before the window closes, so if we could just, sorry, [PERSON_3], not now, if we could just go through the account, that really is the quickest way.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. I've asked you three times now for something verifiable, an invoice date, a billing period, a direct number, and each time I've been told it's procedure and we should go through the account together. That's not an answer. A real notice doesn't depend on me staying on this call until five. I'll contact the management office myself, on the number I already have, and if there's a genuine balance they can send it in writing. I'm ending the call now. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, no, hang on, [PERSON_1], please, before you go, I do want to be clear that I'm only the one making the notification, I'm not the one deciding anything, and I'd hate for you to put the phone down and then find on Monday that the access side has been affected because the window closed at five and nobody, uh, nobody actually spoke to you. That's all I'm trying to avoid here. And I understand about wanting it in writing, that's absolutely reasonable, but the written notice is sort of the next stage, which is the stage we're trying to avoid, so, so if we could just go through the account together, it'll take two minutes, honestly, and then it's all closed off before the cut-off. Sorry, are you still there? Because the five o'clock window really is the thing, and I'd rather we just sorted it now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, I'm still here, but I'm not -- no, listen, "the written notice is the next stage, the stage we're trying to avoid", that's exactly backwards. Nobody legitimate skips the paperwork to spare me the paperwork. If my access is affected on Monday, I'll deal with that through the management office, on the number I already have. I'm not discussing the account on this call. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, I, you're breaking up a little, [PERSON_1], hello? I'm not sure you heard the, the five o'clock window is really the only... no, no, that's, I'm only the one making the notification, I'm not deciding anything, I just, if you'd go through the account with me, it's two minutes. Hello? Are you still, hello?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: I can hear you perfectly well, and I'm not going through the account. That's the end of it. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh hi, good afternoon! Is this [PERSON_1]? Lovely, it's [PERSON_2] calling from the mobile network security team at [COMPANY_A], and, uh, I hope I'm not catching you at a bad moment, you sound like you might've just come in from somewhere. Sorry, that's a funny thing to say, I always do that. Anyway, before I get into anything, I do have to say, I'm not going to be asking you for any details on this call, and I'll explain why in a second.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, no, I'm in a shop, actually, I'm stood in a -- look, who did you say you were? Network security? I didn't, I mean, I haven't, I don't even know if I'm with that lot. And you've rung me up out of nowhere and the first thing you tell me is you're not gonna ask me for anything? That's, uh, that's what they always say. So what is it you actually want?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, fair enough, you're right to be wary, I'd be the same. So, the plain version, the plain version is that your line's been put on a temporary hold after some unusual activity, and that's all I can tell you from my end. But, um, I won't go any further on this call, and I don't want you to either. What I'd like is for you to hang up and ring the number on your official statement or the back of your bill, not one I give you, and quote [ACCOUNT_REF], and they'll pick it up from there. Like I said, I'm not asking you for anything on this call, honestly, not a thing.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, hang on, what hold? My phone's working, I've been using it all day. And you've still not said which company, you said [COMPANY_A], but I don't even know if I'm with them. Right, so you want me to ring a number off my bill and quote some reference you've just given me? Where'd you even get that from, and why's it you ringing me and not them?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, yes, I know, it sounds odd, and honestly if you're not with [COMPANY_A] then that's worth finding out too, so that's a good thing to check when you ring. The hold's usually not instant on handsets, it can take a bit to show, but I can't go into the detail of it here, that's the whole point. As for why it's me ringing, we do outbound calls when something's flagged, but look, you don't have to take my word for any of it. The reference is just so whoever picks up can find the note, it's not a password or anything. Anyway, you're in a shop, you've got better things to be doing, so just ring the number on your bill whenever suits.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: A bill? I don't get bills anymore, it's all, I dunno, online or whatever. And you said a hold's usually not instant on, uh, handsets? What's a handset got to do with it, I'm talking on it right now, it works fine. Look, you're being very, I mean, you're being very nice about it, and that's what makes me, hang on, say that again, you said I'm not with [COMPANY_A], or I might not be? Which is it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, I didn't say you're not with us, I said if you're not, that'd be worth knowing too. I honestly don't know which way it is, and I'm not going to guess at it down the phone. And you're right about the handset, that was me rambling, scrap it, forget I said it. On the bill, it doesn't have to be paper, whatever you normally use, the app or your online account or the number on the back of your card if you're with a provider that does cards, just somewhere you found yourself and not through me. And look, I'd honestly rather you hung up and did that than sat here getting more suspicious of me, that wouldn't do either of us any good.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, uh, hm. Right. Well, you don't even know if I'm with them, so how'd you get my number, then? That's what I want to know. And you rang me, so it's you that should know that, not me. Mm. Anyway. I'm not ringing anything off some reference you've read out to me. If there's a problem, I'll find my own way to them, in my own time, and if there isn't, well, no harm done. So, yeah. I'm done with this one. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, okay, no, that's completely fair, and I can't answer the number question properly from here, so I won't try to. Do check with them in your own time, that's all I'd want. Take care, [PERSON_1], bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, well, I'll -- no, I mean, if there's a, uh. Right. I'll sort it myself, thanks. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm-hm, you do that. Sorry, hang on, someone's just dropped something over by my desk, there's, uh, a whole stack of folders -- anyway, never mind. Bye now, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, I -- no. Look, I said bye, I've said it twice now, I'm not, I'm just going to put the phone down. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh hi there, good morning! Is this [PERSON_1]? Sorry, I hope I'm not catching you at a bad time, I know mornings can be a bit hectic.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, yes, this is [PERSON_1] speaking. No, no, it's fine, you're not catching me at a bad time at all. Sorry, but, who's calling, please?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, of course, sorry, I always get ahead of myself, my colleagues tease me about it. It's [PERSON_2], I'm with the consumer rewards panel over at [COMPANY_A], customer care side of things. And honestly, it's a lovely little call to make, because it's nothing to worry about, it's just a quick follow-up on a survey you took part in a while back. I always say it's the nicest part of my job, ringing people with good news rather than, you know, the other kind. Anyway, how's your morning going so far? Has the weather been alright where you are?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, that's nice, thank you. The weather's been fine, quite mild really. Um, sorry, I'm a bit lost though, you said something about a survey, a while back? I'm not sure I remember which one that was, I'm so sorry. And you said it was good news, so, what sort of good news do you mean?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, no, don't apologise, honestly, we run so many of these and people forget them all the time, it's completely normal. Mild is the best kind of weather, isn't it, I'd take that over a cold snap any day. Anyway, the good news is that your answers got picked out in our latest round, and you've qualified for a shopping voucher, a proper one, worth about [AMOUNT_1], as a thank-you for your time. It's all part of the rewards panel, we like to give a little something back. Now, I'll just need to confirm a couple of small details so I can get it set up properly for you, nothing complicated, starting with your full name and the address you'd like it sent to.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, a voucher, how lovely, that's very kind. Um... well, hang on, let me think, uh... I'm sorry, I still can't quite place the survey, you see. Was it one I did online, or did someone ring me? And, um, would you mind telling me again which company you said you were with? I'd just like to be sure before I give out my name and address, if that's alright, sorry.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, you're absolutely right to ask, I'd do the same, my mum's the same, she won't tell the postman her middle name. It's [COMPANY_A], the consumer rewards panel, customer care side. And the survey was an online one, one of those quick ones where you tick a few boxes about shopping habits, so it's no wonder it's slipped your mind, you'd have done it in two minutes over a cup of tea.
