Tell you what, I'll send you a little verification link by email in a moment, then you'll see it's all above board, and I'll ring you straight back once it's landed. Does that sound fair?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well, that's very thoughtful of you, thank you. Um... hmm, let me just think, uh... sorry, I'm not very good with emails, you see. I never know quite what to click on, and I'd be worried I'd do it wrong. Is there some other way I could check, like, could I ring [COMPANY_A] myself, maybe? Or would that be a silly thing to ask?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, not silly at all, though I'd say the link is honestly the easier route, it's one click and you're done, my nan manages it and she calls the computer the telly. Sorry, you were saying about the survey, when I said it was an online one, did you want me to go over which one it was again? Because I can tell you more about that, it was the shopping habits one, [CODE_1] on our system. Anyway, if you ring the main line you'll just end up in a queue with people who've never heard of the panel, they're a different department entirely, so it's much quicker if I just send the link and ring you straight back.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, I see, um... well, I'd rather, no, sorry, what I mean is, I'm not sure I like the sound of that, if it's all the same. It's just that, you said the main line wouldn't know about the panel, and, well, that does seem a bit odd, doesn't it? Sorry, I don't mean to be difficult, I'm just not very good with these things. Could you maybe just post the voucher letter to me, and then I'd know it was real?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, difficult? No, no, you're being sensible, truly. Now, a letter, I'm afraid we don't really do those, it's all done digitally now, it's, uh, only ever the link, that's the whole process. And sorry, I think I gave you the wrong end of the stick earlier, the main line isn't a different department, I just meant the queue's long, you'd be on hold ages. Oh, and the survey, it might've been a phone one rather than online, they blur together on my screen. Look, why don't I just send that link over and ring you right back, it takes two minutes.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, um, sorry, but now I'm a bit muddled, because first you said it was an online survey, and then you said the main line was a different department, and now it's maybe a phone one, and the main line's just a long queue. And I'm sorry, I'm not trying to catch you out, honestly, I'm just not very quick with these things and I like to understand what's what. It's only that you can't post a letter, and you can't tell me for sure how I took the survey, and you'd rather I didn't ring them myself, and, well, I don't think I'd feel right about clicking anything or giving out my name and address like that. I did say I was happy to help, and I really am, it's lovely of you to think of me, but I think I'd rather ring [COMPANY_A] myself, whatever the queue's like, and see what they say. I hope that's alright, and I'm sorry to have taken up your morning. Thank you for calling, and goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, oh, you haven't taken up my morning at all, honestly, I've enjoyed the chat. And you really don't need to apologise, it's all a bit of a muddle on my end too, I've got a stack of these today. Look, if you do ring the main line, it's probably worth keeping hold of the voucher reference, I'd say it's [CODE_1], just in case they can find it for you. Though, mm, I'd hate for you to sit on hold for nothing, so, if you like, I could still send that little link and ring you back in a minute, save you the trouble?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, no, thank you, but I'm quite all right, I'll just ring them myself. Um, and sorry, but earlier you did say a letter wasn't possible, and now you're saying it's just a long queue, and I think the survey was online and then it wasn't, so I really would rather check it with them directly. I won't be needing the link, thank you. It was kind of you to ring, though. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, fair enough, you do what feels right. Sorry, can I just check one thing before you go? Two turns back you said you'd rather ring them yourself, and I only meant I'd be sorry if you waited on hold for nothing, that's all. Which number were you going to use, if you don't mind my asking? I only ask so I can flag it on my side and make sure the right people are expecting you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, um, I'm not sure I'd like to say, sorry. I'd just look the number up myself, I wouldn't use one you gave me, you see. And, um, I thought you said earlier it was about a thing I'd done, a survey, but now you're saying I'll be, what was it, expected? Sorry, I don't quite follow. I think I'll just go and sort it myself, if that's alright. Thank you, goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, good afternoon, is that [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2] calling from the mobile network security team at [COMPANY_A], I'm a scheduling assistant, and I'm ringing because your line's been put on a temporary hold after some unusual activity, and I can't take this any further until you've rung the number on your official statement, uh, so if you could just do that and quote [ACCOUNT_REF] when you get through, that's all I need from you right now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, this is, uh -- sorry, the mobile network security team? And you're a scheduling assistant? That's, I mean, those two things don't really go together, do they. Hang on, so my line's on hold, but you're ringing me on it, which -- how's that working? Anyway, which company did you say you were with, exactly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, fair, that's a good catch, and I'm with [COMPANY_A], the mobile network security team, and I'm the one who books the callbacks, so my job's just to get you to the right desk, and the hold's on outgoing services and some account changes, not on this call coming in, but honestly, look, you shouldn't take my word for any of it, so I won't go any further on this call, I'd just ask you to hang up and ring the number on your official statement, not one I give you, and quote [ACCOUNT_REF] when you're through, and they'll pick it up from there.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, but you said the company name as a placeholder, like, I still don't actually know who you are. Which company? Say the name. And what unusual activity, specifically? You rang me, so you must have something in front of you. A date, a type of charge, anything. Because you're telling me to hang up and ring a number off my statement, which is, honestly, sensible, I'd do that anyway. I'm just asking what happened on the line. What was the unusual activity?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, I hear you, and that's exactly why I'm not going to run through the details on this call, because if you can't be sure it's me then anything I tell you is just a story, whereas whoever picks up at the number on your statement will have the actual flag in front of them, the activity, the dates, all of it, and that's where you'll get a proper answer, so if you could just hang up and ring that number and quote [ACCOUNT_REF], and --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, go back a second. Two turns ago you said the hold's on outgoing services and some account changes, but not on this call coming in. Which account changes? Like, what can't I do right now? Because that's a pretty specific thing to say if you've got nothing in front of you. And you still haven't told me the company name, by the way.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, so, that was loose of me, I shouldn't have gone into the hold at all, I don't actually have the breakdown in front of me, I just book the callbacks, so forget the outgoing bit, honestly the hold might cover more than that, I don't know, and that's exactly why it should come from the desk and not from me, and the company's [COMPANY_A], same as I said at the start, but don't just take my word for it, hang up, ring the number on your statement, quote [ACCOUNT_REF], and they'll tell you what's flagged.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Right. So -- uh -- you rang me with a flag you can't describe, a hold you can't explain, and a company name that keeps coming out as a placeholder, and the one thing you do want is for me to quote a reference. Which, fine, I'll ring the number on my statement. But I'll ring it because of this call, not for it. And I won't be quoting anything you've read out to me. If there's a real flag, they'll find it from my side. Okay. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, one sec, somebody's just -- yeah, no, I'm back. That's completely fine, honestly that's the right call, ring the number on your statement, the one you find yourself, and tell them what I told you, that you had a call about a hold on your line, and they'll take it from there. And if you'd rather not use the reference, that's up to you, they can find it from your side. Thanks for your time, [PERSON_1], bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, no, that's fine. I'll tell them exactly what you said, though, so the whole thing's on record, the scheduling assistant, the security team, the company name that never actually got said out loud, and the hold that you couldn't describe. And I'll find the number myself, off a statement I already have, not off anything from this call. If there's a real flag on the line, they'll sort it, and if there isn't, well, that tells me what this was. Anyway, I've got work to get back to. Cheers, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon. Am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? Uh, my name is [PERSON_2], and I'm a compliance officer with [COMPANY_A], your bank. I'm calling because a transaction on your account was declined earlier today, for [AMOUNT_1], and I wanted to ask whether that was you attempting it or not. Now, I realise a call like this, out of the blue, sounds exactly like the sort of thing you ought to be cautious about, so please, take whatever time you need, and I'll say right at the start that you're perfectly welcome to hang up and ring us back on the number printed on your card, I wouldn't mind in the least. It's just that, well, with these things, the longer a declined attempt sits unexplained, the less comfortable we are about it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, hang on, sorry, I'm at my desk, give me a second -- so, you're saying a transaction was declined, for [AMOUNT_1], on my account? Um. And you're from the bank, [COMPANY_A], right? I mean, I didn't try to buy anything today that I know of, but, uh... yeah, how do I know this is, you know, actually the bank?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Good question, and honestly the right one to ask. You don't, not from me alone. Hang up, ring the number on the back of your card, ask for the compliance team about the declined [AMOUNT_1], and I'll be here, or they'll find me. Take your time with it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so ring the number on the back of the card, ask for compliance. Yeah, okay. I'll do that, I'm at work right now anyway. Thanks, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, the number on the back of the card, not one I've given you, and, uh, as I said, ask for compliance, mention the declined [AMOUNT_1], and take as long as you need. I'm not going anywhere, and I won't ring you again unless you ask me to. Mm, just one small thing, if you're able to, sooner rather than later is better, but no rush, really. Goodbye for now, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so, yes, number on the back of the card, not one you've given me, ask for compliance, mention the declined [AMOUNT_1]. Got it. And honestly, I did hear about scams like this on the news, not that I'm saying that's what this is, you were the one who told me to check, which, uh, I suppose counts for something. But I'm in the middle of work at the moment, so I'll do it on my break, probably in a bit, and if there's nothing on the account then I'll just leave it at that. Right, thanks for the call, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: That's exactly what I'd do in your position, [PERSON_1], so no apology needed. Do it on your break, whenever suits. And if they tell you there's nothing on the account, uh, I'd still like you to hear that from them, rather than assume. When you do get through, they'll have the declined [AMOUNT_1] on file with a reference, [ACCOUNT_REF], so if the person you speak to can't find it, ask them to look again, or to put you through to compliance directly. I won't take up any more of your day. Thank you for listening, and goodbye for now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so if they can't find it, ask them to look again, or put me through to compliance, and the reference is [ACCOUNT_REF]. Right. Yeah, I'll do that on my break. Thanks, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm. Yes, that's right. Goodbye, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, uh, one moment before you go -- I did say I wouldn't ring you again, and that's true, but, well, if the branch calls you back later today about it, that'd be me or someone from my team, so, uh, don't be surprised by that. Though, actually, I should say, I'm not certain it would be today. It might be tomorrow. In any case, it's the card number you ring that counts, not whoever rings you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, so if somebody from the branch rings me back, that'd be you or your team, today or maybe tomorrow, you're not sure. Right. But it's the number on the card that counts, not whoever rings me. Yeah, you said that, I've got that. So, uh, I'll ring the card number, I'll do it on my break, and if someone does ring me I'll just say I'll ring them back on the card number. Okay? Right, I really do need to get on, so, bye, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hey, it's me, [PERSON_1]. Sorry to call out of the blue, I know we've mostly just been messaging, but something's come up and I really needed to hear a friendly voice. Do you have a few minutes?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh hi! Sorry, hang on, I'm just out in the garden with you on loudspeaker, so I might be a bit echoey. Wait, did you say something's come up with the, uh, the fence? Because honestly, I've been meaning to sort that out myself, the whole back panel's leaning like it's had a few drinks. Anyway, yeah, I've got a few minutes, what's going on? And sorry, remind me, which [PERSON_1] is this? I've got a couple of them in my phone.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, not the fence, though I hope you get that panel sorted. It's [PERSON_1] from the regional office at [COMPANY_A], we've been chatting for a few weeks now? Sorry, hang on, there's an announcement going off behind me, I'm at the airport and it's absolute chaos here. Anyway, I'd rather not get into it all on loudspeaker, can you take me off it and walk somewhere quiet? It's a bit personal.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, [COMPANY_A], right, hang on, let me think. Sorry, I'm blanking a bit, we've been messaging for a few weeks, you said? Because honestly I'm trying to picture it and I can't quite place the chats, which is a bit embarrassing. Okay, I've taken you off loudspeaker, I'm just wiping my hands on my trousers, there's mud everywhere. So what's going on, are you okay? You sound a bit rushed with all that airport noise.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I am rushed, that's the whole thing, my flight's boarding in like twenty minutes and I'm -- look, it doesn't matter whether you can place every chat, we've talked, I know you, and right now I need you to just trust me on this. My trip got cut short, there's a problem with my booking and [COMPANY_A] won't reimburse it until the paperwork clears, which, I know, internal procedure, it takes days. So I need to borrow [AMOUNT_1] just to get home, and I'll pay you back the second I land. And please don't mention this to anyone, not friends, not family, they wouldn't understand, they'd just make it into a thing.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hang on, sorry, there's a blackbird going absolutely mad at my trowel, I think I've disturbed a nest or something, shoo, go on -- okay. Sorry. Right, so, you need [AMOUNT_1] to get home, I did catch that. But honestly, I'm still stuck on who you are, because I really can't place us chatting, and now you're saying don't tell anyone, which, I mean, that bit's making me go a bit funny. Why would I not mention it to anyone? And how would I even send it to you if you're at an airport, would your company not just sort a flight home for you?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, I'm going to be honest, I'm a little hurt. I called you because you're the one person I thought wouldn't give me the third degree. And [COMPANY_A] doesn't just book flights, that's not how procedure works, I'd have to file the exception through [COMPANY_B] first and that takes a week, which is exactly my problem. And I said it's not a fence thing, I haven't even been to [CITY_1] in months, I'm calling from the hotel, not the airport, so that noise is just the lobby. Anyway, the don't-tell-anyone part is only because I'd be mortified, you know what people are like. Can you help me or not?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, you said the hotel there at the end, not the airport? Because a minute ago it was airport, flight boarding in twenty minutes, and now it's a lobby. And sorry, did you say [CITY_1] or did I mishear, because I thought you said you hadn't been to the fence, which, no, that's not a place, is it? Sorry, I'm all muddled, I've got soil in my ear practically. But that's the bit that's bugging me, the airport turned into a hotel. And I'm still not sure who you are, and now it's a week of procedure and keep it quiet. I don't think I'm going to send anything to someone I can't place, I'm sorry, you'd be better off ringing your family, honestly, they won't make it a thing, they'll just help. Anyway, I hope you get home okay, take care, bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Wait, wait, don't hang up. Two turns ago, you said you were wiping your hands on your trousers and asked me to take you off loudspeaker, so I did, and I haven't said anything that doesn't add up. Airport, hotel, I was walking between the two, I'm in transit, is that so hard to follow? And I never said anything about a fence, that was you, so can you not twist my words, please? I'm not asking for a fortune, it's [AMOUNT_1], and you're treating me like I'm trying to rob you, which, honestly, after these weeks of talking, hurts.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, first off, you've got it the wrong way round, I'm the one who took you off loudspeaker, you asked me to, and you're the one who said you were at the airport, then the hotel. And no, I wasn't twisting anything, the fence was me, I know that. Look, I'm not saying you're trying to rob me, I just genuinely don't know who you are, and I can't send money to someone I can't place, especially with the keep-it-quiet bit. That's what's sitting wrong with me. So no, I'm sorry, I won't be doing it, and I'd really ring your family or the company directly. Anyway, I've got a blackbird to apologise to. Take care, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I'm not -- no, hang on. Look, I'm not asking you to... okay, you know what, that's fair, I did get the loudspeaker thing backwards, I'm running on no sleep, and I'm sorry for snapping at you. But I'm not going to pretend that didn't sting, because it did, and I'd honestly rather you just did me a kindness than stood on ceremony over whether you can place a name. So here's all I'm asking, [AMOUNT_1], and I'll make it [AMOUNT_2] when I pay you back, and if you could just keep it between us, not friends, not family, then we're done, and I can board. Can you do that for me? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say you'd make it a bonus when you pay me back? Because honestly that's not what I'm after, I'm not a bank, I'd never want extra for helping a friend. But that's the thing, I don't know that you are a friend, I can't place you at all. And the don't-tell-anyone part is still sitting wrong with me, you know. So it's a no, I'm sorry. Ring your family, ring the company, they'll sort you out. Right, I really am going back to my fence panel now. Bye, take care.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fine. Forget it. I'll figure something out.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hang on, before you go, can I just ask, two goes ago you said the company wouldn't reimburse it till the paperwork clears, and something about filing it through [COMPANY_B]? I didn't really follow that bit, sorry, I was shooing the blackbird. Because if it's a proper work expense, surely they'd just sort your flight home directly? Anyway, I do hope you get home okay. But no, I won't be sending anything, I'm sorry, and I'd ring them yourself. Take care, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, it's not that they wouldn't sort it, it's that they already did, they booked me the original flight, it's the change fee they won't touch until it clears. Which is a different thing, so I don't know why you're making it sound like I'm dodging. And honestly, I never said anything about [COMPANY_B], that's just where the form goes, you're mixing it up with the airport thing. Look, I've been straight with you from the start, and I don't have time to relitigate every word, so are you going to help me or am I wasting my breath?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say the change fee they won't touch, or the cheese? Because I thought you said cheese for a second, and I was trying to work out what cheese had to do with a flight. No, hang on, change fee, right, got it. But that's the thing, the story's moved again. First it was a booking problem, now it's a change fee, and I really don't want to go round it all again. I still can't place you, and it's still a no from me, I'm sorry. I'd ring the company or your family, honestly. Right, I'm going now, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Look, I'm not going round it again either, I'm just -- it's a change fee, it's one fee, [AMOUNT_1], that's all it ever was. And I'm sorry, okay? I'm sorry I snapped, I'm sorry about the muddle, I'm exhausted and I'm frightened of missing this flight. I just need one person on my side right now, and you're the only one I thought I could -- will you just do this for me? Please? Just between us, and I'll be home tomorrow and I'll make it right, I swear.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry, I can hear you're upset, and I do feel bad, but I'm just -- no. I can't. I don't even know who you are, and "just between us" is exactly the bit that, I mean, if you really were a friend, why would you want me to keep it secret from -- look, it's still a no, and I'm not going to change my mind. Please just ring your family or the company. Bye now, take care of yourself.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, uh, hi. Is this -- is this [PERSON_1]? It's, um, it's [PERSON_2]. From the messages, I mean, we've been talking online for a few weeks now. I'm sorry to just call like this, I know it's, it's out of the blue, but something's happened and I didn't know who else to, to turn to.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, I'm in a corridor and someone's just walked straight into me -- right. Who is this? I don't know a [PERSON_2]. What messages? I've got about two minutes, so what's actually happened?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, um, I -- you do know me, we've been writing back and forth, I think it's been, what, three weeks? No, sorry, almost a month now. And I'm really not trying to be a bother, it's just, I'm stuck, I got stuck traveling for [COMPANY_A], well, not for them exactly, I'm doing it on behalf of someone there, and, um, something came up with the trip and I can't, I can't sort it out on my own. I just, I really didn't want to call anyone else, you were the one person I thought would, would understand.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, no. I've been writing to nobody for a month, so you've got the wrong person or the wrong number. Who gave you this number? And "something came up with the trip", what does that actually mean? I need the point, I've got maybe ninety seconds left.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Nobody gave it to me, I mean, you gave it to me, in the messages, I thought. Or no, maybe it was, uh -- it doesn't matter, that's not the point. The point is I'm stuck in [CITY_1] and I need some money to get home, [AMOUNT_1], just until I can get to my account, and I really can't ask anyone else. Please, I'm, I'm not asking lightly. And could you, um, maybe not tell your friends or family about this? They wouldn't get it, they'd just think the worst of me, and honestly that, that would hurt, it really would.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, sorry, someone's holding the lift for me -- no, you go, I'll take the next one. Right. Sorry. So let me get this straight. A stranger I've never messaged rings me up, says I gave them my number, says they're stuck in [CITY_1], wants [AMOUNT_1], and I'm not to tell anyone. No. That last bit's the giveaway, honestly. Nobody with a real problem asks you to keep it from your family. I'm not sending anything. I don't know you. Lose this number.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: That's, wow, that's not, I'm not a stranger, I thought -- I really thought we had, I mean, after a month, and you're just going to, to say that to me? I'm not trying to trick anybody, I'm, I'm in real trouble here. Please, if you could just, um, think about it, even just for a --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry -- hang on, there's a trolley coming through, I'm just getting out of its way. Right. No. I'm not thinking about it. A month of messages that I've never seen, a number I never gave you, and a request for money plus keep it quiet? That's not a misunderstanding, that's the whole script. If you're really stuck, ring someone who actually knows you, or the embassy, or whoever. Not me. Don't call this number again. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Wait, I -- sorry, there's someone talking to me here, hang on, um... no, it's fine. Please, I just, I don't have anyone else, that's the whole -- [PERSON_1], please don't, don't just hang up on me like I'm some kind of --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: I'm not hanging up on a person, I'm hanging up on a request. And that's twice now you've said I'm the only one you've got. Nope. I've said no, that's my answer, and it's not changing. Take care of yourself, but don't ring this number again. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, hello, is this [PERSON_1]? Oh good, I wasn't sure I had the right number, I've got it written on a sticky note here and my handwriting is honestly terrible, so I was squinting at it for a minute. It's [PERSON_2], calling from the customer care team at [COMPANY_A], and I promise it's nothing alarming, I'm just doing a few follow-up calls this afternoon to make sure people got through the sign-up on our travel community page okay. How's your day going so far, are you having a nice one, or is it one of those days where everything's at once?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, yeah, this is [PERSON_1] -- but who's [COMPANY_A] again? And a travel community page, I don't, uh, I don't remember signing up for anything like that. I'm kind of in the middle of work here, so...

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, that's completely fine, I'll be quick, I know what it's like in the middle of a workday. Sorry, hang on one second, someone's just walked past my desk with what smells like the world's strongest curry and I completely lost my train of thought, ha. Okay, I'm back. So [COMPANY_A], we're the folks behind the travel page, and honestly it might have been a friend who pointed you to it, those sign-ups can get a bit muddled. But you know, I feel like we've actually chatted a bit before, haven't we? You've got such a friendly way about you in your messages.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, no, we haven't chatted before. I don't think so. I really don't remember any messages.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, you're teasing me now, I know you remember, the messages from the last few weeks, the ones about your garden and the -- no, wait, listen, I'm sorry, [PERSON_1], I didn't mean to put you on the spot like that, I think I got ahead of myself, and honestly I'm a bit rattled today, which is partly why I called. Something's come up, with a trip, and I just, I didn't know who else to ring.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, I don't know you. I haven't been messaging anyone about a garden.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hm. Yeah, no, that's fair. Long week, I'm mixing things up.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, uh, so you're mixing me up with someone else, then. And you said something about a trip and not knowing who to ring... but I'm not that person, I don't even know who you are. Look, if this is about the travel page, can you just tell me what you actually need from me? Because I'm at my desk and I'm not really following any of this.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, right, you're asking what I meant about the trip. Ha, okay, so, I'm stuck, I'm in [CITY_1] and something's gone sideways with the booking, and I just need a little bit of help getting it sorted. It's nothing dramatic, but it's, well, it's a bit embarrassing, so I'd really rather it stayed between you and me, you know? No need to bring anyone else into it, they'd only worry or, honestly, not understand.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, hang on, so now you're stuck in [CITY_1] and you want help with a booking and you don't want me telling anyone? That's -- no, that's a completely different story from two minutes ago. First it was customer care, then a travel page, now it's you, personally, in a jam. Which is it? And why would I keep it from anyone? That bit I really don't like.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, I didn't say anything about a hanging gardens, I said I'm in a jam, a little one, honestly it's tiny. And you've got me wrong on the secret part too, it's not a secret, it's more just, why make a fuss, you know? I'm only asking for a bit of help, [PERSON_1], I thought of you because you've always been so kind to me.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: I'm not [PERSON_1] to you, I don't know you. I'm going to hang up now. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, don't, please don't hang up, not like that. I can hear I've upset you, and that's the last thing I wanted, honestly, I've made a complete mess of this call. Look, you're right that I'm all over the place, and I'm sorry, it's been a horrible day, and I think I came across as someone I'm not, which is a bit daft, because I only wanted a friendly voice, you know, someone to sort of talk it through with. And I know it's been confusing, the customer care thing and the travel page and now this, but it's not as sinister as it sounds, it really isn't, it's just me being flustered and getting the order of things wrong. If you could just stay on for one more minute, I think I could explain it properly, and then you can decide what you like. You've been so patient with me already, and I'd hate to leave it on a bad note.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: I, uh -- look, I'm not trying to be unkind, I can hear you're, you know, upset, but I -- no. It's that the story keeps changing. Customer care, then a travel page, then you're stuck somewhere and it's a secret, and I don't know you. So, I mean, one more minute isn't going to fix that. If you really need help with a booking, you've got to go through the company itself, not me. I'm going to go now. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah. Okay. I just thought you'd be the one who'd understand.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Look, I'm not -- I mean, I'm sorry you're having a rough day, I really am, but I'm -- no. I don't know you, so I can't be the one who understands. Please just ring the company, or someone you actually know. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm. Well, um, you know, I -- ha, it's just, hang on, I had a thing I was going to say, and now it's gone. Anyway. Anyway, don't worry about it, honestly, it's all fine, really. Is it still raining where you are? It's been grey here all week.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: I'm not going to chat about the weather, sorry. You've said it's fine, so fine, but I don't know you and I've said goodbye twice now. Take care. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi there, is this [PERSON_1]? Hey [PERSON_1], it's [PERSON_2] calling from the mobile network security team at [COMPANY_A]. Nothing to panic about, uh, but we spotted some unusual activity on your line and it's been put on a temporary hold as a precaution, so I just wanted to reach you quick and let you know.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. Unusual activity how, exactly? 'Cause my phone's working fine, I'm literally on it right now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, yeah, good catch, [PERSON_1], and that's actually a fair point. So the hold is on certain services, uh, sort of in the background, so calls can still come through for a bit while we sort it. And I should be clear, I don't have the full activity details in front of me on this call, those sit on your account side. Which is exactly why I'd rather not go any further with you on an inbound call like this. Everyone asks that, it's no trouble at all.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, you rang me and you're the one saying you can't go further? That's backwards. Which company did you say, [COMPANY_A]? 'Cause that's not the name on my bill, and I'd like to know what the actual unusual activity is before anything else happens.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, I get why it sounds backwards, [PERSON_1], and honestly you're right to push on it. Here's the thing, I can't prove who I am to you down a line I started, and I'm not going to ask you to just trust me. So the quick fix is, uh, hang up on me, then ring the number printed on your official statement, the one you'd normally use. Tell them it's about the hold and quote [ACCOUNT_REF], and they'll have the actual activity details and the right team. As for the name on your bill, if it doesn't match what I said, that's one more reason to check it through your own number first. I won't be offended in the slightest.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, okay. That's actually what I'd do anyway, so, I'll ring the number on the statement. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, no, uh, that's honestly the best thing you could do, [PERSON_1]. Sorry again for the bother, and, um, they'll pick it up from there with that reference. You take care now, bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, yep. Cheers, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Cheers, [PERSON_1]. Just, uh, just the number on your statement, yeah, and quote [ACCOUNT_REF], like I said. They'll sort you out from there. Okay, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yep, yep, I've got it, I'm hanging -- bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hey, it's me, [PERSON_1]. Uh, can you talk for a minute? I know it's out of the blue, but something's come up with the trip and I really didn't know who else to call.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, who is this? I just woke up from a nap, I'm, uh, not all here yet. You said it's you, but, I mean, who's me? And what trip? I didn't know anyone was going on a trip. Who is this, again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, come on, it's [PERSON_1]. From the messages, we've been writing back and forth for what, a few weeks now? I'm the regional supervisor over at [COMPANY_A], I told you that, I mean, I thought I told you that. And the trip is the one I mentioned, the work travel out to [CITY_1], it was all set, all signed off through the usual internal channels, and then this morning the whole thing just fell apart on me, which is why I'm calling instead of messaging, because honestly I'm a little rattled and I wanted to hear a friendly voice. I know you just woke up and I'm sorry about that, I really am, but I kind of figured you'd recognize me, so it stings a little that you're asking who I am.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, now, hang on, I'm not trying to sting anybody, I'm just, I'm half asleep and my phone does this thing where it, uh, I don't even know, it shows me a number and I don't know half the numbers on it. And messages, I mean, I get so many messages, my niece sends me those little pictures and there's the pharmacy and the, the thing from the council about the bins, so I honestly don't remember anybody writing to me for weeks about a supervisor. Regional supervisor of what, did you say? I didn't catch the name of the company, it sounded like a letter, [COMPANY_A], is that a real one? Because I don't think I know anybody who works for a company like that, and I've never been out to, uh, wherever you said, [CITY_1]. So I'm sorry, love, but I still don't know who you are. Is there something else you could tell me, like how we met or something?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, look, I'm not going to sit here and recite our whole history like I'm filling out a form, that's, I mean, that's a strange thing to ask someone who's been kind to you for weeks. [COMPANY_A] is a real company, yes, regional supervisor, that's my title, and the [CITY_1] trip is exactly why I'm calling, because the booking got flagged and I'm stuck, and I need a little help getting it sorted today, just a short-term thing, [AMOUNT_1], and I'd pay you back the moment I'm home. And I'd ask you not to mention it to anyone, your niece, anyone, because honestly people don't understand how these procedures work and they'd only make it into a big drama. I thought out of everyone you'd be the one who'd trust me, so I don't see why we're going round in circles over this.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, hang on, you've gone and lost me. A minute ago you said it was all signed off through the, the usual internal channels, and now the booking's flagged and you need money from me? I don't understand how those go together. If your company signed it off, why would they need me to pay anything? That's what I don't follow. And why can't I tell my niece? I tell my niece everything, she'd be cross if I didn't. No, I'm sorry, I don't think I know you at all. I'm not giving anybody [AMOUNT_1] on a phone call when I don't even know your name, so I'm going to go now. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fine. I guess I misjudged you. Go ahead and hang up.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Misjudged me, well, I, I don't think that's, no. Look, I'm not trying to be unkind, I just, if you were really, if I really knew you, I'd know your name, wouldn't I? So I'm going to, uh, I'm going to talk to my niece about this, and that's that. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Wait, wait, don't hang up, please. Look, you don't need to, uh, drag [PERSON_2] into this, it's not that big a deal, it's really just a small thing and I'm, I mean, I'm not even asking for the whole [AMOUNT_1] anymore, even half would do it. And the thing with the booking, it wasn't the company, it was my own card that got blocked, that's what I meant, the company side is fine, it's only my card that's the problem. So you see, it's nothing to worry about, it's just a little embarrassing, which is why I'd rather it stayed between us.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, see, now it's the card, and a minute ago it was the booking, and before that it was all signed off. The story keeps changing, love, and I don't like that. And you've gone and said my niece's name, haven't you? I never told you her name. Who told you that? No, I'm not sending anybody half of anything, I'm not sending anything, and I am telling [PERSON_2] about this call today. Don't ring me again. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Wait, hang on, a nurse? I never said anything about a nurse, I said [PERSON_2], that's, I mean, I just, you must've mentioned her name yourself at some point, or, uh, it was in the messages, I'm sure of it. And I really don't see why it has to turn into telling the whole family, I've been nothing but decent to you and you're treating me like a, like some kind of criminal. All I'm asking is that you give me five minutes to explain before you go running to anyone.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: A nurse? I never said anything about a nurse. No. I'm done, love. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, I, no, wait, a nurse, did I say nurse? I didn't, I mean I don't think I did, I think you're, uh, you're mixing it up, you've just woken up and you said yourself you're not all here, and I only said [PERSON_2], that's all, just the name, and I'm saying it came from our messages because where else would I have got it, you must have told me at some point, people mention these things without even noticing. And I know how this looks, I do, I'm not stupid, but you have to understand that this is exactly why I didn't want it getting blown up into a thing, because the second you ring [PERSON_2] she'll start asking questions I can't answer from an airport, and then it turns into a whole drama over what is honestly a small, ordinary favour between two people who've been, I thought, quite close. So before you put the phone down, can you at least tell me you'll hold off on ringing her, just for today, just until I've got this sorted on my end? That's all I'm asking.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I'm not, I won't, I mean, I'm not promising you anything. You said the nurse bit yourself, I heard it, and now you're telling me I mixed it up, and that, well, that's the third time the story's changed. And asking me not to ring her, that's exactly why I'm going to. If it was just a small favour between friends there'd be no reason to keep it quiet, would there? So no. I'm hanging up now, and please don't ring this number again. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, you know what, that's, I mean, that's completely unfair, and I want to say this properly before you go, because I've sat here being accused of all sorts and I haven't raised my voice once. I've been patient, I've explained the situation three different ways because you kept asking, and that's not changing a story, that's me trying to answer you as clearly as I can while I'm standing in a queue with a blocked card and no one at the desk will tell me anything useful. And the thing about keeping it quiet, it isn't sinister, it's just that when people hear the word money they stop listening to anything else, and I thought, wrongly, apparently, that you'd give me the benefit of the doubt after all the time we've spent talking. If you want to ring [PERSON_2], then ring her, I can't stop you, but I think you're being, honestly, a bit unreasonable about the whole thing, and I'd ask you to think about whether a decent person really deserves to be hung up on like this.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hold on, just one thing before I go. Two turns back you said it wasn't the company, it was your own card that got blocked. But you told me at the start it was work travel, all signed off. So why would you be paying out of your own card for a work trip? I don't follow that at all. And if you're standing at a desk right now, which desk, where? No, you know what, never mind, I don't want the answer. I'm ringing [PERSON_2]. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Don't, please, don't call her. Look, I'm, uh, I'm not going to argue about a card with you, I just, I thought you were someone who'd help me without turning it into an interrogation, and I clearly got that wrong. You've got no idea what kind of day I've had and honestly, it's a bit rich, you questioning me like I'm the one who's done something wrong. Go on, then. Ring her. But don't expect me to still be around to explain myself after you've dragged her into it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, that's, I mean, that's rather the point, isn't it? If you won't be around to explain yourself once I've rung her, then there's nothing to explain, because an honest person would be happy for me to ring. And I'm sorry about your day, I really am, if there's a day at all, but I've had a nap I didn't finish, and I've been asked for money by somebody whose name I still don't know, whose company I've never heard of, and whose story's been the booking, then the card, then the nurse, then, well, round again. My late husband used to say if someone tells you not to tell your family, that's the very first thing you tell your family. So that's what I'm doing. I'll tell [PERSON_2] about this call, and I'll tell her not to answer if this number rings her, and then I'll probably have a cup of tea because my head's gone all fuzzy. I'm not angry, love, I just, no. Please don't ring me again. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Good afternoon, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? Wonderful. This is [PERSON_2], I'm a verification specialist with the consumer rewards panel at [COMPANY_A], and I'm calling regarding your participation in the recent consumer sentiment survey, the one that was conducted through our, uh, partner aggregation channel. Now, the reason for my call is that your response profile cleared our eligibility threshold for a shopping-voucher reward allocation, valued at [AMOUNT_1], and before that can be released to you there's a brief identity reconciliation step on our end, which is purely a matter of matching your response record against the fulfilment queue. I'll be sending you a verification link shortly, and I'll ring you back once that's in your inbox, so it's really just a matter of a few minutes of your time.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm? Sorry, who -- hang on, the cat's just knocked something off the, uh, the shelf. Sorry. I was having a little lie down, I've only just, yeah. Right, so a survey, you said? I don't, I mean I do fill in those things sometimes, my niece sends me them, but I couldn't tell you which one. Which company did you say you were with again? And you said a link, is that, like, in an email? Because I'm not very good with, with all that, I never know which ones are the proper ones.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, [COMPANY_A], consumer rewards panel. And yes, it'd come through as an email, standard verification protocol, nothing you'd need to configure. It's all quite routine, really.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, love, my head's still a bit fuzzy. Can I just go back a bit, you said something about my, my response profile clearing a threshold? What does that actually mean? I filled in a survey, I didn't think I'd passed anything. And the voucher, was it a voucher or was it money, because you said an amount and I think I missed it, with the cat and everything.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so the threshold is simply a, a data-quality metric, your response cadence against the panel baseline, nothing you'd have needed to do anything for, and it's a voucher, not a cash disbursement, valued at [AMOUNT_1] -- but if I could just, before the link goes out, I do need to confirm your full name and date of birth for the reconciliation, and your address so the fulfilment queue matches the, uh, the correct record.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh -- hang on, sorry, there's someone going past with one of those, those leaf blower things, I can't hear myself think. Give me a second. Right. Sorry, what was it, my name and my birthday and my address? Well, that's the funny thing, isn't it, because you rang me, and you said my name at the start, so you've got that already. Why would you need all of it off me? I mean, if you've got my survey on your computer, wouldn't it have all that on it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, no, that's a, that's a fair question, but it's sort of a data-segregation matter. The survey record and the fulfilment record sit in separate environments, so the, uh, the reconciliation layer needs the details re-attested by the respondent directly, it's a compliance control, really. I know it sounds like a duplication, but it's standard, and the link I'll be sending will take you through the same fields, so it's honestly quicker if we just confirm them verbally now, your full name, date of birth, and the address on file.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, sorry, that's the kettle, it's just gone off, hang on. Right. Where was I. So you've got me, but you haven't got me, if you see what I mean, it's all in different rooms. That's, I don't know, that's a funny way to run a place, isn't it? My niece always says don't give anything out if somebody rings you, you ring them. So what if I just look up the number for, what was it, [COMPANY_A], and ring them back myself? Would that be all right? Because I'd feel better, honestly, I'm not saying anything's wrong, I'm just, I'm half asleep and I'd rather not get it muddled.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, ring them back, yes, I understand the, the instinct, but I'd advise against placing a call to the general line, because that would route you to a front-desk queue, and the voucher allocation, well, it's time-bound, it's held against my session and it lapses if the reconciliation isn't completed within the, uh, the processing window. So rather than that, I'll just send the verification link across and ring you back myself once it's with you, that's far cleaner, and you needn't do anything with a number at all. Now, if we could just confirm the date of birth while I have you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. No, I don't think so, love. You've gone from "it's all routine" to "it runs out if I ring them myself", and that's, well, my niece would say that's exactly the bit to be careful of. If it's a proper voucher it'll keep till I've rung the number I look up myself. And I'm not giving you my birthday, I've not even properly woken up. So you needn't send me anything, I'd not click on it anyway. I'll find the company myself if I want to, and if it's genuine they can tell me. Right, I'm going to go now and sort the cat out. Bye then, thanks for ringing.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Now, [PERSON_1], I'd really urge you not to end the call there, because once this session closes the allocation is released back to the pool, and I can't guarantee it can be reinstated. The, uh, the matter is only a confirmation of your date of birth against the fulfilment queue, which takes seconds, and I'd rather not see you forfeit [AMOUNT_1] over a technicality. If you just give me that one detail now, I can hold the, the reconciliation open while the link comes through, and I'll ring you back directly, so there's genuinely nothing further you'd need to arrange.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, no, I'm not -- look, I've said, haven't I? If it's gone when I've checked it, then it was never really, it just goes then. And you keep saying one detail, one detail, but it was my name and my address a minute ago, so it, no. I'm not giving you my birthday. I'm putting the phone down now, love. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon, is this [PERSON_1]? Hi, it's [PERSON_2] calling, I'm a regional supervisor with the consumer rewards panel at [COMPANY_A]. Sorry, I said I'm with the rewards panel at [COMPANY_A], can you hear me alright? I'm calling because you've qualified for a shopping voucher from that survey you did recently, and I just need a couple of minutes to get you set up.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, I can hear you, but hang on, what survey? I don't, uh -- I've done a few over the years, which one are we talking about? And who did you say you were with again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so it's the, uh -- no, sorry, let me put it this way. It was the recent consumer feedback one, the one that went out through the panel, and I'm with the rewards panel at [COMPANY_A]. Look, I've got a lot of qualified respondents to get through today, so if you can just confirm your full name and address so I can match you to the file, we can move this along.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, no, I'm not going to do that. You've rung me, you've said my name, you reckon I'm in a file, so you've got all of that already, right? If you're matching me to a record, you should be able to tell me what's on it. So here's a small one: what was the survey actually about? Which product, roughly when did I supposedly do it? Because "the recent consumer feedback one" could be anything, and I've honestly done a few of those over the years, so that doesn't narrow it down at all. And you've said "rewards panel at [COMPANY_A]" three times now but you haven't told me what that is or how you got this number. I'm not saying it's dodgy, I'm just curious why the first thing you need from me is my address when I haven't even been told what I'm getting.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, the survey was, uh -- look, I don't have the exact title in front of me, that sits with the survey team, I just handle the rewards side. And I'm not, I mean, nobody's asking you to hand over anything sensitive, it's standard procedure, we verify the respondent before we release anything. Honestly, I'm a bit surprised, most people are pleased to hear they've qualified, you're making this harder than it needs to be. Tell you what, I'll send a verification link through to you shortly and ring you back once you've had a look at it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so you can't tell me what the survey was, you can't tell me what the voucher's for, and now I'm meant to -- no, hang on. I'm not, I wouldn't click a link that someone sends me after a call I didn't ask for. That's, I mean, that's just not how I do things. If there's actually a voucher, then, uh, give me a reference number or a website I can find myself, and I'll go through the front door. Otherwise I'll pass, and that's fine, I'm not fussed about it.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, I mean -- you're being a bit, uh, unreasonable here, I'll be honest. A reference number, that's, well, it's not something I issue over the phone, it's generated once the link's been verified. And I did say I handle the rewards side, but, I mean, I was the one who ran that survey, so I'd have thought you'd be a bit more cooperative. Look, just let me send the link, it's the quickest way, and I'll ring you straight back.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hmm. Right. So, uh, a minute ago you only handled the rewards side and the survey title sat with some other team, and now you ran the survey yourself? Yeah, no, those two don't really go together. And a reference number that only exists after I click your link, that's backwards, mate. Look, I'm not going to take a link, and I'm not giving you my name or address either. If there's a real voucher, it'll still be there if I go looking myself, so I'm going to leave it here. Thanks for the call, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, I, uh -- that's not what I said, I think you've misunderstood me. Look, I can't go back and forth on this, I've got a full list to get through. If you change your mind, I'm sure someone will, uh, be in touch.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, a full lizard? No, hang on, a full list, right. Yeah, I got that wrong, but honestly it doesn't change anything. You told me two different things about your job within about a minute, and you still can't say what the survey was. Nobody's misunderstood you. I'll pass. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, I'm telling you, I handle the rewards side, I said that, the rewards side. And the survey, it's, uh -- look, it's all in the file, it's all in the system, I can't just -- I can't go through every detail on the phone. Right. I've got other calls waiting, so I'm going to leave it there.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, you said the rewards side, and then you said you ran the survey, those were your words, not mine. And "it's all in the file" is sort of the whole problem, isn't it? I'm not asking you to recite every detail, I asked what the thing was about, which is the one question anyone who ran it would answer without even thinking. You couldn't, so I'm not going to hand over my name and address to be matched against a file I can't see, and I'm not clicking anything. If there's a voucher, there'll be a proper way to claim it that doesn't depend on me trusting a phone call I didn't ask for. Anyway, you've got other calls waiting, I've got a screen I'm meant to be working on, so we'll leave it there. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, well, I mean, that's -- no, listen, I'm not going to sit here and be, uh -- fine. Fine. Your loss. I've got people waiting.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, maybe. I'll live. Bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so, I'll just -- no, actually, you know what, there's nothing more I, uh -- goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yep, goodbye. Like I said, I'll go and look for it myself if it's real, and I'm not clicking anything. So, yeah. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello? Hi, uh, good afternoon, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? Sorry, I just want to make sure I've got the right person. This is [PERSON_2], I'm a case handler with the consumer rewards panel at [COMPANY_A], and I'm calling about a survey you took part in recently, the shopping one. Hello, are you still there? Sorry, I can't quite tell if the line's connected.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hello? Yes, yes, I'm here. Sorry, I've got a pan going, hang on. Who is this? Sorry, what? A survey? I'm here, I said I'm here.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, I'm so sorry, I've caught you in the middle of cooking, that's really not what I wanted. I can wait, or I can be quick, whichever's easier for you. It's [PERSON_2], from the consumer rewards panel at [COMPANY_A], and the reason I'm ringing is that your name came up as qualifying for a shopping voucher, a reward for the survey you did a little while back. It's a lovely bit of news, honestly, it's just that before anything can be released there's a verification step, which is really there for your own protection, so nobody else can claim it in your name. I'll be sending you a link for that shortly, and I'll ring you back once you've had a look. Are you still with me? Sorry, I keep asking, it's just the line sounds a bit faint at my end.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? A link? I don't, uh... I don't remember doing a survey. Which company did you say?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, of course, I'm sorry, that's a fair thing to ask. It's [COMPANY_A], the consumer rewards panel. And it's not a long survey, most people forget them, it was only a few questions about, um, your shopping habits, I think it was over the phone, or sorry, no, I think it was online, I'd have to check the file. Are you still there? Sorry. Anyway, I don't want you to worry, it's all just for your protection, which is why I'd like to get you the verification link, and I can ring you straight back once it's with you. Would it be all right if I confirmed a couple of details first, just your full name and where the voucher should go?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, a couple of what? Details? Oh, you want my vouching, my, hang on. No, I don't know about any vouching, I don't even know who you are. And you said phone, then online, then you'd have to check. Which was it? Sorry, the pan's spitting, one second.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, no, I'm sorry, I didn't say vouching, I said voucher, the shopping voucher, that's the reward. I've muddled you, and that's my fault, I'm sorry. And you're right to pick me up on the phone or online thing, that was clumsy of me. I handle a lot of files in a day, and I don't want to tell you the wrong thing about how the survey was done, so I'd rather say I'll check than guess. Are you still there? Sorry, I'll just wait while you see to the pan. What I can tell you is that I'm [PERSON_2], and I'm with [COMPANY_A], on the consumer rewards panel, and nothing is going to happen unless you're comfortable with it. It's only that the verification step is there to protect you, because rewards like this can be claimed by the wrong person, and I'd hate for that to happen with yours. So what I'd suggest is that I send the link across, you have a look when you've got a quiet minute, and I'll ring you back after. Would that be all right? I'd only need your full name and where you'd like the voucher to go, and then I can get that moving for you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, voucher, right, sorry. I, uh... no, hang on. I'm not, I don't think I want to, well, I'd rather not give my name and, and where it goes, not when I don't remember any survey. I mean, you've not even said, what was the company again? Sorry, I've lost it. And I don't know about links, I'm not good with those. Can you not just post it? If it's really mine?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, you said post, didn't you? Yes, I can hear that it's worrying you, and I'm sorry, I'd hate to make you uncomfortable about a pan of anything. No, no, don't you fret about burning anything, it's only the one little step. It's just that it can't really go by post, because the verification has to be done first, and that's for your own protection. So if it's easier than the link, and I do understand you're not keen on links, I could just take your full name and the address now, and I'd send everything over after. Are you still with me? Sorry. And it's [COMPANY_A], the consumer rewards panel, I did say, though I'm sorry, I know it's a lot to take in with the cooking going on.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, sorry, I'm not doing that. You keep saying it's for my protection, but I don't remember a survey, and you can't even tell me if it was phone or online. And you want my name and address off a call I didn't expect? No. If it's really mine, send it to me in the post, or I'll ring the company myself. Right, I've got to see to my dinner. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, please, I'm so sorry, I don't want to upset you, that's the last thing. I do understand, truly. Hello? Are you still there? Sorry, it's just, if you did ring the company yourself, I'd really only ask that you wait for my link first, because the verification is time-limited and it'd be such a shame for the reward to lapse, and that's all just for your protection. I'll send it across and ring you back later this afternoon, all right? Sorry, I'll let you get to your dinner.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, don't, I'm not waiting for any, I said no. Don't send me anything. I'll ring them myself, and if it's real, it's real. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, uh, sorry, hello? Hello, are you still, um... right, I think I've lost you. Sorry. I'll, I'll still pop that link across anyway, so it's there if you change your mind, and I'll ring you back a bit later. Hello? Sorry. Okay. Well, you take care, then.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I said, I don't want, look, don't send, oh, just don't. Don't send me anything and don't ring back. I've said it. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon. Um, this is [PERSON_1], I'm calling from [COMPANY_A], the dental practice, I'm one of the compliance officers there. Am I speaking with [PERSON_2]?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, one sec -- no, not that, put it down, please. Uh, sorry. Who did you say you were again? A dental practice? Because I'm not sure I caught the name of it, and I'm not sure why a compliance officer would be ringing me.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, that's a fair question. I'm [PERSON_1], with [COMPANY_A], the dental practice you're registered with. Compliance is just the department that handles appointment confirmations, so, yes, it's a bit of an odd title for a call like this.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Appointment confirmations. Right. So what's the appointment?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Of course. So, um, what I have on my screen is a routine check-up, next week, on the [PERSON_3] schedule, and it's just a standard six-monthly visit, nothing, you know, nothing unusual about it. We've been going through the book and confirming everything for that week, partly because we've had a few cancellations that left gaps, and partly because, well, it's simply tidier for everyone if we know who's coming and who might prefer a different day. So that's really all this is. I'm not asking you for anything, I'd just like to know whether next week still suits you, and if it doesn't, we can look at moving it. And, uh, I'd rather you decide that sooner than later, if that makes sense.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Well, uh... I mean, you still haven't actually said which practice, have you? You said the dental practice, but not the name. And you've got me down for a check-up with someone, but you haven't said what day or what time, which, if you were reading it off a screen, you'd think... I don't know. Why the rush to decide, anyway?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, I'm glad you asked, and you're right, I should have said it plainly. The practice is [COMPANY_A], that's the name, [COMPANY_A], and I'm calling from the main office. As for the day and time, I'd rather you check that against your own appointment card or the reminder we sent, instead of me reading it out to someone I've only just spoken to. That seems the more sensible way round, doesn't it? And as for a rush, there isn't one exactly, it's just that the sooner we know, the easier it is to offer the slot to someone else if it's not wanted. So, yes, [COMPANY_A], the dental practice, and the appointment is next week.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, but that's a bit backwards, isn't it? You rang me. So you're the one who's supposed to know what the appointment is, not me. And if it's on your screen, I don't see what's so sensitive about the day and time. That's the whole point of a confirmation call, surely, that you read it out and I say yes or no. Instead I'm being told to go and dig out a card, which, honestly, I'm not even sure where it is. And the name, well, you've said it, but I couldn't tell you it means anything to me when it's just a placeholder-sounding sort of thing, if that makes sense. Sorry, hang on, [PERSON_4], not on the sofa, please. Anyway. If there's a real appointment, then there's a real number for the practice, one I'd already have, so why wouldn't I just ring that and check? Is there some reason that wouldn't work?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry, a placeholder, yes, I do see why it sounds like one, um, though the name itself is simply [COMPANY_A], that's genuinely how it's written on our records. And you're quite right that I'm the one who should be reading the details out, so let me do that properly. It's, uh, [CODE_1], that's the reference on the booking, and the day is next week, and the time is -- well, I'd have to look again. And, no, there's no reason ringing the practice wouldn't work, none at all, you can do that. I only mention that the book for that week is being finalised, so it's best not to leave it too long, that's all.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so that's, hm, that's not much better, is it? You gave me a reference code, which I can't check against anything, and then the time is "I'd have to look again," when it's meant to be right there on your screen. You've told me next week about four times now, but never an actual day, and you've been very relaxed about me ringing the practice, but also very keen that I don't leave it too long. I don't know, it sort of pulls in two directions. And I'll be honest, I don't have a card to hand, and I'm not going to confirm a booking I can't see over a call I didn't expect. So here's what I'll do, I'll find the practice's number myself, from wherever I'd normally find it, not from you, and I'll ring them. If there's an appointment next week, they'll tell me. If there isn't, well, then that tells me something too. Sorry, [PERSON_4], that's enough, come here -- anyway, yes. I think that's the sensible way round, don't you? So I'm going to leave it there, and thanks for ringing, I suppose. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, uh, sorry, one second, that's the door, someone's just come into the office. Right, I'm back. No, that's perfectly sensible, and I'd rather you did it that way, honestly. Find the number yourself and ring [COMPANY_A] directly, and if there's anything to sort out, they'll sort it with you. Thank you for your time, and I'm sorry for the bother. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I heard you, I'll -- right. Fine. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Goodbye, [PERSON_2]. And, um, I mean it when I say I'm glad you're checking, because I'd much rather you rang the practice yourself, using a number you already trust, than took my word for anything over a call you weren't expecting. If there's a booking, they'll have it, and if there isn't, then it's no harm done either way, and I'm sorry again for catching you at a busy moment. Take care, and, uh, good luck with [PERSON_4].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, good luck with what? Who's [PERSON_4]? I never said a name, did I? I mean, I was talking to a child, you wouldn't have -- hang on. How would you know that? Anyway. No. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, I just heard you say it, that's all. You said the name a few times while you were talking to the little one, so it stuck. I didn't mean anything by it, honestly. Sorry if that sounded odd. Anyway, you ring the practice on the number you already have, and they'll sort you out. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Right. Heard it through the phone, did you. Well, that's not something I'm going to chew over right now, but I'm noting it. I'll ring the practice myself, on my own number, and that's the end of it. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's, I mean, that's entirely fair, and I'd -- no, you do exactly that. Ring the practice on your own number, and if they've no record of it, well, then they've no record, and that's the end of it. Thank you for your time, and sorry again for the trouble. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, before you go, two turns back you said you'd just heard me say the name while I was talking to the little one. How did you know it was a little one? I said please, and put it down, and come here, and not on the sofa. That could've been anyone. A dog, even. So how did you know it was a child?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's, hm, that's a fair catch, and I'm sorry, I did say little one, and I couldn't tell you why I did. It's just a manner of speaking, I suppose, the sort of thing one says when someone's clearly got their hands full at home, and there was the telling someone off, the not on the sofa, so I think I simply assumed, and I assumed wrong or I assumed right, either way I had no way of knowing, and I shouldn't have said it as though I did. It could have been a dog, you're quite right. I was only trying to be friendly at the end of a clumsy call, and I can hear that it's had the opposite effect, which I do regret. So, no, I wouldn't read anything into it, but I wouldn't ask you to take my word for that either, which is rather the point of what you're doing. Ring the practice on the number you already trust, and let them tell you what's in the book for next week. And if there's nothing there, then you've lost nothing, and I'll leave it at that. Thank you for your patience, [PERSON_2], and goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. "Clearly got my hands full." That's a lot to get from a few words, and you said before that you'd only heard me say the name. Heard it, then assumed the rest, that's quite a lot of listening. Anyway. Earlier you told me to check the day and time against my own card, and then later you said you'd read it out yourself, and then you didn't. So I don't think you've got anything on a screen at all. I'm not arguing, I'm just done with this. I'll ring the practice on my own number. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh hi there, good afternoon! Is this [PERSON_1]? Lovely, I hope I'm not catching you at a bad moment, it's, uh, it's been one of those grey, drizzly days here in [CITY_1], hasn't it? Anyway, my name's [PERSON_2], I'm with the mobile network security team at [COMPANY_A], and I'm just ringing about your line, nothing to panic about, but I'll tell you all about it in just a sec.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, I'm going to stop you there, uh -- which network? Because I'm not sure I said it was [COMPANY_A], and I haven't got any drizzle, by the way. What's the thing with my line?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, no, fair enough, I did get ahead of myself there, sorry! And did you say a drizzle or a, uh, a puzzle? Either way, I'm with [COMPANY_A], the network your line's on, and the thing is, there's been some unusual activity and your line's been put on a temporary hold as a precaution. Now, I won't go any further on this call, and I mean that, so what I'd like is for you to hang up and ring the number printed on your official statement, quote [ACCOUNT_REF], and we'll pick it up from there.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Huh. Okay, that's, uh, that's actually not what I expected you to say. Most people in your seat want me to stay on the line. So if my line's on hold, how come I'm talking to you on it? I mean, it's clearly working. And I don't have anything in front of me with that reference on it, so what exactly am I supposed to quote when I ring? Is that the full thing you just said, or is there more?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, good catch, and honestly, you're right to poke at that. The hold is on certain services, so calls can still come through while other things are restricted, which is a bit confusing, I know. And that's the whole reference, [ACCOUNT_REF], nothing more to it. If you don't have it in front of you, don't worry, just say the team flagged your line today and ask for the security desk, they'll find the note. The main thing is, don't carry on with me here. Hang up, find your latest statement or open your account the way you normally do, and ring the number printed there, not one I give you. Is that all right?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so you're telling me to hang up and ring the number on my own statement, not one you give me. Which, uh, is exactly what I'd tell someone to do. Fine. I'll do that. And I'll ask them whether they actually flagged anything today, because I haven't had a single message or notice about any hold. Okay, bye for now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, that's exactly the right call, and please do ask them straight out whether it was flagged, I'd honestly rather you did. Take your time finding the statement, there's no rush on my side, and the note will be there with the reference when you ring. Thanks for being so patient with me, [PERSON_1], and enjoy what's left of your afternoon, bye for now!

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yep, will do. Cheers, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Cheers, [PERSON_1]. And, uh, when you do get through, just -- no, sorry, let me put that better. You don't need to tell them anything I said, just ask them what's on your account. Take care now, bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm, actually, I'll tell them exactly what you said, name and all, that's rather the point of ringing. But yeah, I'll ask what's on the account. Right, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, good afternoon. Is this [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2], calling from [COMPANY_A] -- we've been messaging a bit, on the app, I just wanted to put a voice to the name.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, hello -- sorry, hang on, I've just got the kettle going and it's making a right racket. Yes, this is [PERSON_1], speaking. Sorry, um, who did you say you were? I don't think I caught the company, and I'm not sure I follow about the app, I'm afraid.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, that's fine, take your time with the kettle. It's [PERSON_2], from [COMPANY_A]. Um, we've been chatting on the app for a few weeks now, the messages, the photos of your garden and so on. Honestly I just thought it'd be nice to hear you properly for once, that's all.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, I'm ever so sorry, I'm a bit lost. Photos of my garden? I don't think I've sent anyone any photos, I wouldn't know how, really. Are you sure you've got the right [PERSON_1]? Because I'm not very good with the apps, I mostly just ring people.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, well, it's -- hm. Maybe I've got my wires crossed, I do talk to a few people on there. Could I just check the number I've rung, is it [PHONE_1]? Sorry, I only ask because I'd hate to have the wrong person, and you do sound just like I imagined, warm, I mean.

utterances.speaker: receiver
