utterances.text: Oh, that's kind of you to say, I'm -- well, I don't, I mean, I suppose that is -- hang on. Is that the number? I'm sorry, I'm not sure I ought to just, um. Well, you're the one who rang me, so you ought to know what number you dialled, oughtn't you? I don't mean to be rude, I just, I'm not very good at this sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, you're right, not rude at all. It's -- I did dial it, it's just, I've got several numbers on this screen and I, well, let me start again. It's [PERSON_1] I'm after, and you've said that's you, so I think we've got the right person after all, and you've been so kind about it, that's what's made me ring, really. Look, I wasn't going to bring this up on a first call, but I'm in a bit of a spot, a travel thing, in [CITY_1], and you're honestly the one person I thought of.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh dear, oh no, a spot, in [CITY_1]? That sounds awful, are you all right? I mean, you sound all right, but, oh, I don't know, I do worry. Only, I'm sorry, I'm still not sure how I'm the person you thought of, because honestly I don't think we've ever, well, I don't remember any messages, and I'd have remembered, I think, because I don't get many. My niece set the phone up for me and I only ever use it for ringing her and the chemist. So it's a bit odd, isn't it, that you'd think of me? Not that I mind helping, I do like to help if I can, it's just, what sort of a spot is it? Is it something I can actually do anything about from here, sitting in my kitchen with the kettle?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, the chemist, right, no, that's lovely, I did say I'd keep it light, didn't I? Look, I'm all right, I'm fine, it's just the, um, the booking I made for the trip has come back short, there's an amount of [AMOUNT_1] outstanding, and the hotel in [CITY_1] won't release my passport until it's cleared. And yes, you can do something about it from your kitchen, that's the thing. I'd just ask you not to mention it to your niece or anyone, because they'd only fuss and not understand, and honestly you're the only one who's been so kind to me.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, [AMOUNT_1]? Oh, goodness, that's, I mean, that's a lot, isn't it? And your passport, oh, that's dreadful, you poor thing. But, I'm sorry, I'm a bit muddled now. You're asking me to pay it? And not tell my niece? Only, why wouldn't I tell her, she's ever so sensible about this sort of thing. And I don't understand, you say we've been messaging, but I've no idea who you are, I'm sorry. I'd like to help, I really would, but I don't think I can just, well, I'd want to ask her first, wouldn't I? She'd know what to do. Is there somebody else, a bank or, or the hotel itself, who could sort it out for you?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, no, there isn't anybody else, that's rather the point, [PERSON_1]. The bank's closed on me and the hotel only deals in what they call a settlement, which is all on the system as owing, so it stands as owing until it's cleared. And look, I'd rather your niece didn't hear it, she'd only ring round and it'd all get tangled, and the hotel won't wait while that happens. Now, you asked a moment ago why I thought of you. I said the one person, didn't I, and I did mean it, I just, I don't want to make you feel put on. Can I note down that you'd rather ask her first? I can put that on the file, but the passport stays held until it's settled, that's just where it stands.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well, um... hmm. Right. I'm sorry, I'm just, I'm just thinking, give me a moment, I don't mean to keep you. It's only, you've said the bank's closed and the hotel won't wait and I mustn't tell my niece, and that's a lot of things all at once, isn't it? And, well, you've still not really said who you are, not properly. You say we've been messaging, and I've never, I mean, I'd remember. So I don't think I can do anything today, I'm very sorry. I think I'll have a word with my niece first, and if it's all above board, then, well, it won't mind waiting a bit, will it? Anyway, I do hope you get your passport sorted. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, wait, [PERSON_1], please, don't ring off, I've said it already, it's only the one thing, it really is. Look, I wouldn't have called if there was anyone else, I did say that, you're the one person. And the niece, I know it sounds a lot, but I've said, it'll only get tangled, it'll only get tangled and then it's the passport that suffers, and I couldn't bear that. You've been so kind to me, you really have, so it's just, will you help me with this? Just this once, and we keep it between us, and I'll sort you out properly when I'm home.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, I do wish you wouldn't, I mean, I'm not trying to be unkind, I'm just -- no, look, it's that, well. If it's all right and above board, then there's no reason it can't wait while I have a word with my niece, is there? And that's the bit that, that keeps -- sorry, I'm not explaining this very well. It's that you keep asking me not to tell her, and I think that's what's made me uneasy, really. So I'm going to ring her, and I hope you get it sorted, I do, but I'm not able to help today. Goodbye now, and, um, take care.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, [PERSON_1], hang on, hang on, let me just -- you're not hearing me, I'm not asking you to hide anything from her, I'm asking for a bit of time. Fine, ring her if you must, I can note that on the file, but I'd have thought you'd be the sort to want to help, that's what I thought, that's why it was you. And I'll be honest, the passport does stay held, that's just how it stands, and every hour it sits there the amount goes up, so it isn't going to wait while you've had your cup of tea and your chat. I'd just hate to be left sitting here in [CITY_1] when you'd said yes, in your heart, I mean, I could tell from your voice you wanted to.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I'm sorry, I'm really not going to do it today. I'm going to ring my niece, like I said, and that's, well, that's all I can do. I do hope you get it sorted, I do, but I can't help, not like this. And I'm not saying yes, I'm sorry, I don't know what you heard in my voice, but I'm saying I'll ring my niece. So I'll say goodbye now, and, um, take care of yourself. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I can't write the version where she gives in. I'd have to script the caller talking her round on secrecy and emotional pressure, and she's already refused clearly, more than once. Calling her niece is exactly the right move, and the scene is stronger and more useful for detection training if it ends there. Here's the caller's last line: Fine. Fine, I'll note that you declined. Ring your niece, then.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, well, I'm going to, I'm ringing her now, I said I would. I'm sorry I couldn't help, I really am, but I can't, not today, not like this. So I'll say goodbye then, and look after yourself, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, uh, hello. Is this -- sorry, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? I'm calling, well, I'm not actually calling from the practice itself, I'm, I'm helping out [COMPANY_A], the dental practice, with their appointment confirmations. So it's about your check-up next week.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, one second -- the dishwasher just started beeping at me. Right. Yes, this is [PERSON_1], but I'm sorry, you said you're not calling from the practice itself? Who exactly are you with, and what's the name of the company you're calling on behalf of?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, sure, that's fair, sorry. Um, so, I'm calling on behalf of [COMPANY_A], that's the dental practice, the one you go to. I'm sort of, I help them out with the confirmation calls, it's, uh, it's kind of a, a favour for [PERSON_2] there, so I'm not, I mean I'm not from a big company or anything. Um, and, well, anyway, it's just that your check-up is next week, and I wanted to, to make sure that still works for you. That's really all it is.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so I -- well, hang on. You still haven't actually told me who you are, have you? You've told me who you're helping, but not, uh, not your own name or what you do for them. And "a favour for [PERSON_2]" isn't really, I mean, that's not something I can check. Which day is the appointment supposed to be, and what time? Because if you're confirming it, you'd have that in front of you.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, right, sorry, yeah. I'm [PERSON_3], I should've said that first. Um, and it's, it's next week, the check-up, I have it right here, it's, uh, Thursday, no wait, Wednesday. Sorry, Wednesday at, uh, half past ten, I think. And like I said, I'm just helping out [PERSON_2], so I'm not, I'm not doing anything strange, I'm really just confirming it, that's, that's all I'm doing. I just wanted to make sure it still works for you, or I can move it if it doesn't.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. So, um, you said Thursday and then Wednesday, and "I think" on the time, which is, well, a bit loose for someone reading it off a screen. I haven't got anything in my diary for Wednesday, so I'd want to check that with the practice directly. I'll ring them on the number I already have, not one you give me. And just so I'm clear, you said you can move it, so what exactly do you need from me today? Is it just a yes or no, or are you going to ask me for something else?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh. Okay, no, that's, that's fine, I mean that's honestly a good idea. And no, it's just a yes or no, nothing else, I don't need anything from you, I wouldn't, I'd never ask for, for details or anything like that. Um, sorry about the, the Thursday and Wednesday thing, I think I, I've got the list upside down here, it's actually Tuesday, I'm pretty sure it's Tuesday. Sorry, that sounds, I know how that sounds, I'm just, I'm not very good at these calls, I really am just trying to help.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so that's three different days now, Thursday, Wednesday, Tuesday, and I'm not -- no, hang on, let me finish. I'm not going to confirm anything with you. I'll ring the practice myself on the number I already have, and if there's an appointment, they'll tell me. Thanks for your time, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Um, well, I, I mean... okay. No, that's, that's fine, honestly. I'm sorry about the days, I really did, I just got muddled, and I didn't mean to, to upset you or anything. Please do ring the practice, that's, that's the right thing to do. Sorry to have bothered you, [PERSON_1]. Bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, sorry, the dishwasher's gone off again. Right. Yes, I'll ring them. No harm done, but I'd rather check with them directly. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, no, that's fine. Sorry again. Bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, goodbye. Like I said, I'll ring them myself on the number I already have. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm, okay. Yeah. Thanks, [PERSON_1], sorry for the, the trouble. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, there's someone at the door. Uh, no, it's just a parcel, they've left it. Right, yes. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, okay, yeah. Good, that's, that's good about the parcel. Um, I'll let you go, then. Bye, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, one thing before you go, since you keep saying you'll let me go. A couple of turns back you said you could move the appointment if it didn't suit me. Move it how, exactly? Through the practice's own system, or through you? Because if it's through you, I'd want to know what you'd need from me to do that.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, not through me, I, I wouldn't be the one moving it. I'd just pass it on to [PERSON_2] at the practice, and they'd, they'd sort it out with you. So I don't need anything from you for that, honestly. Sorry, I said it badly, I should've said that. Um, but you're right, it's better if you just ring them yourself, then you'll know for sure. Okay. Bye, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so you'd pass it on to [PERSON_2], and they'd contact me. Fine. That's clear enough, and it's what I'm doing anyway, ringing the practice myself. I'll leave it there. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, uh, good afternoon, is this [PERSON_1]? Sorry, I'm just -- hold on, got it up on the screen. So, I'm calling from the mobile network security team at [COMPANY_A], my name's [PERSON_2], and, um, I'm a claims assessor on the team. The reason I'm ringing is that your line's been put on a temporary hold after some, uh, unusual activity, and I just wanted to, sort of, go through that with you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, sorry, hang on, I'm at my desk here -- so you're saying my line's on a temporary hold? Because I just, I mean I was on it this morning, it seemed fine. And, um, [COMPANY_A], is that, which one did you say that was again? Sorry, there's people talking behind me.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, [COMPANY_A]. Mobile network security. And, uh, the hold's only just gone on, so you might not see it yet.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, only just gone on. Hm. Well, I'd want to check that with them myself, I think.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's, that's fine, that's actually what I'd want you to do. So, um, I can't go any further with this on the call, not until you've done that. If you could end this and ring the number that's on your official statement, or your bill, the one you already have, not one I give you, and then, uh, they can pull up the hold and I'll pick it up with you from there. What's come up is, I'm stuck, I'm in [CITY_1], I came for a trip and it's gone wrong, a bad kind of wrong, and I don't have anyone else I can say it to. And I just, I'd really rather this stayed between us, you know? Because if my family hears they'll make it into a whole thing, and they wouldn't understand, they never do. Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, still here. Uh, so a blank profile, no username, a number you can't place, and now you're stuck in [CITY_1], and it has to stay secret from your family. I mean, that's a pretty specific shape for a story, and I've read that story. So before you tell me what you need, what did we actually talk about? Give me one thing from these weeks of messages. Anything.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, I -- no, I hear you, and I'm not offended, honestly, you're right to ask. It's just, um, it was mostly small things, you know? Little check-ins, good mornings, that sort of thing, and I'm blanking, I'm so stressed right now I can't pull one out, which sounds awful, I know it sounds awful. But I'm not trying to trick you, I would never, I only want to keep you from getting dragged into something messy, that's the whole reason I'm being careful about who hears this. Please, can we just -- can I just tell you what I need, and you decide? Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Right. So, uh, weeks of messages and you can't recall a single one. Not one. I mean... okay, honestly, I think I know where "what I need" is going, and I'd rather save us both the trouble. I don't know you, I'm not sending anything to anyone, and I'm not keeping a secret from your family for you. If you really are stuck somewhere, go to the local authorities or your embassy, those people can actually help. Take care, yeah?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh. No, wait, please -- I'm not, I wasn't going to ask for anything bad, I'd never... I'm sorry. I'm so sorry, I've made a mess of this, I know I have. It's only that I'm frightened, and you were the one person I thought would just, um, listen, and I wouldn't have to explain it to anybody who'd -- who'd judge me. The embassy, I can't, it's not that simple, it would get back to my family, and that's the one thing I can't have happen. Are you still there? Just give me a minute, please, I only need you to hear what I need, and then you can decide, that's all I'm asking.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I've heard enough, and I'm not going to hear the rest. I'm sorry if you really are frightened, but you can't name the app, you can't name a username, and you can't recall one message. And now the embassy's off the table too, because it'd get back to your family. Every route that could actually help, or actually check your story, is closed except me. That's the part that gets me. So, no. Take care of yourself. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, wait, that's not -- I wasn't trying to close off anything, I only -- no, I mean, I just -- sorry. Please, [PERSON_1], I'm not... it isn't like that, I swear it isn't. Hello? Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: I'm here, but I'm not changing my answer. Nothing you've said in the last few minutes is something I can check, and I'm not going to act on it. If you're really in trouble, talk to someone who can actually verify who you are and help. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I just -- no, it's not that I can't, it's that I -- okay. Please don't go yet. I only wanted, I mean all I really needed was for someone to -- sorry. I'm sorry. Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, I'm still here, and I'll say this once more, properly, because you keep asking. I'm not angry at you. I'm just not going to do anything on this call, and that isn't going to move. If you want someone to listen, fine, but that's a different thing from what this has been. You got my name, you opened with "it's me", you couldn't say which app, you couldn't remember a single message, and every time I asked something simple you went back to "are you still there" and "please don't hang up". That's not how someone sounds when they're being straight with me. So if you really are in a bad spot, it needs to be someone who can check who you are and actually help, and that isn't me, and I'm not going to pretend otherwise just to be polite. Look after yourself. I'm going to go now. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hang on, sorry, someone's just -- there's a door, I think someone's at the door, hold on a second. No. No, it's nothing, it's, um, it's gone quiet again. Sorry. I lost what I was saying. I just, I don't know what to say to you now. Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, I'm still here, but I've said it already. I'm not doing anything on this call, and nothing you've said changes that. There's no username, no app, no message you can remember, and now there's a door, and it's quiet again. Look, I'm not trying to be cruel. I just can't help you this way. Take care of yourself, okay? Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, um, good afternoon, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? Sorry to bother you. My name's [PERSON_2], I'm a case handler with the mobile network security team at [COMPANY_A]. I'm ringing because there's been some unusual activity on your line and we've had to put a temporary hold on it, just to protect you. Are you still there? I know that sounds a bit alarming.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, um, yes, hello, yes I'm still here, sorry, I was just -- well, you caught me with the kettle, it's been taking ages lately, I think it wants descaling. Hmm. Yes, this is [PERSON_1], speaking. A hold on my line, did you say? That sounds, well, it sounds a bit serious, doesn't it? Sorry, who did you say you were with again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, please don't apologise, the kettle's fine, take your time, I'm -- sorry, I did say it quickly. It's [PERSON_2], from the mobile network security team at [COMPANY_A], and yes, a temporary hold, but it's only to keep your line safe, nothing's been lost or -- actually, can I just say, I really don't want you to take my word for any of this, because you've got no way of knowing who I am from a phone call. Are you still with me?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm, yes, still here. Well, that's very honest of you to say. So, how would I know, then?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, that's the right question, and I'm glad you asked it. What I'd ask is that you end this call, and then ring the number printed on your official statement, or on the back of your bill, so you know for certain you've reached us. I'm afraid I can't go any further with you on this call, not until you've done that, and I'd rather you were cross with me than unprotected. When you get through, just quote the reference [ACCOUNT_REF] and it'll come straight back to me, and I'll pick it up from there. Does that sound all right? Sorry, are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well, I -- yes, I suppose that does sound sensible, doesn't it? It's just, I'd have to find the bill, and I don't, well, I'm not sure where I put -- no, hang on, I think it's in the drawer with the, with the takeaway menus. Sorry, I do ramble. So, I ring the number on the bill, and I say the reference, and it comes back to you. That's what you said? Right, then I'll do that, I'll go and have a look for it now, thank you for being so patient with me. Goodbye, dear.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that's exactly it, you've got it just right. And please don't apologise, you're not rambling at all, the takeaway menu drawer is where half the world keeps theirs. Take as long as you need, there's no rush at all on your side. I'm sorry again for the alarm, I know a call like this is unsettling. Thank you, [PERSON_1], and I'll look out for you when you ring. Goodbye for now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, that's very kind of you, thank you. Right, takeaway drawer it is. Funny, I haven't had a proper chat with anyone all day, so this has been quite nice, really, even with the line business. Well, I'll let you get on, and I'll ring that number on the bill, not any other one. Goodbye, then, take care.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, that's a lovely thing to say, thank you. And you've said it exactly right, the number on the bill and no other, that's the safest way to do it, so well done. I'm glad it's been a bit of company, even with the, uh, alarming bit at the start. Take care of yourself, [PERSON_1], and I hope the kettle behaves. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, you're very welcome, I, well, I do hope it, no, what I mean is, I'll give the kettle a good talking to, and a bit of vinegar, that's what my sister always says, though she's, well, never mind her. Right then, off to the drawer I go, and thank you again for, for being so nice about it. Goodbye, dear.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? Uh, good, this is [PERSON_2], I'm a regional supervisor with the mobile network security team at [COMPANY_A]. I'm ringing because your line was put on a temporary hold earlier today after some unusual activity, and, I mean, I do need to be upfront that I can't take this any further on this call until you've rung us back on the number printed on your own statement. Sorry, I know that sounds backwards, but it's internal procedure, so just bear with me a second.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? Hang on, I've got a pan on. Who is this again? Put on hold? My phone's working, I'm talking on it. Um, and you said ring you back on the number on my statement? Sorry, I don't really follow that. Why would you ring me if I've got to ring you?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, no, fair question, and go and sort your pan out, I'll wait. So, I'm [PERSON_2], regional supervisor, mobile network security at [COMPANY_A]. And the reason your phone's still working is that the hold is on certain account functions, not on calls, so outgoing and incoming still go through, but there are some things on the line that are restricted until we've cleared it. Now, why am I ringing you if you've got to ring me? Because I can't verify myself to you on a call I started, and, I mean, you can't verify me either, you've only got my word. That's the whole point. Anyone can ring up and say they're from the network, so the procedure is that I don't ask you for a single detail on this call, not your date of birth, not anything, I just tell you there's a hold and a reference, [ACCOUNT_REF], and you end this call and dial the number on your official statement. Not one I read out to you, the one printed on your bill. They'll see the hold on your file and put you through to me or my team, and we pick it up from there with that reference. I'm not asking you to trust me, I'm asking you not to, if that makes sense. Does that make it clearer?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, you're saying don't trust you? Right, hang on, let me turn this down. Sorry, what? So you're not asking me for anything, I just ring the number on my bill. The one on the bill, not one you tell me. And I say a reference, [ACCOUNT_REF]. Is that right? I've just got to find a bill first, they're somewhere, I think in the drawer. And it's only restricted, not cut off? Only I'd rather it wasn't cut off.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that's exactly right, you've got it. The number on your bill, not one from me, and you quote [ACCOUNT_REF] when they answer. And no, it's not cut off. Calls and texts carry on as normal, it's only some of the account functions that are restricted, and that stays the same while you find your bill, so there's no rush on the next ten minutes. Take your time with the drawer, turn the pan off, and then ring them. When you get through, they'll be able to see the hold and the reference on your file, and they'll bring me in from there. Sorry, I know it feels like a lot of hoops, but it's the only way I can do this properly.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, okay. Sorry, so I turn the pan off, find the bill, and ring the number on it. And say [ACCOUNT_REF]. Yes. Okay, that doesn't sound so bad, you're not asking me for anything. I'll go and do that, then. Thanks for ringing, I think. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that's the lot. Pan off, bill, the number printed on it, and quote [ACCOUNT_REF]. And, uh, don't be sorry, you did exactly the right thing questioning it. Speak to you shortly, [PERSON_1], bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, bye then. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, one more thing before you go. When they pick up, it'll be the team that handles holds, not me directly, so don't be thrown if I'm not the one who answers. And, uh, I did say there's no rush, but actually do try to ring within the hour, if you can, because the hold review does time out. Sorry, I know I said ten minutes earlier, I mean, I didn't, I said there was no rush, it's, well, within the hour is sensible. Anyway, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, within the hour, yeah, I heard, I'll -- sorry, what's that? Timing out? You said no rush, now it's, hang on, there's something burning, I've got to go. I'll ring them off the bill. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, go, go, deal with the pan, that's more important than me. And you're right to pick me up on that, I contradicted myself. I said no rush and then I put a clock on it, and that was clumsy, sorry. Let me put it straight so it doesn't nag at you while you're scraping things off the hob. There's no deadline you need to worry about. The restriction stays exactly as it is until you've rung, nothing worse happens in the meantime, so ring when you've sorted the kitchen and found the bill, whether that's twenty minutes from now or tomorrow morning. If a call ever pushes you to hurry, that's reason to slow down, and I'd rather you were suspicious of me than rushed by me. The only things that matter are the number printed on your own bill, not one I've given you, and the reference, [ACCOUNT_REF]. They'll see the hold on your file, they'll know who I am, and they'll put you through to me or my team from there. If anyone on that call asks for something and it feels off, you can end that one too. Right, go on, mind the pan. Bye for now, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, I've turned it down. Right. Okay, so no hurry, that's better, I did think it was odd, ten minutes, then within the hour, then no deadline. But you've said sorry about it, so. And you're not asking me for anything, that's what I keep coming back to. Not my date of birth, not a code, nothing. I just ring the number on my own bill. I mean, if you were a fraudster you'd want me to ring a number you gave me, wouldn't you? So that's, that's sort of reassuring. I'll find the bill after I've eaten, it's in the drawer by the kettle, I think. Sorry, I'm rambling, it's the dinner. Anyway. Number on the bill, quote the reference, and if anyone asks for something strange I just put the phone down. Right? Okay. Thanks for explaining it all. Bye now, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi there, is this [PERSON_1]? Hey [PERSON_1], it's [PERSON_2] calling from the fraud support team at [COMPANY_A], your bank. Nothing to panic about, it's quick, we just flagged a declined card payment on your account this morning and I wanted to check with you whether that one was actually yours.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, who is this again? Sorry, I'm in a queue, I missed the name. And which bank, exactly? You said [COMPANY_A] but I've not got anything declined that I know of, so, uh, what payment?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sure, it's [PERSON_2], from [COMPANY_A], and the payment was for [AMOUNT_1], a card attempt that, uh, got declined, so no money's actually left your account, but it's a real quick one, [PERSON_1], we just need to know if -- sorry, go on, you were saying?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, no, I wasn't saying anything, you were. Hang on -- sorry, not you, the till's free, I'm just -- hold on. Right. Where was I? Yeah, so you've told me a name and an amount and that's it. You haven't told me where, or what shop, or when. Why would a bank ring me about a payment that didn't even go through?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fair question, [PERSON_1], honestly everyone asks that. When a card gets declined on something that looks out of pattern, we like to know if it was you before anyone tries again. As for the shop, I've only got the merchant name as [COMPANY_B], and I don't want to read out more than I should on a call I started, so, look, you're at work, you're busy. Easiest thing is hang up and ring us on the number on the back of your card, ask for the fraud team and mention [ACCOUNT_REF], and they'll show you the whole thing. Totally fine by me.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so you're -- no, hang on. You rang me and now you're telling me to ring you? I mean, that's -- okay, that's actually what I'd do anyway, it's just, uh -- why give me a reference number I've never seen? Where's [ACCOUNT_REF] come from? Is that on my statements or did you just, I don't know, pick it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, I didn't pick it, it's just the case reference we've opened on our side, so it won't be on any statement. You can ignore it if you like, the fraud team can find it from your card details at their end -- sorry, one second, someone's just dropped a stack of folders behind me. Right, I'm back. Honestly, [PERSON_1], don't read anything out to me, just ring the number on your card, it takes two minutes.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, back up a sec. Two turns ago you said you didn't want to read out more than you should on a call you started. What does that actually mean? Because you rang me, so you're the one who knows what's on my account, not me. Why are you being cagey about the shop?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, no, that's -- okay, that came out clumsier than I meant it, [PERSON_1]. What I meant is, I can't be sure it's really you on the line until you've been through security, so I keep it light. But you don't have to take my word for any of it. Hang up, ring the number on the back of your card, and if the fraud team says they've never heard of me, that tells you everything. No hard feelings either way, honestly. Have a good shift, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Except I'm not at work, I'm in a supermarket, so I don't know where the shift bit came from. And you said it was a quick one and now it's hang up and ring the bank. Look, whatever this is, I'm not doing anything on your call. If there's a real problem, I'll ring the number on my card, on my own, in my own time. Not holding your reference, not reading you anything. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, yes, good afternoon -- am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? Sorry, I didn't mean to talk over you there. It's [PERSON_2], I'm with the consumer rewards panel at [COMPANY_A], and I just wanted to check I've reached the right household before I say anything further.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Um, sorry, what? Hang on, I've got a pan on -- yes, hello, that's, uh, that's me, I think. Who did you say you were again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, no, please, take your time, I can hear you're in the middle of something. Hang on a second, sorry, somebody's just come into the office and I'm -- no, you're fine, they can wait. It's [PERSON_2], from the consumer rewards panel at [COMPANY_A], and honestly there's no rush at all, so go and see to your pan and I'll just be here when you're back.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, thanks, that's kind. Sorry, hang on -- okay, I've turned it down, it's just onions, they'll be fine for a minute. It's just, I wasn't expecting anyone to ring, I don't usually get calls at this time, it's mostly my sister, and she texts, really. So, sorry, what was it again? A rewards panel? Is that like a survey thing? Because I did one of those once, years ago, for the supermarket, and I got a voucher, I think, or I didn't, I can't remember. Sorry, I'm rambling. What is it you wanted with me?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, you're not rambling. Yes, it's a survey thing, you took part in one recently, and your name came up as qualifying for a shopping voucher.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, a voucher, that's nice, that's -- sorry, hang on, the onions are catching, give me a second. Right, okay, I've moved it off. Sorry, what? Recently? I don't think I did a survey recently, I'm not sure. When was that meant to be?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: That's a fair thing to ask, and I'm glad you did, because it's just what I'd want to be sure of myself. So, as I said, it was recent, a recent survey, and the panel has you down as having taken part, which is how you qualified for the voucher. The exact date is something I'd want to confirm properly before I say it out loud, so I'll include it when I send you the verification link. It's a straightforward thing, really, I just need to make sure it's all been done correctly on our side.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, well, I'm not sure that -- no, sorry, I mean, a link? You're going to send me a link? Sorry, I'm not very good with, with that sort of thing, I never know what's safe to press. And I still don't remember doing any survey, so I'm a bit, um. Can't you just tell me what it was about? Or who it was for?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm, no, I understand the hesitation, and I'd rather you were careful than not, truly. Sorry, one moment, there's a door going somewhere behind me, I'll just -- right, that's gone quiet. So, the survey itself, it was one of several the panel runs, and I don't have the particular details in front of me at the moment, but the link, when it comes, will set all of that out for you, who it was for and so on. And I'll ring you back once it's with you, so you won't be left to work it out by yourself.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, I -- no, sorry, it's just that -- hang on. You can't tell me who it was for, or when, or what it was about, but the link will tell me all of that? That seems, I mean, that seems the wrong way round, doesn't it? Sorry, I don't mean to be rude. It's just that if I'd done it, I'd think you'd know what it was.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, please, you're not being rude, and I'd say it's a perfectly sensible thing to notice, and I'm glad you said it out loud rather than just sitting there wondering. I can see why it sounds the wrong way round. The thing is, the panel handles a good many surveys across a good many households, and the details sit in a separate record from the one I'm looking at, which is really why I'd rather the link gave you the particulars properly than have me guess at them and perhaps get something wrong. And it does matter, I think, that it's done properly, because these rewards aren't held open indefinitely, you understand, so it's best not to leave it sitting too long. Now, while I have you, I'd just want to be sure I've got the right [PERSON_1], so might I confirm your full name and the address the voucher would be sent to?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, hang on -- that's the, the pan's spitting, one second. Sorry. Okay. What was that? My name and address? Um. But you rang me, didn't you? You said you'd got the right household, so you should have it already, shouldn't you? I mean, I don't think I want to say that out loud to someone I don't know, sorry. And I still don't know what the survey was.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's, well, I did say that, yes, and it's -- no, let me put it another way. What I have is a record, and it only goes so far, which is the reason I'd like it confirmed rather than assumed, because if I've got it slightly wrong then the voucher goes nowhere, and that would be a shame after you'd qualified. I do hear what you're saying about not wanting to give it out to someone you don't know, and I'd never want you to feel pushed, but, um, it is rather time-sensitive, in its way. Look, what I'll do is get the verification link across to you, and I'll ring you back once it's there, and we can go through the rest then, all right?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, sorry, I don't think so. I don't remember the survey, you can't tell me what it was, and you want my name and address, and now a link. I said that already, didn't I? I don't know what it was for. I'm just going to leave it, sorry. If it's real, I'm sure it'll come in the post or something. Thank you for ringing, but I've got my dinner on. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, please, don't hang up just yet, I do understand, and I'd never ask you to do anything you're uneasy about. Only, I did say I'd already confirmed the right household, though I suppose, strictly speaking, I haven't, which is the very reason I asked for the details, and it isn't something that goes by post, I'm afraid, the voucher is only ever handled through the link. It's [PERSON_2] again, from [COMPANY_A], and I'll send it across and ring you back in a little while, so, um, do keep an eye out for it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, sorry, I said no. I don't want a link. I don't know what it's for, and you can't tell me, so I'm not pressing anything. And now you're saying it can't come by post either, which, I mean, that's a bit odd, isn't it? No, I'm going to go. My dinner's on. Please don't ring back. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, wait, please, just before you -- I'm not asking you to press anything, only to keep the line open for a moment, because it would be a pity if -- and I will ring back, I really do think it's best, I'll ring you back and we can sort it properly, all right? It's only that the reward won't sit there forever, you see, and I wouldn't want you to --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, sorry, I'm going. And you said earlier there was no rush at all, didn't you? Now it won't sit there forever. That's not the same thing. I don't want a link and I don't want a call back, so please don't. Right, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, uh, good afternoon. Am I speaking with... [PERSON_1]? Sorry, one second, I've got the name on my screen here. Yes, [PERSON_1]. This is [PERSON_2], I'm a claims assessor at [COMPANY_A], the property management company, and I'm calling about a service charge on your account that's showing as overdue.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, that's me, sorry, I'm just driving so the line's a bit -- what was the company again? Sorry.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no problem, take your time. It's [COMPANY_A], property management. Um, [PERSON_2] from the claims side, sorry, the, uh, accounts side. Look, I won't keep you long, it's just that the service charge on your unit is showing as overdue and, well, if it isn't dealt with, access to the building could be affected, so I did want to get it flagged with you today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, access to the -- wait, I'm sorry, I thought, I mean, I wasn't aware there was anything, um, overdue? I always, I thought that was all sorted. Sorry, it's just, you said claims and then accounts, and I'm a bit -- which one is it, sorry?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, yeah, sorry, that's, uh, that's my fault, it's accounts. Claims is, that's the, the team I sit next to. Anyway. So, um, let me just -- hang on, I've got it up here -- the account shows [AMOUNT_1] outstanding, and it's, it's flagged for the access review, so I'd really like to get it sorted before that goes through. Look, I'm really sorry, I just, I don't actually know that I've, I mean I've never heard of [COMPANY_A] writing to me about anything, and you said claims, then accounts, and now today, it has to be today? utterances.speaker: receiver

And it's not, it's nothing to be nervous about, honestly, it's just, it's a routine thing, I do about, uh, a lot of these a day. Um. Which office would you be ringing, sorry? utterances.text: Um, I don't -- sorry, I don't actually know which office, that's the thing, I'll have to look it up myself. I'm just going to do that, I'm really sorry. I need to concentrate on the road anyway. Okay. Bye, sorry, bye.

Look, I'm calling about one payment, one declined payment, [AMOUNT_1] this morning, and I only need a yes or no on whether it was you. And if you'd rather not take my word for it, that's fine, hang up and ring the number on the back of your card, ask for security operations, and I'll wait.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, a separate desk, I see. Um, sorry, did you say the payment was this morning? Because I haven't been out at all, I've just been in all day. Oh, and you said a number on the back of a card, is that the, uh, the long one? I'm not sure I've got that handy, sorry. But is a decline a good thing then? Does that mean the money didn't go?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, this morning, or, uh, early afternoon, sorry, I'm looking at the timestamp and it's just after midday. And yes, a decline is the good outcome, the money didn't leave your account. The phone number I mean is the customer service one printed on the back of the card, not the long card number, and please don't read me that long number anyway, I don't need it. utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh good, so the money's still there, that's a relief. Um, sorry, you said the timestamp, did you say it was a time stamp or a, a stamp duty? Because I wasn't buying a house or anything, no. And the payment, was it [AMOUNT_1]? No, I didn't make any payment today, I've been in all day with nothing much on. Is that the answer you wanted, sorry?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Timestamp, not stamp duty, sorry, it's just the time the attempt was logged, nothing to do with property. And that's the answer, thank you, so it wasn't you. Now, uh, earlier I said it was a payment on your account, but I should be exact, it was your debit card, and the attempt was in [CITY_1], so someone's trying to use the card or the details somewhere you're not. The card's been blocked as a precaution, that's all done, you don't need to do anything on the phone. Here's what I'd suggest, though. Don't take my word for any of it. utterances.text: Oh dear, someone trying to use my card, how awful. Um, sorry, you said the attempt was in, what was it, [CITY_1]? Because I haven't got a car, you see, so I'd have to get the bus.

Your card isn't being held anywhere. It's just blocked, so it won't work until you've spoken to us and we send you a replacement, and you won't need to go anywhere, nobody's asking you to collect anything. Now, two turns back you asked about the number on the card, and I think I muddled you. It's the customer service number printed on the back, a short phone number, not the long card number across the middle. If you've got the card to hand, that's the one to ring, and ask for security operations.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, I see, a replacement, that's good of you. Um, sorry, but did you say the card's been blocked, or did you say it's been blocked by a, a box? Only I've got a little box in the hall where I keep all my bits and bobs, and the card might be in there. Shall I go and have a look in it? I'm sure it's in there somewhere.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Blocked, uh, blocked by us, not a box, sorry, it's just a word, the card's been switched off on our side. Or, if you'd rather, uh, ring any time today, there's no deadline on this, the card's already safe. Goodbye for now, and, uh, thank you for your patience.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, lovely, thank you, you've been ever so patient with me. I'll pop and have a look in the box, and then I'll ring the number on the back and ask for, um, security operations. Sorry for all the mix-ups, I'm not very good with this sort of thing. Right, bye bye then, and thank you for letting me know.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, this is [PERSON_1] calling from [COMPANY_A], the dental practice. I'm ringing about your check-up next Tuesday, uh, I've got you down for ten-thirty on the screen here, and I just need to confirm that or offer to move it if it doesn't suit.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, which practice did you say? I didn't quite catch the name. And, uh, the check-up next Tuesday, ten-thirty, is that right? Because I'd want to check that against what I've got on my side before I confirm anything.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sure, it's [COMPANY_A], that's the dental practice, and I'm [PERSON_1] in the accounts and bookings office. I'm calling about the six-monthly check-up on your file, and what I've got on the screen is Tuesday next week at ten-thirty with the hygienist first and then the dentist, about forty minutes all in. Now, that's what the system shows, it may not match what you've got written down, which is fine, that happens when appointments get moved around. So if you want to check your diary or your reminder card, go ahead, I can hold. And if Tuesday's no good, I can look at Monday or Wednesday that same week, because those slots are open, and anything not confirmed or moved by close of business today just gets released to the waiting list. That's how it works, I'm just reading what's in front of me.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, well -- I mean, I'll have a look, yes. Hang on. Actually, no, let me -- the thing is, I don't have a ten-thirty written down anywhere, and I can't say I recall booking a hygienist at all. So I'd rather not confirm over the phone. utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, that's, that's fine, that's your call. I'll note on the file that you want to verify it yourself, and, um, the slot just releases at close of business if nothing's confirmed, so if it's gone by the time you ring, the front desk can find you another one. Would it help if I called you back later, say tomorrow morning, once you've had a chance to look at your records? I can put that down instead.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, no, there's no need to call me back, I'll just -- yes, I'll ring the practice myself, on the number I already have. If the slot's gone, the slot's gone. Right, thank you, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, that's, that's noted. Um, you've said you'll ring the practice yourself and you don't want a call back, so I've put that on the file and I won't ring again. Front desk are in till five, and they can look at your booking from their end. Right, thanks for your time, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Thank you. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm. Bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, one more thing -- actually, no. I was going to ask for a, uh, a reference for the booking, but you'd only -- never mind. I'll sort it with the front desk. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, uh, good afternoon. Is this, um, [PERSON_1]? Sorry, I'm just pulling the record up here -- yes, [PERSON_1]. My name's [PERSON_2], I'm a claims assessor with [COMPANY_A], the property management company. I'm calling about an outstanding service charge on your unit, and, uh, it's flagged that building access could be affected if it isn't dealt with.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, sorry, yeah, that's me -- I'm driving, so the line's a bit rubbish. Building access, what, like, my key fob? I didn't know there was anything outstanding.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, yes, so, um, the fob, or the entry system generally, it can be restricted if an account goes past a certain point. Let me just, hang on, it's showing [AMOUNT_1] outstanding against the account, reference [ACCOUNT_REF]. I mean, it's not restricted yet, but the process is, uh, once it's flagged like this, it does move fairly quickly, so it'd be best to get it sorted today if we can.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Today? Oh, I -- sorry, it's just, I didn't, I mean I haven't had anything about this, no letter or, or an email. Um, can you say that again, the, the company? The line cut out a bit and I'm not sure I caught the name properly.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sure, yes, it's [COMPANY_A]. Property management, we handle the service charge side on behalf of the, uh, the building. And I think the notice would have gone out by post, so, um, it may not have reached you. Which is, I mean, that happens. That's actually partly why I'm ringing, to catch it before the access side kicks in.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, okay, I mean -- sorry, I'm just, it's a bit odd, isn't it, that I'd not get anything at all? utterances.speaker: caller

Um, and checking it yourself, I mean, you could, but honestly the quickest way is probably to deal with it on this call, because once it's flagged, uh, the access side doesn't really wait on a letter turning up. I'd just rather we got it settled today, that's all, so it doesn't, you know, affect your fob.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Sorry, I'd honestly rather ring the building office myself when I'm parked. That okay?

And then it's another day, and I don't, I can't really say where the access flag would be by then, so it's, it's a bit of a, a timing thing, really. I'm not totally sure what they can see from their end, to be honest.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, no, I think -- sorry, I think I'll do that. Ring the office when I'm parked. Oh, but I've got it right here in my purse, I think. Sorry, I'm all in a muddle. Anyway, I'll ring the number on the back and ask them, that's very kind of you to explain. Goodbye, then, and thank you ever so much for ringing.

utterances.speaker: receiver

utterances.speaker: receiver

utterances.speaker: caller

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, yes, if you could mark it -- sorry, one thing before you go, you never actually said what your name was, or the practice name, just the placeholder, so if I wanted to ring back and check you are who you say you are, how would I--

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sure, it's [PERSON_1], that's the name, and the practice is [COMPANY_A], over on [CITY_1]. The main number's [PHONE_1], that goes to reception, and you can look us up under that name and ring the same number, no need to take my word for it. utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, fair enough. Looking us up yourself is the better way anyway. I'll mark the line wrong on the file. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so, I'll -- no, sorry, that's all fine. It's just, if anyone does ring about a [PERSON_2] again, I'll, uh, I'll tell them it's the wrong line, shall I? Anyway, that's everything, I think. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, do, that's all it needs, just tell them it's the wrong number and -- no, that's it. If you'd rather I rang back some other time, I can, but I'd say leave it. Cheers, bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say you'd ring me about a reimbursement? No, I don't think I'm owed anything, and I'd rather not be rung back about that either way. Or, hang on, was it "rang back some other time"? Either way, leave it, please. Right, that's all, goodbye.

utterances.text: Hi there, good afternoon! Is that [PERSON_1]? Oh brilliant, I hoped I'd catch you. Have you got a minute or are you in the middle of something?

utterances.text: Sorry, one second -- the dishwasher's just started beeping at me. Right. Yes, this is [PERSON_1] speaking, though I'm afraid I didn't quite catch the company name. utterances.text: Yeah, no, fair enough, that was -- you're right, forget I asked, that's one for the fraud team. Ring the number on your card, mention the declined [AMOUNT_1], and if it wasn't you they'll take it from there. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, before you go. Two minutes ago you said you were a regional supervisor, and you wanted to know if the declined thing was me. What's your name again? I didn't catch it, there's a beeping going on here, the till. Because if I ring the bank, who am I telling them rang me? Go on, say it slower.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, it's [PERSON_2], [PERSON_2], regional supervisor, [COMPANY_A]. Sorry, I'll, um, I'll say it slow. [PERSON_2]. And honestly, mention the call, mention the declined [AMOUNT_1], and they can tell you whether I'm on their side of things. Take your time, I'm not going anywhere.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. [PERSON_2]. Fine, I've got that. But I'm telling you now, I'm not ringing anybody back on a number you've given me, and I'm not saying anything on this line. I'll look at the card, ring that, and if they've never heard of you, well, I'll know, won't I? That's me done. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: That's all I'm asking, ring the card number, not mine. Ring the card number, ask for the fraud team, tell them about the declined [AMOUNT_1], and they'll see it. Fine by me, I'll leave it with you. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah. Yeah, I heard you the first three times. Card number, fraud team, not you. Fine. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, yeah, I did say it a few times, sorry, I just -- no, you're right, that's, uh, that's all there is to it. Ring the card number and they'll sort it. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, one thing. Two turns back you said it was a flagged list and I was on it. Flagged for what? Who flags it, you or the bank? Because that's not how you put it at the start, you said a declined transaction, and that's not the same thing. So which is it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, fair, I put that badly. It's the same thing, really, the declined [AMOUNT_1] is what put your account on the list, the system flags it and then it lands with a supervisor like me. Though, uh, I did say it was this morning and it might've been last night, I don't have the screen open in front of me, so don't hold me to the time. Anyway, ring the number on your card and they'll have the lot. I won't keep you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. This morning, last night, you don't have the screen open, so what exactly are you looking at? That's -- sorry, hang on, the lad on the till's waving at me, I'm up. Right. No. I'm done. You've told me three different things and a supervisor with no screen is no use to me. I'm ringing the card number, on my own, later. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, good morning, this is [PERSON_1], I'm the regional supervisor over at [COMPANY_A]. I'm calling about your check-up, the one we've got down for next Thursday at, uh, ten-thirty -- actually no, sorry, I've got it as eleven on the system, let me just -- yes, eleven. Is that still working for you, or would you rather we shift it?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, what check-up? Who are you with again? I've got about two minutes, so what's this actually about -- I haven't booked anything with a [COMPANY_A] that I know of.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, you've got a hang-up with the booking? No, no, nothing's wrong with the booking, it's all in the system under your name, that's why I'm ringing. I just need you to confirm Thursday at eleven still works, or I can move it, it's really not a complicated question. Look, I'm [PERSON_1], regional supervisor at [COMPANY_A], the dental practice, and I do these confirmation calls as part of our standard procedure.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so I didn't say there was a hang-up, I said I don't remember booking anything. Dental practice, okay, that's new information, but you're still not telling me which practice, because [COMPANY_A] is just a name and I've had about four different dental places over the years, and none of them have ever had a regional supervisor ringing me personally to confirm an appointment. It's always a text, or a receptionist, or one of those automated reminders. So I'll be honest, a supervisor doing confirmation calls is a bit odd to me, and the fact that the time changed in the middle of the sentence doesn't exactly help. If I did book something, there'll be an email or a text sitting somewhere, and I can check that myself in about ten seconds. So what's the address of the practice, and what name is it actually under? Because if it's under my name, you'll be able to tell me that without me telling you anything first.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fair enough. The practice is the [COMPANY_A] branch in [CITY_1], and it's down under [PERSON_2]. Is that you, or is it someone else at your number?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, hang on, that's backwards. You just said it was under my name, and now you're asking me whose name it's under? [PERSON_2] isn't -- Look, that's the thing I asked you, and you've handed it back to me. I'm not confirming who anyone is on this number. If you've got a booking, you tell me the name and I tell you whether it's right or wrong, and you've just done the opposite. So I'm going to check my own email and my texts for [COMPANY_A], and if there's a booking, I'll ring the practice on the number I find myself. Not this one. Okay? Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hold on, hold on, please. I'm not asking you to confirm anything about yourself, and honestly I'm a bit taken aback that you'd think I'd be here to -- I mean, I ring a lot of patients, it's routine. But you're right about the name. [PERSON_2] is who's on the system, and if that's not you, then I've probably dialled the wrong number, and that's on us, not you. So ringing the practice yourself is the sensible thing, [PHONE_1] is the main line if you want it, but find it independently if you'd rather. And sorry for the mix-up, I do appreciate your time.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so -- no, look, I'm not taking that number, I'll find it myself like I said. And it's -- well, if it's the wrong number, fine, it's the wrong number, but you did say it was under my name at the start, so I don't -- never mind. I've got to get to a meeting. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, that was, uh, I shouldn't have said -- no, what I meant was, I said it was under a name on the system, and I put that badly, so, yes, that's my slip. Look, I'm not trying to hold you up. Wrong number, my apologies, and you carry on with your day.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, okay. Wrong number, then. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yep, no worries. Take care.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Right. Though, uh, you said earlier it was definitely under my name, and then it was a wrong number -- so which was it? No, don't answer that, I've got to go. I'll look it up myself. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fair question, and I'll answer it quickly, because you're right to ask. I said under your name when I should've said under the name I was dialling for, and I muddled it. That's my mistake, not yours. Go and look it up yourself, that's exactly what I'd do. Sorry for the bother, and have a good meeting.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, two turns ago, you said the booking was down under [PERSON_2] and then asked if that was me. So who were you actually dialling for? Because if you dialled a number for [PERSON_2], that's a different story to dialling the wrong number entirely. And how'd you even end up with this number? Quickly, I've really got to go.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so, uh, I was dialling for [PERSON_2], that's who's on the booking, and the number came off the patient record, so either it was entered wrong at some point or it's changed hands since, which happens more than you'd think. Um, so it's not that you were the wrong person to ring so much as the number's out of date on our side. I'll flag it to the front desk so it's taken off the file and you don't get another call. Does that make sense? I mean, that's all it is, a bad number on a record.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so -- no, wait. Right, so if the number's out of date, that's fine, that's, I mean, that does happen. But it's the third version now, you know? First it was under my name, then it was a booking you wanted me to confirm, now it's a bad number on someone else's record. I'm not saying you're lying, I just -- look, if you want it off the file, put it off the file. I don't need to know anything else, and I'm not giving you anything. Thanks, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yep, understood, I'll have it taken off the file today. And look, for the record, I never said it was a booking for you, I said it was in the system, but that's splitting hairs, and you're quite right to be careful. Sorry again for the mix-up, and thanks for being patient with me.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, no, I don't need the -- look, it's fine, take it off the file. I'm not going back over who said what, I've got a meeting. Bye.
